name: Abdullah bin Masud
title: Master Reciter of the Kufan Codex
biography: One of the earliest converts to Islam and the foremost authority on Quranic recitation among the Companions. Prophet Muhammad explicitly instructed the Muslim community to learn the recitation of the Quran from four individuals, naming Abdullah bin Mas'ud first (Sahih al-Bukhari 4999). Appointed to Kufa by Caliph Umar bin Al-Khattab as teacher and treasurer, his personal Mushaf became the foundational text of the Kufan school. When Caliph Uthman ordered all regional codices burned to enforce a single standard text, Ibn Mas'ud famously refused to surrender his codex, reminding the community that he had learned over seventy Surahs directly from the lips of the Prophet while Zaid bin Thabit was still a youth. His codex omitted Surahs 1, 113, and 114 (treating them as protective prayers rather than Quranic chapters) and preserved dozens of distinct consonantal, lexical, and legal readings recorded across Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, Tafsir al-Tabari, and Tafsir Ibn Kathir.

virtues.hadith_arabic: سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ: اسْتَقْرِئُوا الْقُرْآنَ مِنْ أَرْبَعَةٍ مِنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ ـ فَبَدَأَ بِهِ ـ وَسَالِمٍ مَوْلَى أَبِي حُذَيْفَةَ، وَمُعَاذِ بْنِ جَبَلٍ، وَأُبَىِّ بْنِ كَعْبٍ
virtues.hadith_english: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) saying: "Learn the recitation of the Qur'an from (any of these) four persons: Abdullah bin Mas'ud — he started with him — Salim the freed slave of Abu Hudhaifa, Mu'adh bin Jabal, and Ubayy bin Ka'b."

virtues.hadith_arabic: قَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: وَاللَّهِ الَّذِي لاَ إِلَهَ غَيْرُهُ مَا أُنْزِلَتْ سُورَةٌ مِنْ كِتَابِ اللَّهِ إِلاَّ أَنَا أَعْلَمُ أَيْنَ أُنْزِلَتْ، وَلاَ أُنْزِلَتْ آيَةٌ مِنْ كِتَابِ اللَّهِ إِلاَّ أَنَا أَعْلَمُ فِيمَا أُنْزِلَتْ، وَلَوْ أَعْلَمُ أَحَدًا أَعْلَمَ مِنِّي بِكِتَابِ اللَّهِ تُبَلِّغُهُ الإِبِلُ لَرَكِبْتُ إِلَيْهِ
virtues.hadith_english: Abdullah (bin Mas'ud) said: "By Allah other than Whom none has the right to be worshipped! There is no Sura revealed in Allah's Book but I know at what place it was revealed; and there is no Verse revealed in Allah's Book but I know about whom it was revealed. And if I knew that there is somebody who knows Allah's Book better than I, and he is at a place that camels can reach, I would go to him."

variants.short_title: 2:31 — Presenting 'Them' (Inanimate vs. Rational)
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran uses the masculine pronoun 'presented them' (implying rational beings), Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy read the feminine 'presented them' (things/creatures).
variants.title: Pronominal Shift from 'ʿAraḍahum' to 'ʿAraḍahunna' / 'ʿAraḍahā' in 2:31
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 2:31, after God taught Adam all the names, the Uthmanic text reads 'ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ' ('Then He presented them to the angels'), using the masculine plural pronoun '-hum' which in Arabic grammar denotes rational beings. Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record that Abdullah bin Mas'ud read 'ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُنَّ' (feminine plural '-hunna') and Ubayy bin Ka'b read 'ثُمَّ عَرَضَهَا' (feminine singular '-hā'), referring broadly to all named objects and non-rational creatures.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: Then He presented them
variants.variant_target_english: Then He presented them (those things)
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِي بِأَسۡمَآءِ هَـٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: And He taught Adam the names – all of them. Then He presented them to the angels, and said, ‘Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful.’
variants.variant_full_arabic: وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُنَّ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِي بِأَسۡمَآءِ هَـٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
variants.variant_full_english: And He taught Adam the names – all of them. Then He presented them (those things) to the angels, and said, ‘Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful.’

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari explains that the Uthmanic masculine plural pronoun '-hum' prevails by grammatical predominance (taghlīb) whenever rational beings (angels and humans) are grouped alongside non-rational things, whereas Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy's feminine pronouns refer directly to the feminine noun 'names' or inanimate objects.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari explicitly notes that Ibn Abbas's famous exegesis—that Adam was taught the names of all everyday objects rather than only angels and human progeny—was based on his following the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b ('ثُمَّ عَرَضَهَا').

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: آدم وأسماء الملائكة، وإن كان ما قال ابن عباس جائزًا على مثال ما جاء في كتاب الله من قوله: وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَ كُلَّ دَابَّةٍ مِنْ مَاءٍ فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِي عَلَى بَطْنِهِ الآية. وقد ذكر أنها في حرف ابن مسعود: " ثم عَرضهن "، وأنها في حرف أبَيّ: " ثم عَرضَها ". (115)
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Therefore, I said: it is most fitting regarding the interpretation of the verse that the names which He taught Adam were the names of the specific entities of the children of Adam and the names of the angels, even though what Ibn 'Abbas said is permissible, akin to what occurs in the Book of Allah in His statement: {Allah has created every moving creature from water. Of them there are some that creep on their bellies} the verse. And it has been mentioned that it is recited in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "Thumma aradahunna" (Then He presented them - fem. pl.), and that it is in the reading of Ubayy: "Thumma aradaha" (Then He presented them - fem. sing.) (115).
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وقد ذكر أنها في حرف ابن مسعود: " ثم عَرضهن "، وأنها في حرف أبَيّ: " ثم عَرضَها "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "Thumma aradahunna" (Then He presented them - fem. pl.), and that it is in the reading of Ubayy: "Thumma aradaha"

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: [ وقد قرأ عبد الله بن مسعود : ثم عرضهن وقرأ أبي بن كعب : ثم عرضها أي : السماوات ] .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: ['Abdullah bin Mas'ud recited: {Then He presented them (hunna)}, and Ubayy bin Ka'b recited: {Then He presented them (ha)}, meaning: the heavens].
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وقد قرأ عبد الله بن مسعود : ثم عرضهن وقرأ أبي بن كعب : ثم عرضها
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud recited: {Then He presented them (hunna)}, and Ubayy bin Ka'b recited: {Then He presented them (ha)}

variants.short_title: 'Its Garlic' (Thumiha) vs 'Its Corn' (Fumiha) in 2:61
variants.plain_english_hook: Commentators debated whether 'fumiha' in 2:61 meant wheat/bread or garlic; Abdullah bin Masud's recitation read 'thumiha' ('its garlic' with tha) and 'Misr' without an alif.
variants.title: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:61 — 'Wa-Thumiha' (Its Garlic) in Ibn Mas'ud's Reading
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 2:61, the Israelites ask Moses for the earth's produce including وَفُومِهَا ('its corn/wheat' or 'garlic', written with fa'), and Moses replies اهْبِطُوا مِصْرًا (written with a final alif of tanwin, which many interpreted as 'any city'). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record that Abdullah bin Mas'ud recited وَثُومِهَا ('and its garlic', with tha'), and that both Ubayy bin Ka'b and Ibn Mas'ud read اهْبِطُوا مِصْرَ without an alif or tanwin (specifying Pharaoh's Egypt rather than an indefinite city).
variants.uthmanic_target_english: its corn
variants.variant_target_english: its garlic
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: وَإِذۡ قُلۡتُمۡ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَن نَّصۡبِرَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامٖ وَٰحِدٖ فَٱدۡعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُخۡرِجۡ لَنَا مِمَّا تُنۢبِتُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ مِنۢ بَقۡلِهَا وَقِثَّآئِهَا وَفُومِهَا وَعَدَسِهَا وَبَصَلِهَاۖ قَالَ أَتَسۡتَبۡدِلُونَ ٱلَّذِي هُوَ أَدۡنَىٰ بِٱلَّذِي هُوَ خَيۡرٌۚ ٱهۡبِطُواْ مِصۡرٗا فَإِنَّ لَكُم مَّا سَأَلۡتُمۡۗ وَضُرِبَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلذِّلَّةُ وَٱلۡمَسۡكَنَةُ وَبَآءُو بِغَضَبٖ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ يَكۡفُرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقۡتُلُونَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ بِغَيۡرِ ٱلۡحَقِّۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا عَصَواْ وَّكَانُواْ يَعۡتَدُونَ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: (Remember) when you said, ‘Moses! We cannot endure just one kind of food. Call on your Lord for us, that He may bring forth for us some of what the earth grows: its green herbs, its cucumbers, its corn, its lentils, and its onions.’ He said, ‘Would you exchange what is worse for what is better? Go (back) down to Egypt! Surely you will have what you ask for.’ Humiliation and poverty were stamped upon them, and they incurred the anger of God. That was because they had disbelieved in the signs of God, and killed the prophets without any right. That was because they disobeyed and went on transgressing.

Call on your Lord for us, that He may bring forth for us some of what the earth grows: its green herbs, its cucumbers, its garlic, its lentils, and its onions.’ He said, ‘Would you exchange what is worse for what is better? scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari explains 'fumiha' and 'thumiha' as phonetic labial/interdental alternates (ibdal between fa' and tha'), while disallowing the un-nunated reading 'Misr' because all Uthmanic manuscripts write an alif at the end of 'Misran'.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: The presence of two distinct consonantal variants in a single verse in Ibn Mas'ud's and Ubayy's recitations ('thumiha' with tha' and 'Misr' without alif) shows how early Companion codices differed both lexically and orthographically from the Uthmanic rasm.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وذكر أن ذلك قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود: " وثومها " بالثاء . قالوا: وأخرى، أنها في قراءة أبي بن كعب وعبد الله بن مسعود: " اهبطوا مصر " بغير ألف . قالوا: ففي ذلك الدلالة البينة أنها " مصر " بعينها .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: And it was mentioned that this is the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud: "wa-thumiha" (and its garlic) with a Tha'. They said: And another, is that it is in the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b and 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud: "Go down to Misr" without an Alif. They said: So in this is clear evidence that it is "Egypt" specifically.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود: " وثومها " بالثاء
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud: "wa-thumiha" (and its garlic) with a Tha'

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وأما الفوم فقد اختلف السلف في معناه فوقع في قراءة ابن مسعود وثومها بالثاء ، وكذلك فسره مجاهد في رواية ليث بن أبي سليم ، عنه ، بالثوم . وقال ابن جرير : وقع في قراءة أبي بن كعب وابن مسعود : اهبطوا مصر من غير إجراء يعني من غير صرف .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: As for the *Fum*, the Salaf differed over its meaning. In the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud, it is *Thum* (garlic) with a *Tha*. Likewise, Mujahid explained it as garlic, in a narration by Layth bin Abi Sulaym from him... Ibn Jarir said, "In the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b and Ibn Mas'ud, it is '*Misr*' without inflection (without *Tanwin*).
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة ابن مسعود وثومها بالثاء
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: In the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud, it is *Thum* (garlic) with a *Tha*.

variants.short_title: The Abrogation Verse (2:106) in Ibn Masud's Codex
variants.plain_english_hook: In the famous abrogation verse (2:106), Abdullah bin Masud's codex transposed the verbs, addressed Muhammad directly ('We cause you to forget'), and omitted 'better than it'.
variants.title: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:106 — 'Ma Nunsika min Ayatin' in Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 2:106, God states: 'Whatever verse We cancel or cause to be forgotten, We bring a better (one) than it, or (one) similar to it' (مَا نَنْسَخْ مِنْ آيَةٍ أَوْ نُنْسِهَا نَأْتِ بِخَيْرٍ مِنْهَا أَوْ مِثْلِهَا). Al-Tabari records that in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud the verse read: 'Whatever verse We cause you to forget or cancel, We bring (one) similar to it' (مَا نُنْسِكَ مِنْ آيَةٍ أَوْ نَنْسَخْهَا نَجِئْ بِمِثْلِهَا)—adding the second-person suffix -ka to 'nunsika', inverting the order of forgetting and cancelling, substituting 'naji'' for 'na'ti', and omitting 'a better (one) than it, or'.
variants.uthmanic_target_arabic: مَا نَنسَخۡ مِنۡ ءَايَةٍ أَوۡ نُنسِهَا نَأۡتِ بِخَيۡرٖ مِّنۡهَآ أَوۡ مِثۡلِهَآ
variants.uthmanic_target_english: Whatever verse We cancel or cause to be forgotten, We bring a better (one) than it, or (one) similar to it
variants.variant_target_arabic: مَا نُنسِكَ مِنۡ ءَايَةٍ أَوۡ نَنسَخۡهَا نَجِئۡ بِمِثۡلِهَا
variants.variant_target_english: Whatever verse We cause you to forget or cancel, We bring (one) similar to it
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: ۞مَا نَنسَخۡ مِنۡ ءَايَةٍ أَوۡ نُنسِهَا نَأۡتِ بِخَيۡرٖ مِّنۡهَآ أَوۡ مِثۡلِهَآۗ أَلَمۡ تَعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ قَدِيرٌ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: Whatever verse We cancel or cause to be forgotten, We bring a better (one) than it, or (one) similar to it. Do you not know that God is powerful over everything?
variants.variant_full_arabic: ۞مَا نُنسِكَ مِنۡ ءَايَةٍ أَوۡ نَنسَخۡهَا نَجِئۡ بِمِثۡلِهَاۗ أَلَمۡ تَعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ قَدِيرٌ
variants.variant_full_english: Whatever verse We cause you to forget or cancel, We bring (one) similar to it. Do you not know that God is powerful over everything?

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari cites Ibn Mas'ud's codex reading to support the interpretation of 'nunsiha' as literal forgetting (al-nisyan) experienced by the Prophet rather than merely leaving or delaying a verse.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: The reading preserved in Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf exhibits four distinct consonantal differences across a single clause—including the omission of 'bi-khayrin minha aw' ('a better one than it, or') and the substitution of 'naji'' for 'na'ti'—which cannot be reduced to vocalization.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: اخْتَلَفَتْ الْقِرَاءَة فِي قَوْله ذَلِكَ , فَقَرَأَهَا قُرَّاء أَهْل الْمَدِينَة وَالْكُوفَة : { أَوْ نُنْسِهَا } وَلِقِرَاءَةِ مَنْ قَرَأَ ذَلِكَ وَجْهَانِ مِنْ التَّأْوِيل , أَحَدهمَا : أَنْ يَكُون تَأْوِيله : مَا نَنْسَخ يَا مُحَمَّد مِنْ آيَة فَنُغَيِّر حُكْمهَا أَوْ نُنْسِهَا . وَقَدْ ذُكِرَ أَنَّهَا فِي مُصْحَف عَبْد اللَّه : { مَا نُنْسِك مِنْ آيَة أَوْ نَنْسَخهَا نَجِئْ بِمِثْلِهَا } , فَذَلِكَ تَأْوِيل النِّسْيَان .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: One of them is that its interpretation is: Whatever verse We cancel, O Muhammad, and thus change its ruling, or We cause it to be forgotten. And it has been mentioned that in the Mus-haf of 'Abdullah (bin Mas'ud) it is: "Whatever verse We cause you to forget (*ma nunsika*) or We cancel, We bring its like." And that is the interpretation of forgetting (*al-nisyan*).
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: فِي مُصْحَف عَبْد اللَّه : { مَا نُنْسِك مِنْ آيَة أَوْ نَنْسَخهَا نَجِئْ بِمِثْلِهَا }
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the Mus-haf of 'Abdullah (bin Mas'ud) it is: "Whatever verse We cause you to forget (*ma nunsika*) or We cancel, We bring its like."

variants.short_title: 'You Will Never Be Questioned' in 2:119
variants.plain_english_hook: Canonical reciters split over whether 2:119 means 'Do not ask' or 'You will not be questioned'; Ibn Masud read 'You will never be questioned' (wa-lan) and Ubayy read 'wa-ma'.
variants.title: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:119 — 'Wa-Lan Tus'ala' (Ibn Mas'ud) vs Uthmanic 'Wa-La'
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 2:119, the consonantal rasm وَلَا تُسْأَلُ was read by Nafi' and Ya'qub as a prohibition ('And do not ask [wa-la tas'al] about the companions of the Furnace') and by the other canonical reciters as a declarative statement ('And you will not be questioned [wa-la tus'alu]'). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record that in the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud it read وَلَنْ تُسْأَلَ ('And you will never be questioned', with lan), and in the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b it read وَمَا تُسْأَلُ ('And you are not questioned', with ma), both consonantally excluding the prohibitive reading.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: You will not be questioned
variants.variant_target_english: You will never be questioned
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: إِنَّآ أَرۡسَلۡنَٰكَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ بَشِيرٗا وَنَذِيرٗاۖ وَلَا تُسۡـَٔلُ عَنۡ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلۡجَحِيمِ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: Surely We have sent you with the truth, as a bringer of good news and a warner. You will not be questioned about the companions of the Furnace.
variants.variant_full_arabic: إِنَّآ أَرۡسَلۡنَٰكَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ بَشِيرٗا وَنَذِيرٗاۖ وَلَن تُسۡـَٔلَ عَنۡ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلۡجَحِيمِ
variants.variant_full_english: Surely We have sent you with the truth, as a bringer of good news and a warner. You will never be questioned about the companions of the Furnace.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari appeals to the recitations of Ubayy ('wa-ma tus'alu') and Ibn Mas'ud ('wa-lan tus'ala') as corroborating evidence that the Uthmanic word 'wa-la tus'alu' is a declarative statement rather than a prohibition.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Replacing the ambiguous particle 'la' (which can be either negative or prohibitive) with 'lan' in Ibn Mas'ud's codex and 'ma' in Ubayy's codex alters the consonantal skeleton and eliminates the grammatical ambiguity that divided the canonical Medinan and Iraqi reciters.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقد ذكر أنها في قراءة أبي: (وما تسأل) ، وفي قراءة ابن مسعود: (ولن تسأل) ، وكلتا هاتين القراءتين تشهد بالرفع والخبر فيه ، دون النهي.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: And it has been mentioned that in the recitation of Ubayy it is: (And you are not questioned), and in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: (And you will never be questioned), and both of these recitations testify to the raf' and the informative statement within it, exclusive of the prohibition.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود: (ولن تسأل)
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: (And you will never be questioned)

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقوله : ( ولا تسأل عن أصحاب الجحيم ) قراءة أكثرهم ( ولا تسأل ) بضم التاء على الخبر . وفي قراءة أبي بن كعب : " وما تسأل " وفي قراءة ابن مسعود : " ولن تسأل عن أصحاب الجحيم " نقلهما ابن جرير .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: The majority recite it as *(wa la tus'alu)* with a Dammah on the Ta' as a declarative sentence. In the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b, it is read: *(wa ma tus'al)* (and you are not questioned), while in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud, it is read: *(wa lan tus'ala 'an ashab il-jahim)* (and you will never be questioned about the companions of the Furnace). Both of these were transmitted by Ibn Jarir.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود : " ولن تسأل عن أصحاب الجحيم "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud, it is read: *(wa lan tus'ala 'an ashab il-jahim)* (and you will never be questioned about the companions of the Furnace)

variants.short_title: Added Negation 'Not to Go Around' in Surah 2:158
variants.plain_english_hook: The codices of Abdullah bin Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas included the word 'not' in Surah 2:158 ('no blame if he does not go around Safa and Marwa'), reversing the verse into an exemption from the ritual.
variants.title: Addition of the Negative Particle 'La' ('An La Yattawwafa Bihima') in Surah 2:158
variants.diff_summary: Whereas the Uthmanic Mushaf reads 'fa-lā junāḥa 'alayhi an yaṭṭawwafa bihimā' ('there is no blame on him if he goes around both of them'), Tafsir al-Tabari (#1953–1954) documents that the codex of Abdullah bin Mas'ud and the recitation of Ibn Abbas included the negative particle 'lā' ('an lā yaṭṭawwafa bihimā' — 'there is no blame on him if he does not go around both of them'). Based on this codex reading, early jurists such as Ata', Anas bin Malik, and Ibn Sirin ruled that walking between al-Safa and al-Marwah is optional, whereas Aisha (in Sahih al-Bukhari 1643 and 4495) rejected that legal conclusion by appealing to the Uthmanic wording without 'lā'.
variants.uthmanic_target_arabic: فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡهِ أَن يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَا
variants.uthmanic_target_english: (there is) no blame on him if he goes around both of them
variants.variant_target_arabic: فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ لَا يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَا
variants.variant_target_english: (there is) no blame on him if he does not go around both of them
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: ۞إِنَّ ٱلصَّفَا وَٱلۡمَرۡوَةَ مِن شَعَآئِرِ ٱللَّهِۖ فَمَنۡ حَجَّ ٱلۡبَيۡتَ أَوِ ٱعۡتَمَرَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡهِ أَن يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَاۚ وَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرٗا فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَاكِرٌ عَلِيمٌ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: Surely al-Ṣafā and al-Marwa are among the symbols of God. Whoever performs pilgrimage to the House or performs visitation – (there is) no blame on him if he goes around both of them. And whoever does good voluntarily – surely God is thankful, knowing.
variants.variant_full_arabic: ۞إِنَّ ٱلصَّفَا وَٱلۡمَرۡوَةَ مِن شَعَآئِرِ ٱللَّهِۖ فَمَنۡ حَجَّ ٱلۡبَيۡتَ أَوِ ٱعۡتَمَرَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ لَا يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَاۚ وَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرٗا فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَاكِرٌ عَلِيمٌ
variants.variant_full_english: Surely al-Ṣafā and al-Marwa are among the symbols of God. Whoever performs pilgrimage to the House or performs visitation – (there is) no blame on him if he does not go around both of them. And whoever does good voluntarily – surely God is thankful, knowing.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: In Sahih al-Bukhari 1643 and 4495, Aisha defends the Uthmanic reading by explaining the historical occasion of revelation (the Ansar's pre-Islamic hesitation to walk between the two hills), while al-Tabari argues that even if 'lā' was written in Ibn Mas'ud's codex, it could be interpreted as a pleonastic (redundant) negation.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari's explicit transmission (#1953–1954) that Ata' and other early authorities derived the non-obligatory status of Sa'i directly 'because of the saying of God in the codex of Ibn Mas'ud: there is no blame on him if he does not go around both of them' proves that the particle 'lā' was understood by its readers as a substantive legal negation, not a grammatical redundancy.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 1953 - حدثنا محمد بن بشار , قال : ثنا أبو عاصم , قال : ثنا ابن جريج , قال : قال عطاء : لو أن حاجا أفاض بعدما رمى جمرة العقبة فطاف بالبيت ولم يسع , فأصابها - يعني امرأته - لم يكن عليه شيء , لا حج ولا عمرة ; من أجل قول الله في مصحف ابن مسعود : " فمن حج البيت أو اعتمر فلا جناح عليه أن لا يطوف بهما " ... 1954 - حدثني يعقوب بن إبراهيم , قال : ثنا هشيم , قال : أخبرنا عبد الملك , عن عطاء , عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرأ : { إن الصفا والمروة من شعائر الله } الآية , { فلا جناح عليه أن لا يطوف بهما } .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 1953 - Muhammad b. Bashshar narrated to us, from Abu 'Asim, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Ata' said: If a pilgrim departs after he threw the Jamrat al-'Aqabah, and went around the House and did not hasten, then touched her—meaning his wife—there would be nothing upon him, not in Hajj nor in 'Umrah; due to the saying of God in the codex of Ibn Mas'ud: "Whoever performs pilgrimage to the House or performs visitation – (there is) no blame on him if he does not go around both of them." ... 1954 - Ya'qub b. Ibrahim narrated to me, from Hushaym, from 'Abd al-Malik, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite: {Surely al-Safa and al-Marwa are among the symbols of God}, the verse, "(there is) no blame on him if he does not go around both of them."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: من أجل قول الله في مصحف ابن مسعود : " فمن حج البيت أو اعتمر فلا جناح عليه أن لا يطوف بهما "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: due to the saying of God in the codex of Ibn Mas'ud: "Whoever performs pilgrimage to the House or performs visitation – (there is) no blame on him if he does not go around both of them."

variants.short_title: 2:196 — 'Establish Hajj and Umrah to the House'
variants.plain_english_hook: Instead of 'Complete the pilgrimage and the visitation for God,' Ibn Mas'ud's codex read 'Establish the pilgrimage and the visitation to the House.'
variants.title: Substitution of 'Establish... to the House' for 'Complete... for God' in 2:196
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 2:196, the Uthmanic text begins 'وَأَتِمُّواْ ٱلۡحَجَّ وَٱلۡعُمۡرَةَ لِلَّهِۚ' ('Complete the pilgrimage and the visitation for God.'). Both al-Tabari (2599–2601, 2622) and Ibn Kathir record via al-A'mash from Ibrahim from Alqamah that in the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud (and endorsed by Ibn Abbas and Ali) it read 'وَأَقِيمُوا الْحَجَّ وَالْعُمْرَةَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ' ('Establish the pilgrimage and the visitation to the House.'), which Kufan jurists cited to show that Umrah rites end at the Ka'bah.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: Complete the pilgrimage and the visitation for God
variants.variant_target_english: Establish the pilgrimage and the visitation to the House
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: وَأَتِمُّواْ ٱلۡحَجَّ وَٱلۡعُمۡرَةَ لِلَّهِۚ فَإِنۡ أُحۡصِرۡتُمۡ فَمَا ٱسۡتَيۡسَرَ مِنَ ٱلۡهَدۡيِۖ وَلَا تَحۡلِقُواْ رُءُوسَكُمۡ حَتَّىٰ يَبۡلُغَ ٱلۡهَدۡيُ مَحِلَّهُۥۚ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوۡ بِهِۦٓ أَذٗى مِّن رَّأۡسِهِۦ فَفِدۡيَةٞ مِّن صِيَامٍ أَوۡ صَدَقَةٍ أَوۡ نُسُكٖۚ فَإِذَآ أَمِنتُمۡ فَمَن تَمَتَّعَ بِٱلۡعُمۡرَةِ إِلَى ٱلۡحَجِّ فَمَا ٱسۡتَيۡسَرَ مِنَ ٱلۡهَدۡيِۚ فَمَن لَّمۡ يَجِدۡ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَٰثَةِ أَيَّامٖ فِي ٱلۡحَجِّ وَسَبۡعَةٍ إِذَا رَجَعۡتُمۡۗ تِلۡكَ عَشَرَةٞ كَامِلَةٞۗ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن لَّمۡ يَكُنۡ أَهۡلُهُۥ حَاضِرِي ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: Complete the pilgrimage and the visitation for God. But if you are prevented, (make) whatever offering is easy to obtain. Do not shave your heads until the offering has reached its lawful place. Whoever of you is sick or has an injury to his head, (there is) a ransom of fasting or a freewill offering or a sacrifice. When you are secure, whoever makes use of (the time from) the visitation until the pilgrimage, (let him make) whatever offering is easy to obtain. Whoever cannot find (an offering), (let him perform) a fast of three days during the pilgrimage, and seven (days) when you return. That is ten (days) in all. That is for the one whose family is not present at the Sacred Mosque. Guard (yourselves) against God, and know that God is harsh in retribution.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Commentators view 'Establish... to the House' as an exegetical reading clarifying that the rites of Umrah are confined to the Sacred House (the Ka'bah and Safa-Marwah) rather than extending to Arafat.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari records multiple authentic Kufan chains showing that Alqamah and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i actively recited 'وَأَقِيمُوا الْحَجَّ وَالْعُمْرَةَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ' as the text of the verse following Abdullah bin Mas'ud.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 2599 - حدثني عبيد بن إسماعيل الهباري , قال : ثنا عبد الله بن نمير , عن الأعمش , عن إبراهيم , عن علقمة : { وأتموا الحج والعمرة لله } قال : هو في قراءة عبد الله : { وأقيموا الحج والعمرة إلى البيت } قال : لا تجاوزوا بالعمرة البيت . قال إبراهيم : فذكرت ذلك لسعيد بن جبير , فقال : كذلك قال ابن عباس .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: {Complete the pilgrimage and the visitation for God}, he said: It is in the recitation of 'Abdullah: {And establish the Hajj and the 'Umrah to the House}. He said: Do not pass beyond the House during the 'Umrah. Ibrahim said: I mentioned that to Sa'id bin Jubayr, and he said: Ibn 'Abbas also said thus.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: هو في قراءة عبد الله : { وأقيموا الحج والعمرة إلى البيت }
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: It is in the recitation of 'Abdullah: {And establish the Hajj and the 'Umrah to the House}

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقال قتادة ، عن زرارة ، عن ابن عباس أنه قال : الحج عرفة ، والعمرة الطواف . وكذا روى الأعمش ، عن إبراهيم عن علقمة في قوله : ( وأتموا الحج والعمرة لله ) قال : هي [ في ] قراءة عبد الله : " وأقيموا الحج والعمرة إلى البيت " لا تجاوز بالعمرة البيت . قال إبراهيم : فذكرت ذلك لسعيد بن جبير ، فقال : كذلك قال ابن عباس .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: "'Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) recited it this way: 'Establish [wa-aqimu] Hajj and 'Umrah to the House, so that one does not exceed the area of the House during the 'Umrah'." Ibrahim then said, "I mentioned this statement to Sa'id bin Jubayr and he said, 'Ibn 'Abbas also said that.'"
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: قراءة عبد الله : " وأقيموا الحج والعمرة إلى البيت "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: 'Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) recited it this way: 'Establish [wa-aqimu] Hajj and 'Umrah to the House

variants.short_title: 'For the One Who Fears God' in 2:203 (Ibn Masud)
variants.plain_english_hook: In the Hajj rites of 2:203, the standard Quran ends the clause with 'for the one who guards (himself)' (liman ittaqa); Ibn Masud's codex added the object 'God' (liman ittaqa Allaha).
variants.title: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:203 — Addition of 'Allah' in Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 2:203, pilgrims departing Mina in two days or delaying have no sin on them 'for the one who guards (himself)' (لِمَنِ اتَّقَىٰ), followed by 'Guard (yourselves) against God' (وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ). Al-Tabari records via Ibn Jurayj that in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud the first clause explicitly included the divine name: لِمَنِ اتَّقَى اللَّهَ ('for the one who guards (himself) against God').
variants.uthmanic_target_english: (at least) for the one who guards (himself)
variants.variant_target_english: (at least) for the one who guards (himself) against God
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: ۞وَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ فِيٓ أَيَّامٖ مَّعۡدُودَٰتٖۚ فَمَن تَعَجَّلَ فِي يَوۡمَيۡنِ فَلَآ إِثۡمَ عَلَيۡهِ وَمَن تَأَخَّرَ فَلَآ إِثۡمَ عَلَيۡهِۖ لِمَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰۗ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّكُمۡ إِلَيۡهِ تُحۡشَرُونَ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: Remember God during a (certain) number of days. Whoever hurries (through it) in two days – no sin (rests) on him, and whoever delays – no sin (rests) on him, (at least) for the one who guards (himself). Guard (yourselves) against God, and know that you will be gathered to Him.

Whoever hurries (through it) in two days – no sin (rests) on him, and whoever delays – no sin (rests) on him, (at least) for the one who guards (himself) against God. Guard (yourselves) against God, and know that you will be gathered to Him.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical commentators regard the addition of 'Allah' after 'liman ittaqa' as making explicit the implied object of piety (taqwa) that immediately follows in 'wattaqu Allaha'.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari records Ibn Jurayj's direct statement that the word 'Allah' stood in the text of Abdullah bin Mas'ud's Mushaf at this position.

variants.short_title: 'One Community, Then They Differed' in 2:213
variants.plain_english_hook: Surah 2:213 jumps directly from 'The people were one community' to 'Then God raised up the prophets'; Ibn Masud and Ubayy's codices supplied the missing link: 'then they differed'.
variants.title: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:213 — Addition of 'Fa-Ikhtalafu' in Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 2:213, the verse begins 'The people were (once) one community. Then God raised up the prophets as bringers of good news and warners' (كَانَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ النَّبِيِّينَ), leaving unstated why prophets were sent if humanity was united. Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record via authentic chains from Ibn Abbas and Abu al-'Aliyah that the recitations of Abdullah bin Mas'ud and Ubayy bin Ka'b explicitly included 'then they differed' (كَانَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً فَاخْتَلَفُوا فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ النَّبِيِّينَ), and also note that Ubayy read 'and so that they may be witnesses over the people on the Day of Resurrection' near the end of the verse.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: The people were (once) one community. Then God raised up
variants.variant_target_arabic: كَانَ ٱلنَّاسُ أُمَّةٗ وَٰحِدَةٗ فَٱخۡتَلَفُواْ فَبَعَثَ
variants.variant_target_english: The people were (once) one community, then they differed. Then God raised up
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: كَانَ ٱلنَّاسُ أُمَّةٗ وَٰحِدَةٗ فَبَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنذِرِينَ وَأَنزَلَ مَعَهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ لِيَحۡكُمَ بَيۡنَ ٱلنَّاسِ فِيمَا ٱخۡتَلَفُواْ فِيهِۚ وَمَا ٱخۡتَلَفَ فِيهِ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوهُ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَتۡهُمُ ٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتُ بَغۡيَۢا بَيۡنَهُمۡۖ فَهَدَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لِمَا ٱخۡتَلَفُواْ فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلۡحَقِّ بِإِذۡنِهِۦۗ وَٱللَّهُ يَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٖ مُّسۡتَقِيمٍ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: The people were (once) one community. Then God raised up the prophets as bringers of good news and warners, and with them He sent down the Book with the truth to judge among the people concerning their differences. Only those who had been given it differed concerning it, after the clear signs had come to them, (because of) envy among themselves. And God guided those who believed to the truth concerning which they differed, by His permission. God guides whomever He pleases to a straight path.

variants.variant_full_english: The people were (once) one community, then they differed. Then God raised up the prophets as bringers of good news and warners, and with them He sent down the Book with the truth to judge among the people concerning their differences. Only those who had been given it differed concerning it, after the clear signs had come to them, (because of) envy among themselves. And God guided those who believed to the truth concerning which they differed, by His permission. God guides whomever He pleases to a straight path.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical scholars explain that the Uthmanic text relies on rhetorical ellipsis (idmar) where 'then they differed' is understood from the later phrase 'to judge among the people concerning their differences', while treating the Companion wording as an explanatory gloss.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir cite the authenticated report of Ibn Abbas (graded sahih by al-Hakim) appealing directly to the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud and Ubayy bin Ka'b ('fa-ikhtalafu') to supply the verb required by the narrative logic of the verse.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 4048 - حدثنا محمد بن بشار، قال: حدثنا أبو داود، قال: حدثنا همام بن منبه، عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، قال: كان بين نوح وآدم عشرة قرون، كلهم على شريعة من الحق، فاختلفوا، فبعث الله النبيين مبشرين ومنذرين، قال: وكذلك هي في قراءة عبد الله " كان الناس أمة واحدة فاختلفوا ". وهي في قراءة أبي بن كعب: ( وليكونوا شهداء على الناس ) يوم القيامة ( والله يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم ).
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 4048 - Muhammad bin Bashshar narrated to us... from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Between Nuh and Adam were ten generations, all of them upon a law of truth, then they differed, so Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good news and warners. He said: And likewise it is in the recitation of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]: "The people were one community, then they differed." And it is in the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b: {(And so that they would be witnesses over the people)} on the Day of Resurrection {(And God guides whomever He pleases to a straight path)}.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة عبد الله " كان الناس أمة واحدة فاختلفوا "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]: "The people were one community, then they differed."

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: عن عكرمة ، عن ابن عباس ، قال : كان بين نوح وآدم عشرة قرون ، كلهم على شريعة من الحق . فاختلفوا ، فبعث الله النبيين مبشرين ومنذرين . قال : وكذلك هي في قراءة عبد الله : " كان الناس أمة واحدة فاختلفوا " . ورواه الحاكم في مستدركه ، من حديث بندار عن محمد بن بشار . ثم قال : صحيح ولم يخرجاه . وكذا روى أبو جعفر الرازي ، عن أبي العالية ، عن أبي بن كعب : أنه كان يقرؤها : " كان الناس أمة واحدة فاختلفوا فبعث الله النبيين مبشرين ومنذرين " .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: From 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Between Nuh and Adam were ten generations, all of them upon a law of truth. Then they differed, so Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good news and warners." He said: "And likewise it is in the recitation of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]: 'The people were one community, then they differed.'" Al-Hakim recorded it in his Mustadrak... and said: "It is Sahih, though they (Al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it." Similarly, Abu Ja'far Ar-Razi narrated from Abu Al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy bin Ka'b, that he used to recite it: "The people were one community, then they differed, so Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good news and warners."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة عبد الله : " كان الناس أمة واحدة فاختلفوا "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]: 'The people were one community, then they differed.'

variants.short_title: Who Knows the Ambiguous Verses in 3:7?
variants.plain_english_hook: Scholars debated for centuries where the sentence breaks in 3:7; Ibn Masud and Ubayy's codices worded the clause so that only God knows the ambiguous verses' interpretation.
variants.title: Surah Al 'Imran 3:7 — Syntactic Separation of 'Those Firm in Knowledge'
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 3:7 (وَمَا يَعْلَمُ تَأْوِيلَهُ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَالرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ يَقُولُونَ آمَنَّا بِهِ), exegetes and theologians were divided over whether 'and those firmly grounded in knowledge' is conjoined to 'God' (meaning scholars also know the interpretation of ambiguous verses) or begins a new sentence. Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record that Abdullah bin Mas'ud's reading was 'Its interpretation is only with God, and the ones firmly grounded in knowledge say, We believe in it' (إِنْ تَأْوِيلُهُ إِلَّا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَالرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ يَقُولُونَ آمَنَّا بِهِ), while Ubayy bin Ka'b read 'and those firmly grounded in knowledge say' (وَيَقُولُ الرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ), both syntactically precluding conjunction with God.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: No one knows its interpretation except God.
variants.variant_target_english: Its interpretation is only with God.
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنزَلَ عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِنۡهُ ءَايَٰتٞ مُّحۡكَمَٰتٌ هُنَّ أُمُّ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَأُخَرُ مُتَشَٰبِهَٰتٞۖ فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمۡ زَيۡغٞ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَٰبَهَ مِنۡهُ ٱبۡتِغَآءَ ٱلۡفِتۡنَةِ وَٱبۡتِغَآءَ تَأۡوِيلِهِۦۖ وَمَا يَعۡلَمُ تَأۡوِيلَهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُۗ وَٱلرَّـٰسِخُونَ فِي ٱلۡعِلۡمِ يَقُولُونَ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦ كُلّٞ مِّنۡ عِندِ رَبِّنَاۗ وَمَا يَذَّكَّرُ إِلَّآ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: He (it is) who has sent down on you the Book, of which some verses are clearly composed – they are the mother of the Book – but others are ambiguous. As for those in whose hearts (there is) a turning aside, they follow the ambiguous part of it, seeking (to cause) trouble and seeking its interpretation. No one knows its interpretation except God. And (as for) the ones firmly grounded in knowledge, they say, ‘We believe in it. All (of it) is from our Lord.’ Yet no one takes heed except those with understanding.
variants.variant_full_arabic: هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنزَلَ عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِنۡهُ ءَايَٰتٞ مُّحۡكَمَٰتٌ هُنَّ أُمُّ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَأُخَرُ مُتَشَٰبِهَٰتٞۖ فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمۡ زَيۡغٞ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَٰبَهَ مِنۡهُ ٱبۡتِغَآءَ ٱلۡفِتۡنَةِ وَٱبۡتِغَآءَ تَأۡوِيلِهِۦۖ إِنْ تَأْوِيلُهُ إِلَّا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَٱلرَّـٰسِخُونَ فِي ٱلۡعِلۡمِ يَقُولُونَ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦ كُلّٞ مِّنۡ عِندِ رَبِّنَاۗ وَمَا يَذَّكَّرُ إِلَّآ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
variants.variant_full_english: He (it is) who has sent down on you the Book, of which some verses are clearly composed – they are the mother of the Book – but others are ambiguous. As for those in whose hearts (there is) a turning aside, they follow the ambiguous part of it, seeking (to cause) trouble and seeking its interpretation. Its interpretation is only with God. And (as for) the ones firmly grounded in knowledge, they say, ‘We believe in it. All (of it) is from our Lord.’ Yet no one takes heed except those with understanding.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical commentators cite the readings of Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy bin Ka'b as explanatory recitations (qira'at tafsiriyya) proving that a mandatory pause (waqf) falls after the name of God in the Uthmanic text.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explicitly rely on the non-Uthmanic wording of Ibn Mas'ud ('in ta'wiluhu illa 'inda Allah') and Ubayy bin Ka'b ('wa yaqulu al-rasikhuna') to settle a foundational theological dispute over whether human scholars can know the ta'wil of the mutashabihat.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وهو فيما بلغني مع ذلك في قراءة أبي : " ويقول الراسخون في العلم " كما ذكرناه عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرؤه ; وفي قراءة عبد الله : إن تأويله إلا عند الله " والراسخون في العلم يقولون " .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: And that is, along with that, according to what reached me regarding the recitation of Ubayy: "and the ones firmly grounded in knowledge say", just as we mentioned it from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite it; and in the recitation of 'Abdullah: "its interpretation is not except with God, and the ones firmly grounded in knowledge say".
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وفي قراءة عبد الله : إن تأويله إلا عند الله " والراسخون في العلم يقولون "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of 'Abdullah: "its interpretation is not except with God, and the ones firmly grounded in knowledge say"

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وحكى ابن جرير أن في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود : " إن تأويله إلا عند الله والراسخون في العلم يقولون آمنا به " . وكذا عن أبي بن كعب . واختار ابن جرير هذا القول .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Ibn Jarir narrated that in the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud it is: "Its interpretation is only with Allah, and those who are firmly grounded in knowledge say: 'We believe in it.'" And similarly it was narrated from Ubayy bin Ka'b. Ibn Jarir preferred this opinion.

variants.short_title: 'And Fought' (Wa-Qatalu) vs 'And Kill' in 3:21
variants.plain_english_hook: In 3:21, the standard Quran says 'and kill those of the people who command justice'; al-Tabari records that in Ibn Masud's codex it was written 'and fought' (wa-qatalu).
variants.title: Surah Al 'Imran 3:21 — 'Wa-Qatalu' in Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf vs 'Wa-Yaqtuluna'
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 3:21, those who disbelieve are condemned because they kill the prophets and 'kill those of the people who command justice' (وَيَقْتُلُونَ الَّذِينَ يَأْمُرُونَ بِالْقِسْطِ مِنَ النَّاسِ). Al-Tabari records that some Kufan reciters read 'and fight' (وَيُقَاتِلُونَ) based on the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud, in which the verb was written in the past tense Form III: وَقَاتَلُوا ('and fought').
variants.uthmanic_target_english: and kill those of the people who command justice
variants.variant_target_english: and fought those of the people who command justice
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكۡفُرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقۡتُلُونَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ بِغَيۡرِ حَقّٖ وَيَقۡتُلُونَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَأۡمُرُونَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ فَبَشِّرۡهُم بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: Surely those who disbelieve in the signs of God, and kill the prophets without any right, and kill those of the people who command justice – give them news of a painful punishment.
variants.variant_full_arabic: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكۡفُرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقۡتُلُونَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ بِغَيۡرِ حَقّٖ وَقَٰتَلُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ يَأۡمُرُونَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ فَبَشِّرۡهُم بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ
variants.variant_full_english: Surely those who disbelieve in the signs of God, and kill the prophets without any right, and fought those of the people who command justice – give them news of a painful punishment.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari rejects the Kufan reading 'wa-yuqatiluna' and the appeal to Ibn Mas'ud's codex, maintaining that the consensus of the authoritative reciters across the garrison cities establishes 'wa-yaqtuluna' (and kill).
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari's testimony again illustrates how Kufan reciters attempted to bridge the gap between Ibn Mas'ud's codex ('wa-qatalu', Form III past tense) and the Uthmanic rasm by reading Form III imperfect ('wa-yuqatiluna').

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقرأه بعض المتأخرين من قرأة الكوفة: ( ويقاتلون )، بمعنى القتال، تأولا منه قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود، وادعى أن ذلك في مصحف عبد الله: ( وقاتلوا )، فقرأ الذي وصفنا أمره من القراءة بذلك التأويل: ( ويقاتلون ).
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: And some of the later reciters of Kufa recited it: (*wa yuqātilūna* - *and they fight*), in the meaning of fighting, interpreting from it the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud, and he claimed that this was [written] in the codex of 'Abdullah: (*wa qātalū* - *and they fought*), so the one whose matter of recitation we described read with that interpretation: (*wa yuqātilūna*).
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في مصحف عبد الله: ( وقاتلوا )
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the codex of 'Abdullah: (*wa qātalū* - *and they fought*)

variants.short_title: 3:81 — Covenant of the Book's People vs. Prophets
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran says God took a covenant with 'the prophets,' Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy bin Ka'b read 'those who were given the Book,' with Mujahid calling 'prophets' a scribal error.
variants.title: Substitution of 'Those Given the Book' for 'The Prophets' in 3:81
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 3:81, the Uthmanic text reads 'وَإِذۡ أَخَذَ ٱللَّهُ مِيثَٰقَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ' ('when God took a covenant with the prophets'). Al-Tabari records via two authentic chains from Mujahid (7323–7324) and from al-Rabi' bin Anas (7325) that in the recitations of Abdullah bin Mas'ud and Ubayy bin Ka'b it read 'وَإِذْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثَاقَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ' ('when God took a covenant with those who were given the Book').
variants.uthmanic_target_english: a covenant with the prophets
variants.variant_target_english: a covenant with those who were given the Book
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: وَإِذۡ أَخَذَ ٱللَّهُ مِيثَٰقَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ لَمَآ ءَاتَيۡتُكُم مِّن كِتَٰبٖ وَحِكۡمَةٖ ثُمَّ جَآءَكُمۡ رَسُولٞ مُّصَدِّقٞ لِّمَا مَعَكُمۡ لَتُؤۡمِنُنَّ بِهِۦ وَلَتَنصُرُنَّهُۥۚ قَالَ ءَأَقۡرَرۡتُمۡ وَأَخَذۡتُمۡ عَلَىٰ ذَٰلِكُمۡ إِصۡرِيۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَقۡرَرۡنَاۚ قَالَ فَٱشۡهَدُواْ وَأَنَا۠ مَعَكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّـٰهِدِينَ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: (Remember) when God took a covenant with the prophets: ‘Whatever indeed I have given you of the Book and wisdom, when a messenger comes to you confirming what is with you, you are to believe in him and you are to help him.’ He said, ‘Do you agree and accept My burden on that (condition)?’ They said, ‘We agree.’ He said, ‘Bear witness, and I shall be with you among the witnesses.’
variants.variant_full_arabic: وَإِذۡ أَخَذَ ٱللَّهُ مِيثَاقَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ لَمَآ ءَاتَيۡتُكُم مِّن كِتَٰبٖ وَحِكۡمَةٖ ثُمَّ جَآءَكُمۡ رَسُولٞ مُّصَدِّقٞ لِّمَا مَعَكُمۡ لَتُؤۡمِنُنَّ بِهِۦ وَلَتَنصُرُنَّهُۥۚ قَالَ ءَأَقۡرَرۡتُمۡ وَأَخَذۡتُمۡ عَلَىٰ ذَٰلِكُمۡ إِصۡرِيۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَقۡرَرۡنَاۚ قَالَ فَٱشۡهَدُواْ وَأَنَا۠ مَعَكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّـٰهِدِينَ
variants.variant_full_english: (Remember) when God took a covenant with those who were given the Book: ‘Whatever indeed I have given you of the Book and wisdom, when a messenger comes to you confirming what is with you, you are to believe in him and you are to help him.’ He said, ‘Do you agree and accept My burden on that (condition)?’ They said, ‘We agree.’ He said, ‘Bear witness, and I shall be with you among the witnesses.’

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari argues that single-chain reports attributing variant readings or scribal errors to Companions cannot override the consensus codex, and later editors suggest Mujahid only meant the scribe wrote an earlier recitation instead of the final review.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In Tabari 7323–7324, Mujahid explicitly states regarding 'covenant with the prophets': 'It is an error from the scribe (هي خطأ من الكاتب), and in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud it is: And when God took the covenant of those who were given the Book.'

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 7323 - حدثني محمد بن عمرو قال، حدثنا أبو عاصم، عن عيسى، عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد في قوله: " وإذ أخذَ الله ميثاق النبيين لما آتيتكم من كتاب وحكمة "، قال: هي خطأ من الكاتب، وهي في قراءة ابن مسعود: " وإذ أخذَ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب ". (37) 7325 - حدثني المثنى قال، حدثنا إسحاق قال، حدثنا عبد الله بن أبي جعفر، عن أبيه، عن الربيع في قوله: " وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق النبيين "، يقول: وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب، وكذلك كان يقرؤها الربيع: " وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب "، إنما هي أهل الكتاب. قال: وكذلك كان يقرأها أبي بن كعب.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: **7323** - *Muhammad bin ‘Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu ‘Asim narrated to us, from ‘Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying:* "(Remember) when God took a covenant with the prophets: ‘Whatever indeed I have given you of the Book and wisdom’", he said: It is an error from the scribe, and it is in the recitation of Ibn Mas‘ud: "And when God took the covenant of those who were given the Book." 7325 — Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abdullah bin Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from Al-Rabi' regarding His saying: "And when God took the covenant of the prophets", he says: "And when God took the covenant of those who were given the Book," and thus Al-Rabi' used to recite it. He said: And thus Ubayy bin Ka'b used to recite it as well.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: هي خطأ من الكاتب، وهي في قراءة ابن مسعود: " وإذ أخذَ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: It is an error from the scribe, and it is in the recitation of Ibn Mas‘ud: "And when God took the covenant of those who were given the Book."

variants.short_title: 'It Will Be Written' vs 'We Shall Write' in 3:181
variants.plain_english_hook: In 3:181, the standard Quran reads in the first-person plural 'We shall write... and We shall say' (wa-naqulu); Ibn Masud's codex had the passive 'and it will be said' (wa-yuqalu).
variants.title: Surah Al 'Imran 3:181 — Passive 'Sayuktabu... wa-Yuqalu' in Ibn Mas'ud's Codex
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 3:181, the majority of reciters read in the first-person plural active: سَنَكْتُبُ مَا قَالُوا وَقَتْلَهُمُ الْأَنْبِيَاءَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ وَنَقُولُ ('We shall write down what they have said, along with their killing the prophets without any right, and We shall say'). Al-Tabari notes that the Kufan canonical reciter Hamzah read the passive سَيُكْتَبُ ('will be written') and nominative وَقَتْلُهُمُ by relying on the Mushaf and recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud, which read سَيُكْتَبُ ... وَيُقَالُ ('will be written ... and it will be said', with ya' and alif in 'yuqalu' instead of nun and waw in 'naqulu').
variants.uthmanic_target_arabic: سَنَكۡتُبُ مَا قَالُواْ وَقَتۡلَهُمُ ٱلۡأَنۢبِيَآءَ بِغَيۡرِ حَقّٖ وَنَقُولُ
variants.uthmanic_target_english: We shall write down what they have said, along with their killing the prophets without any right, and We shall say
variants.variant_target_arabic: سَيُكۡتَبُ مَا قَالُواْ وَقَتۡلُهُمُ ٱلۡأَنۢبِيَآءَ بِغَيۡرِ حَقّٖ وَيُقَالُ
variants.variant_target_english: What they have said will be written down, along with their killing the prophets without any right, and it will be said
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: لَّقَدۡ سَمِعَ ٱللَّهُ قَوۡلَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ فَقِيرٞ وَنَحۡنُ أَغۡنِيَآءُۘ سَنَكۡتُبُ مَا قَالُواْ وَقَتۡلَهُمُ ٱلۡأَنۢبِيَآءَ بِغَيۡرِ حَقّٖ وَنَقُولُ ذُوقُواْ عَذَابَ ٱلۡحَرِيقِ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: Certainly God has heard the words of those who said, ‘Surely God is poor and we are rich.’ We shall write down what they have said, along with their killing the prophets without any right, and We shall say, ‘Taste the punishment of the burning (Fire)!
variants.variant_full_arabic: لَّقَدۡ سَمِعَ ٱللَّهُ قَوۡلَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ فَقِيرٞ وَنَحۡنُ أَغۡنِيَآءُۘ سَيُكۡتَبُ مَا قَالُواْ وَقَتۡلُهُمُ ٱلۡأَنۢبِيَآءَ بِغَيۡرِ حَقّٖ وَيُقَالُ ذُوقُواْ عَذَابَ ٱلۡحَرِيقِ
variants.variant_full_english: Certainly God has heard the words of those who said, ‘Surely God is poor and we are rich.’ What they have said will be written down, along with their killing the prophets without any right, and it will be said, ‘Taste the punishment of the burning (Fire)!

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Supporters of Hamzah's canonical reading argue that the shift from passive 'sayuktabu' to first-person active 'wa-naqulu' is an instance of rhetorical person-shifting (iltifat) necessitated by the Uthmanic rasm.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari criticizes Hamzah's hybrid reading for adopting the passive beginning ('sayuktabu') from Ibn Mas'ud's codex while being forced by the Uthmanic rasm to abandon Ibn Mas'ud's matching passive continuation ('wa-yuqalu').

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقرأ ذلك بعض قرأة الكوفيين: ( " سيكتب ما قالوا وقتلهم الأنبياء بغير حق " ) بالياء من " سيكتب " وبضمها، ورفع " القتل "، على مذهب ما لم يسم فاعله، اعتبارا بقراءة يذكر أنها من قراءة عبد الله في قوله: " ونقول ذوقوا "، يذكر أنها في قراءة عبد الله: " ويقال". فأغفل قارئ ذلك وجه الصواب فيما قصد إليه من تأويل القراءة التي تنسب إلى عبد الله، وخالف الحجة من قرأة الإسلام.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: And some of the Kufan reciters recited that: ("What they have said will be written down [sayuktabu], and their killing [wa-qatluhumu] the prophets without right") with a ya' in 'sayuktabu' and a dammah on it, and the nominative in 'al-qatl', in the passive voice, by analogy with a recitation mentioned to be from the recitation of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud] in His saying: 'and We shall say, Taste', which is mentioned to be in the recitation of 'Abdullah: 'and it will be said [wa-yuqalu]'. Thus the reciter of that overlooked the correct aspect in what he intended of interpreting the recitation attributed to 'Abdullah.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة عبد الله: " ويقال"
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of 'Abdullah: 'and it will be said [wa-yuqalu]'

variants.short_title: 4:19 — 'Unless They Act Insolently' vs. 'Immorality'
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran allows taking back a wife's dowry only if 'they commit clear immorality,' Ibn Mas'ud's codex read the single verb 'unless they act insolently.'
variants.title: Substitution of 'Unless They Act Insolently' (Illā An Yafḥushna) in 4:19
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 4:19, the Uthmanic text forbids husbands from pressuring wives to forfeit part of their dowries 'إِلَّآ أَن يَأۡتِينَ بِفَٰحِشَةٖ مُّبَيِّنَةٖۚ' ('unless they commit clear immorality.'). Al-Tabari (3816, 8900) records from Miqsam that in the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud this clause read 'إِلَّا أَنْ يَفْحُشْنَ' ('unless they act insolently.')—along with 'وَلَا أَنْ تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ' earlier in the verse—which Miqsam cited to show that verbal insolence and disobedience suffice to make a khul' ransom lawful.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: unless they commit clear immorality
variants.variant_target_english: unless they act insolently
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمۡ أَن تَرِثُواْ ٱلنِّسَآءَ كَرۡهٗاۖ وَلَا تَعۡضُلُوهُنَّ لِتَذۡهَبُواْ بِبَعۡضِ مَآ ءَاتَيۡتُمُوهُنَّ إِلَّآ أَن يَأۡتِينَ بِفَٰحِشَةٖ مُّبَيِّنَةٖۚ وَعَاشِرُوهُنَّ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِۚ فَإِن كَرِهۡتُمُوهُنَّ فَعَسَىٰٓ أَن تَكۡرَهُواْ شَيۡـٔٗا وَيَجۡعَلَ ٱللَّهُ فِيهِ خَيۡرٗا كَثِيرٗا
variants.uthmanic_full_english: You who believe! It is not permitted to you to inherit women against their will. And do not prevent them, so that you may take part of what you have given them, unless they commit clear immorality. Associate with them rightfully. If you dislike them, it may be that you dislike something in which God has placed much good.
variants.variant_full_arabic: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمۡ أَن تَرِثُواْ ٱلنِّسَآءَ كَرۡهٗاۖ وَلَا تَعۡضُلُوهُنَّ لِتَذۡهَبُواْ بِبَعۡضِ مَآ ءَاتَيۡتُمُوهُنَّ إِلَّا أَنْ يَفْحُشْنَۚ وَعَاشِرُوهُنَّ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِۚ فَإِن كَرِهۡتُمُوهُنَّ فَعَسَىٰٓ أَن تَكۡرَهُواْ شَيۡـٔٗا وَيَجۡعَلَ ٱللَّهُ فِيهِ خَيۡرٗا كَثِيرٗا
variants.variant_full_english: You who believe! It is not permitted to you to inherit women against their will. And do not prevent them, so that you may take part of what you have given them, unless they act insolently. Associate with them rightfully. If you dislike them, it may be that you dislike something in which God has placed much good.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Jurists who interpret 'clear immorality' (fāḥisha mubayyina) as encompassing marital defiance and verbal abuse (bhadhā' al-lisān) view Ibn Mas'ud's verb 'yafḥushna' as an explanatory reading supporting that broader legal definition.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari cites Ibn Mas'ud's reading 'إِلَّا أَنْ يَفْحُشْنَ' twice (under both 2:229 and 4:19), where the three-word Uthmanic noun phrase 'commit clear immorality' is replaced by a single intransitive verb meaning to speak or act insolently.

He said:*
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: ( ولا تعضلوهن لتذهبوا ببعض ما آتيتموهن إلا أن يفحشن ) في قراءة ابن مسعود
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: (And do not prevent them, so that you may take part of what you have given them, unless they act immorally) in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud

variants.variant_arabic: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمۡ أَن تَرِثُواْ ٱلنِّسَآءَ كَرۡهٗاۖ وَلَا تَعۡضُلُوهُنَّ لِتَذۡهَبُواْ بِبَعۡضِ مَآ ءَاتَيۡتُمُوهُنَّ إِلَّا أَنْ يَفْحُشْنَۚ وَعَاشِرُوهُنَّ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِۚ فَإِن كَرِهۡتُمُوهُنَّ فَعَسَىٰٓ أَن تَكۡرَهُواْ شَيۡـٔٗا وَيَجۡعَلَ ٱللَّهُ فِيهِ خَيۡرٗا كَثِيرٗا
variants.variant_english: You who believe! It is not permitted to you to inherit women against their will. And do not prevent them, so that you may take part of what you have given them, unless they act insolently. Associate with them rightfully. If you dislike them, it may be that you dislike something in which God has placed much good.
variants.hadith_arabic: 8900 - حدثنا ابن حميد قال، حدثنا حكام قال، حدثنا عنبسة، عن علي بن بذيمة، عن مقسم في قوله: ( ولا تعضلوهن لتذهبوا ببعض ما آتيتموهن إلا أن يفحشن ) في قراءة ابن مسعود. قال: إذا عصتك وآذتك، فقد حل لك أخذ ما أخذتْ منك. (93)
variants.hadith_english: **8900** - *Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hukkam narrated to us, saying: 'Anbasah narrated to us, from 'Ali bin Badhimah, from Miqsam regarding His saying: (And do not prevent them, so that you may take part of what you have given them, unless they act immorally) in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud. He said:*

variants.short_title: 'A Qintar of Gold' & 'Not Lawful to Take' in 4:20
variants.plain_english_hook: When a woman challenged Umar's cap on marriage dowries using 4:20, she and Ibn Masud's recitation read 'a qintar of gold, it is not lawful for you to take any of it'.
variants.title: Surah An-Nisa 4:20 — 'Qintaran min Dhahabin' in Ibn Mas'ud's Recitation
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 4:20, husbands wishing to divorce and remarry are told: 'and you have given one of them a qintar, take (back) none of it' (وَآتَيْتُمْ إِحْدَاهُنَّ قِنْطَارًا فَلَا تَأْخُذُوا مِنْهُ شَيْئًا). Ibn Kathir records in the famous report of Umar bin al-Khattab and the woman who objected to his dowry restriction that the verse was recited with 'a qintar of gold' (قِنْطَارًا مِنْ ذَهَبٍ) and that in Abdullah bin Mas'ud's recitation it read: 'it is not lawful for you to take (back) any of it' (فَلَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَأْخُذُوا مِنْهُ شَيْئًا).
variants.uthmanic_target_english: a qinṭr, take (back) none of it
variants.variant_target_arabic: قِنطَارٗا مِّن ذَهَبٍ فَلَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمۡ أَن تَأۡخُذُواْ مِنۡهُ شَيۡـًٔا
variants.variant_target_english: a qintar of gold, then it is not lawful for you to take (back) any of it
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: وَإِنۡ أَرَدتُّمُ ٱسۡتِبۡدَالَ زَوۡجٖ مَّكَانَ زَوۡجٖ وَءَاتَيۡتُمۡ إِحۡدَىٰهُنَّ قِنطَارٗا فَلَا تَأۡخُذُواْ مِنۡهُ شَيۡـًٔاۚ أَتَأۡخُذُونَهُۥ بُهۡتَٰنٗا وَإِثۡمٗا مُّبِينٗا
variants.uthmanic_full_english: And if you wish to exchange a wife for (another) wife, and you have given one of them a qinṭr, take (back) none of it. Would you take it (back by) slander and clear sin?
variants.variant_full_arabic: وَإِنۡ أَرَدتُّمُ ٱسۡتِبۡدَالَ زَوۡجٖ مَّكَانَ زَوۡجٖ وَءَاتَيۡتُمۡ إِحۡدَىٰهُنَّ قِنطَارٗا مِّن ذَهَبٍ فَلَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمۡ أَن تَأۡخُذُواْ مِنۡهُ شَيۡـًٔاۚ أَتَأۡخُذُونَهُۥ بُهۡتَٰنٗا وَإِثۡمٗا مُّبِينٗا
variants.variant_full_english: And if you wish to exchange a wife for (another) wife, and you have given one of them a qintar of gold, then it is not lawful for you to take (back) any of it. Would you take it (back by) slander and clear sin?

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical scholars treat 'min dhahabin' (of gold) and 'fa-la yahillu lakum an' (it is not lawful for you to) as explanatory glosses clarifying the value of a qintar and the prohibitive force of 'fa-la ta'khudhu'.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: The narration preserved by Ibn Kathir links both phrase expansions directly to the public legal exchange with Caliph Umar and explicitly attests 'fa-la yahillu lakum an ta'khudhu minhu shay'an' as the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: قال عمر بن الخطاب : لا تغالوا في مهور النساء . فقالت امرأة : ليس ذلك لك يا عمر ، إن الله تعالى يقول : " وآتيتم إحداهن قنطارا من ذهب " . قال : وكذلك هي في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود : " فلا يحل لكم أن تأخذوا منه شيئا " فقال عمر : إن امرأة خاصمت عمر فخصمته .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 'Umar bin Al-Khattab said: 'Do not be excessive in the dowries of women.' A woman said: 'You do not have that right, O 'Umar, for Allah the Exalted says: "and you have given one of them a Qintar of gold."' He (the narrator) said: 'And likewise it is in the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud: "so it is not lawful for you to take any of it."' Thereupon 'Umar said: 'Indeed, a woman disputed with 'Umar and defeated him in argument.'
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود : " فلا يحل لكم أن تأخذوا منه شيئا "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud: "so it is not lawful for you to take any of it."

variants.short_title: Grammatical Case Shift in 4:162 (Al-Muqimuna)
variants.plain_english_hook: Surah 4:162 shifts mid-sentence from nominative plural nouns to the accusative 'wal-muqimina'; Aisha called it a scribal error, and Ibn Masud's codex read the nominative 'wal-muqimuna'.
variants.title: Surah An-Nisa 4:162 — Nominative 'Wal-Muqimuna' in Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 4:162, 'and the ones who observe the prayer' (وَالْمُقِيمِينَ الصَّلَاةَ) is written in the accusative/oblique case with a ya' (-ina), surrounded before and after by nominative plurals ending in waw-nun (الرَّاسِخُونَ, وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ, وَالْمُؤْتُونَ). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record that in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud it is written in the nominative with a waw (وَالْمُقِيمُونَ الصَّلَاةَ), and al-Tabari transmits the famous report of Urwah asking Aisha about 4:162, 5:69, and 20:63, to which she replied: 'O son of my sister, this is the work of the scribe; they erred in the writing.'
variants.uthmanic_target_english: And the ones who observe the prayer
variants.variant_target_english: And the ones [nominative: al-muqimuna] who observe the prayer
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: لَّـٰكِنِ ٱلرَّـٰسِخُونَ فِي ٱلۡعِلۡمِ مِنۡهُمۡ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡكَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ مِن قَبۡلِكَۚ وَٱلۡمُقِيمِينَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَۚ وَٱلۡمُؤۡتُونَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ أُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ سَنُؤۡتِيهِمۡ أَجۡرًا عَظِيمًا
variants.uthmanic_full_english: But the ones who are firm in knowledge among them – and the believers – believe in what has been sent down to you, and what has been sent down before you. And the ones who observe the prayer, and who give the alms, and who believe in God and the Last Day, those – We shall give them a great reward.
variants.variant_full_arabic: لَّـٰكِنِ ٱلرَّـٰسِخُونَ فِي ٱلۡعِلۡمِ مِنۡهُمۡ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡكَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ مِن قَبۡلِكَۚ وَٱلۡمُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَۚ وَٱلۡمُؤۡتُونَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ أُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ سَنُؤۡتِيهِمۡ أَجۡرًا عَظِيمًا
variants.variant_full_english: But the ones who are firm in knowledge among them – and the believers – believe in what has been sent down to you, and what has been sent down before you. And the ones [nominative: al-muqimuna] who observe the prayer, and who give the alms, and who believe in God and the Last Day, those – We shall give them a great reward.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical grammarians and commentators explain the Uthmanic accusative 'wal-muqimina' either as an accusative of praise (mansub 'ala al-madh) or as conjoined to the genitive pronoun 'ka' ('what was sent down to you'), arguing that Ubayy bin Ka'b's codex agreed with the Uthmanic rasm.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari preserves two direct chains (via Abu Mu'awiyah and Yahya bin Sa'id from Hisham bin 'Urwah from his father) in which Aisha attributes the case anomaly in 4:162 to scribal error, while Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf preserved the regular nominative consonantal form 'wal-muqimuna' (with waw).

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 10835- حدثنا الحسين بن يحيى قال، أخبرنا الحسين بن الأسود قال، حدثنا يحيى بن آدم، عن أبي بكر بن عياش، عن هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه قال: سألت عائشة عن اللحن في القرآن، عن قوله: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَالَّذِينَ هَادُوا وَالصَّابِئُونَ) [سورة المائدة: 69]، وعن قوله: (وَالْمُقِيمِينَ الصَّلاةَ وَالْمُؤْتُونَ الزَّكَاةَ)، وعن قوله: (إِنْ هَذَانِ لَسَاحِرَانِ) [سورة طه: 63]، فقالت: يا ابن أختي، هذا عمل الكاتب، أخطئوا في الكتاب. وذكر أن ذلك في قراءة ابن مسعود: (وَالْمُقِيمُونَ الصَّلاةَ).
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 10835 - Al-Husayn bin Yahya narrated to us... from Hisham bin 'Urwah, from his father, who said: I asked 'A'ishah about the grammatical anomaly (lahn) in the Qur'an, concerning His saying: {Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews and the Sabians [al-Sabi'una]} [5:69], and concerning His saying: {And the ones who observe the prayer [wa-al-muqimina al-salah] and who give the alms [wa-al-mu'tuna al-zakah]}, and concerning His saying: {Indeed, these two [in hadhani] are magicians} [20:63], and she said: O son of my sister, this is the work of the scribe, they erred in the writing. And it is mentioned that it is in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: 'and the ones who observe the prayer' (wa-al-muqimuna al-salah).
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة ابن مسعود: (وَالْمُقِيمُونَ الصَّلاةَ)
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: 'and the ones who observe the prayer' (wa-al-muqimuna al-salah)

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقوله : ( والمقيمين الصلاة ) هكذا هو في جميع المصاحف الأئمة ، وكذا هو في مصحف أبي بن كعب . وذكر ابن جرير أنها في مصحف ابن مسعود : " والمقيمون الصلاة " ، قال : والصحيح قراءة الجميع . ثم رد على من زعم أن ذلك من غلط الكتاب ثم ذكر اختلاف الناس فقال بعضهم : هو منصوب على المدح .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: *(Wal-Muqimina As-Salah)* is written as such in all the leading copies of the Qur'an *(Masahif Al-A'immah)*, and similarly in the Mushaf of Ubayy bin Ka'b. Ibn Jarir mentioned that in the Mushaf of Ibn Mas'ud it is: "and the ones who observe the prayer *(Wal-Muqimuna As-Salah)*." He said: "And the correct recitation is that of the majority." Then he refuted those who claimed that this was a mistake by the scribes.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في مصحف ابن مسعود : " والمقيمون الصلاة "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the Mushaf of Ibn Mas'ud it is: "and the ones who observe the prayer *(Wal-Muqimuna As-Salah)*."

variants.short_title: 5:38 — Cut Off the Thief's 'Right Hands' vs. 'Hands'
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran commands to 'cut off their hands' for theft, Abdullah bin Mas'ud's codex explicitly specified 'cut off their right hands.'
variants.title: Substitution of 'Their Right Hands' (Aymānahumā) for 'Their Hands' in 5:38
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 5:38, the Uthmanic text prescribes the punishment for theft as 'فَٱقۡطَعُوٓاْ أَيۡدِيَهُمَا' ('cut off their hands'). Both al-Tabari (11907–11910) and Ibn Kathir record that Abdullah bin Mas'ud recited 'فَاقْطَعُوا أَيْمَانَهُمَا' ('cut off their right hands'), which Ibn Kathir classifies as an anomalous (shādhdh) recitation whose legal ruling is nevertheless unanimously followed by Islamic jurists.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: cut off their hands
variants.variant_target_english: cut off their right hands
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: وَٱلسَّارِقُ وَٱلسَّارِقَةُ فَٱقۡطَعُوٓاْ أَيۡدِيَهُمَا جَزَآءَۢ بِمَا كَسَبَا نَكَٰلٗا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٞ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: (As for) the male thief and the female thief: cut off their hands as a penalty for what they have done – a punishment from God. God is mighty, wise.
variants.variant_full_arabic: وَٱلسَّارِقُ وَٱلسَّارِقَةُ فَاقْطَعُوا أَيْمَانَهُمَا جَزَآءَۢ بِمَا كَسَبَا نَكَٰلٗا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٞ
variants.variant_full_english: (As for) the male thief and the female thief: cut off their right hands as a penalty for what they have done – a punishment from God. God is mighty, wise.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Ibn Kathir and Sunni legal theorists state that Ibn Mas'ud's wording is a non-canonical (shādhdh) explanatory reading, arguing that the restriction of amputation to the right hand is established by Prophetic practice rather than this variant text.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari records multiple Kufan transmissions from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and al-Sha'bi citing 'in our recitation / in the recitation of Abdullah: cut off their right hands' as a direct textual reading of the verse.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 11910 - حدثنا ابن وكيع قال، حدثنا أبي، عن سفيان، عن جابر، عن عامر قال: في قراءة عبد الله: ( والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا أيمانهما ).
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: **11910** - *Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from 'Amir, who said:* In the recitation of 'Abdullah: *(The male thief and the female thief, so cut off their right hands)*.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة عبد الله: ( والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا أيمانهما )
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: In the recitation of 'Abdullah: *(The male thief and the female thief, so cut off their right hands)*

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: يقول تعالى حاكما وآمرا بقطع يد السارق والسارقة ، وروى الثوري عن جابر بن يزيد الجعفي عن عامر بن شراحيل الشعبي أن ابن مسعود كان يقرؤها : " والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا أيمانهما " . وهذه قراءة شاذة ، وإن كان الحكم عند جميع العلماء موافقا لها ، لا بها ، بل هو مستفاد من دليل آخر . وقد كان القطع معمولا به في الجاهلية ، فقرر في الإسلام وزيدت شروط أخر ، كما سنذكره إن شاء الله تعالى ، كما كانت القسامة والدية والقراض وغير ذلك من الأشياء التي ورد الشرع بتقريرها على ما كانت عليه ، وزيادات هي من تمام المصالح . ويقال : إن أول من قطع الأيدي في الجاهلية قريش قطعوا رجلا يقال له : " دويك " مولى لبني مليح بن عمرو من خزاعة كان قد سرق كنز الكعبة ، ويقال : سرقه قوم فوضعوه عنده .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Allah commands and decrees that the hand of the thief, male or female be cut off. Ath-Thawri reported from Jabir bin Yazid Al-Ju'fi from 'Amir bin Sharahil Ash-Sha'bi that Ibn Mas'ud used to recite it: "And the male thief and the female thief, cut off their right hands." This is a *Shaadh* (anomalous) recitation, although the ruling among all scholars is in agreement with it (cutting the right hand), not because of this recitation, but derived from another evidence.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: أن ابن مسعود كان يقرؤها : " والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا أيمانهما "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: Ibn Mas'ud used to recite it: "And the male thief and the female thief, cut off their right hands."

variants.variant_arabic: وَٱلسَّارِقُ وَٱلسَّارِقَةُ فَاقْطَعُوا أَيْمَانَهُمَا جَزَآءَۢ بِمَا كَسَبَا نَكَٰلٗا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٞ
variants.variant_english: (As for) the male thief and the female thief: cut off their right hands as a penalty for what they have done – a punishment from God. God is mighty, wise.

variants.short_title: 'Those Who Commit Shirk' vs 'The Disbelievers' (5:57)
variants.plain_english_hook: In 5:57, the standard Quran pairs 'those given the Book' with 'the disbelievers' (wal-kuffar); Ibn Masud's reading had 'and from those who associate partners with God'.
variants.title: Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:57 — 'Wa-mina Alladhina Ashraku' vs Uthmanic 'Wal-Kuffara'
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 5:57, believers are forbidden to take mocking allies 'from those who were given the Book before you, or (from) the disbelievers [وَالْكُفَّارَ]', where reciters differed on whether وَالْكُفَّارَ is accusative or genitive since the preposition مِنْ ('from') is not repeated. Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record that Abdullah bin Mas'ud recited 'and from those who associate partners with God' (وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا), while Ubayy bin Ka'b recited 'and from the disbelievers' (وَمِنَ الْكُفَّارِ), both repeating the preposition مِنْ.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: or (from) the disbelievers
variants.variant_target_english: or from those who associate (partners with God)
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَتَّخِذُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ دِينَكُمۡ هُزُوٗا وَلَعِبٗا مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ وَٱلۡكُفَّارَ أَوۡلِيَآءَۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: You who believe! Do not take those who take your religion in mockery and jest as allies, (either) from those who were given the Book before you, or (from) the disbelievers. Guard (yourselves) against God, if you are believers.
variants.variant_full_arabic: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَتَّخِذُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ دِينَكُمۡ هُزُوٗا وَلَعِبٗا مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ وَمِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَشۡرَكُواْ أَوۡلِيَآءَۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
variants.variant_full_english: You who believe! Do not take those who take your religion in mockery and jest as allies, (either) from those who were given the Book before you, or from those who associate (partners with God). Guard (yourselves) against God, if you are believers.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir cite the recitations of Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy to show that 'al-kuffar' in 5:57 specifically denotes the Arab polytheists (al-mushrikun) as distinct from the People of the Book.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Both Ibn Mas'ud's wording ('wa-mina alladhina ashraku') and Ubayy's wording ('wa-mina al-kuffari') supply the repeated preposition 'min' whose absence in the Uthmanic rasm caused a canonical grammatical dispute between the genitive and accusative readings of 'wal-kuffar'.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 12217 - حدثني به أحمد بن يوسف قال، حدثنا القاسم بن سلام قال، حدثنا حجاج، عن هارون، عن ابن مسعود= يقرأ: ( مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا ). وكذلك ذلك في قراءة أبيّ بن كعب فيما بلغنا: ( من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم ومن الكفار أولياء ).
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 12217 - Ahmad bin Yusuf narrated to me, saying: al-Qasim bin Sallam narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Harun, from Ibn Mas'ud, used to recite: {from those who were given the Book before you, and from those who commit shirk [polytheism]}. And likewise is that [found] in the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b, according to what has reached us: {from those who were given the Book before you, and from the disbelievers, as allies}.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: عن ابن مسعود= يقرأ: ( مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا )
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: Ibn Mas'ud, used to recite: {from those who were given the Book before you, and from those who commit shirk [polytheism]}

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: والمراد بالكفار ههنا المشركون ، وكذا وقع في قراءة ابن مسعود فيها ، رواه ابن جرير .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: The meaning here of "the disbelievers" is the idolaters. Similarly, Ibn Jarir recorded that in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud [in place of "the disbelievers"] he recited it: "and those who commit *Shirk*."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: والمراد بالكفار ههنا المشركون ، وكذا وقع في قراءة ابن مسعود فيها ، رواه ابن جرير
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud [in place of "the disbelievers"] he recited it: "and those who commit *Shirk*."
