variants.short_title: Oath Atonement: 'Three Consecutive Days'
variants.plain_english_hook: The standard Quran requires fasting 'three days' to break an oath, leaving jurists divided on whether they must be back-to-back; Ibn Masud and Ubayy's codices explicitly added 'consecutive'.
variants.title: Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:89 — Addition of 'Mutatabi'at' (Consecutive) in Oath Expiation
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 5:89, the expiation for a broken oath when unable to feed or clothe the poor is 'a fast for three days' (فَصِيَامُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record via multiple authentic chains that the codices and recitations of Abdullah bin Mas'ud and Ubayy bin Ka'b read 'a fast for three consecutive days' (فَصِيَامُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ مُتَتَابِعَاتٍ), a variant that directly shaped Hanafi and Hanbali law requiring uninterrupted fasting.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: a fast for three days
variants.variant_target_english: a fast for three consecutive days
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: لَا يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِٱللَّغۡوِ فِيٓ أَيۡمَٰنِكُمۡ وَلَٰكِن يُؤَاخِذُكُم بِمَا عَقَّدتُّمُ ٱلۡأَيۡمَٰنَۖ فَكَفَّـٰرَتُهُۥٓ إِطۡعَامُ عَشَرَةِ مَسَٰكِينَ مِنۡ أَوۡسَطِ مَا تُطۡعِمُونَ أَهۡلِيكُمۡ أَوۡ كِسۡوَتُهُمۡ أَوۡ تَحۡرِيرُ رَقَبَةٖۖ فَمَن لَّمۡ يَجِدۡ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَٰثَةِ أَيَّامٖۚ ذَٰلِكَ كَفَّـٰرَةُ أَيۡمَٰنِكُمۡ إِذَا حَلَفۡتُمۡۚ وَٱحۡفَظُوٓاْ أَيۡمَٰنَكُمۡۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: God will not take you to task for a slip in your oaths, but He will take you to task for what you have pledged by oath. Atonement for it is the feeding of ten poor persons with the average (amount of food) which you feed your households, or clothing them, or the setting free of a slave. Whoever does not find (the means to do that), (the penalty is) a fast for three days. That is the atonement for your oaths when you have sworn (them, and broken them). But guard your oaths! In this way God makes clear to you His signs, so that you may be thankful.
variants.variant_full_arabic: لَا يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِٱللَّغۡوِ فِيٓ أَيۡمَٰنِكُمۡ وَلَٰكِن يُؤَاخِذُكُم بِمَا عَقَّدتُّمُ ٱلۡأَيۡمَٰنَۖ فَكَفَّـٰرَتُهُۥٓ إِطۡعَامُ عَشَرَةِ مَسَٰكِينَ مِنۡ أَوۡسَطِ مَا تُطۡعِمُونَ أَهۡلِيكُمۡ أَوۡ كِسۡوَتُهُمۡ أَوۡ تَحۡرِيرُ رَقَبَةٖۖ فَمَن لَّمۡ يَجِدۡ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَٰثَةِ أَيَّامٖ مُّتَتَٰبِعَٰتٍۚ ذَٰلِكَ كَفَّـٰرَةُ أَيۡمَٰنِكُمۡ إِذَا حَلَفۡتُمۡۚ وَٱحۡفَظُوٓاْ أَيۡمَٰنَكُمۡۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
variants.variant_full_english: God will not take you to task for a slip in your oaths, but He will take you to task for what you have pledged by oath. Atonement for it is the feeding of ten poor persons with the average (amount of food) which you feed your households, or clothing them, or the setting free of a slave. Whoever does not find (the means to do that), (the penalty is) a fast for three consecutive days. That is the atonement for your oaths when you have sworn (them, and broken them). But guard your oaths! In this way God makes clear to you His signs, so that you may be thankful.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical jurists and commentators classify the word 'mutatabi'at' (consecutive) either as an explanatory gloss (qira'a tafsiriyya) inserted by Companions or as a recitation whose wording was abrogated while its legal ruling remained debated.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari transmits seven independent chains to Ubayy bin Ka'b, Abdullah bin Mas'ud, and his Kufan disciples (including Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and al-A'mash) affirming 'mutatabi'at' as their established recitation, while explicitly rejecting its Quranic status solely because it is absent from the Uthmanic manuscripts.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 9750 - حدثنا عبد الأعلى بن واصل الأسدي، قال: ثنا عبيد الله بن موسى، عن أبي جعفر الرازي، عن الربيع بن أنس، عن أبي العالية، عن أبي بن كعب، أنه كان يقرأ: "فصيام ثلاثة أيام متتابعات". 9751 - حدثنا ابن وكيع، قال: ثنا يزيد بن هارون، عن قزعة بن سويد، عن سيف بن سليمان، عن مجاهد، قال: في قراءة عبد الله: "فصيام ثلاثة أيام متتابعات". فأما ما روي عن أبي وابن مسعود من قراءتهما "فصيام ثلاثة أيام متتابعات" فذلك خلاف ما في مصاحفنا، وغير جائز لنا أن نشهد بشيء ليس في مصاحفنا من الكلام أنه من كتاب الله.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 9750 - 'Abd al-A'la b. Wasil al-Asadi narrated to us... from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy b. Ka'b, that he used to read: 'a fast for three consecutive days'. 9751 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us... from Mujahid, he said: In the reading of 'Abd Allah: 'a fast for three consecutive days'. As for what was narrated from Ubayy and Ibn Mas'ud regarding their reading 'a fast for three consecutive days', that is contrary to what is in our manuscripts of the Qur'an.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة عبد الله: "فصيام ثلاثة أيام متتابعات"
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: In the reading of 'Abd Allah: 'a fast for three consecutive days'

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: قال أبو جعفر الرازي ، عن الربيع ، عن أبي العالية ، عن أبي بن كعب أنه كان يقرؤها : " فصيام ثلاثة أيام متتابعات " . وحكاها مجاهد والشعبي وأبو إسحاق ، عن عبد الله بن مسعود . وقال إبراهيم : في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود : " فصيام ثلاثة أيام متتابعات " . وقال الأعمش : كان أصحاب ابن مسعود يقرءونها كذلك .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Abu Ja'far Ar-Razi recorded from Ar-Rabi', from Abu Al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy bin Ka'b that he used to read it as: 'Then he should fast three consecutive days.' Mujahid, Ash-Sha'bi, and Abu Ishaq narrated it from 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud. Ibrahim said: 'In the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud: "Then he should fast three consecutive days."' Al-A'mash said: 'The companions of Ibn Mas'ud used to read it like that.'
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود : " فصيام ثلاثة أيام متتابعات "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: In the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud: "Then he should fast three consecutive days."

variants.short_title: 'He Has Studied' (Darasa) vs 'You Have Studied' (6:105)
variants.plain_english_hook: In 6:105, the standard Quran has 'so that they will say, You have studied' (darasta, with a final t); the codices of Ubayy and Ibn Masud read 'He has studied' (darasa).
variants.title: Surah Al-An'am 6:105 — 'Wa-li-Yaqulu Darasa' in Ubayy and Ibn Mas'ud's Codices
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 6:105, the consonantal rasm دَرَسْتَ (with a final ta') is read by the majority as 'You have studied' (darasta), by Ibn Kathir/Abu 'Amr as 'You have studied with others' (darasta, adding an alif), and by Ibn 'Amir as 'They have become old/erased' (darasat). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record via Abu 'Ubayd al-Qasim bin Sallam and Ma'mar from Qatadah that in the codex/harf of Ubayy bin Ka'b and Abdullah bin Mas'ud the word was written without the final ta': 'so that they will say, He has studied' (وَلِيَقُولُوا دَرَسَ).
variants.uthmanic_target_english: so that they will say, ‘You have studied,’
variants.variant_target_english: so that they will say, ‘He has studied,’
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: وَكَذَٰلِكَ نُصَرِّفُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ وَلِيَقُولُواْ دَرَسۡتَ وَلِنُبَيِّنَهُۥ لِقَوۡمٖ يَعۡلَمُونَ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: In this way We vary the signs, so that they will say, ‘You have studied,’ and that We may make it clear to a people who know.

variants.variant_full_english: In this way We vary the signs, so that they will say, ‘He has studied,’ and that We may make it clear to a people who know.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari remarks that third-person 'darasa' and second-person 'darasta' both convey the disbelievers' allegation that the Prophet studied previous texts, while preferring 'darasta' because it conforms to the Uthmanic consonantal script.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: The absence of the final consonant ta' in 'darasa' is attested by both Qatadah and Abu 'Ubayd for the codices (harf) of both Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy bin Ka'b, representing a genuine consonantal divergence from the Uthmanic rasm.

variants.short_title: Missing Object Pronoun 'Annahum' in 8:59
variants.plain_english_hook: Al-Tabari criticizes the standard Hafs reading of 8:59 as grammatically incomplete unless 'annahum' ('that they') is present—as it was in Abdullah bin Masud's codex.
variants.title: Surah Al-Anfal 8:59 — 'Annahum Sabaqu' in Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf vs Uthmanic 'Sabaqu'
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 8:59, the Kufan and Medinan reading (including Hafs) is وَلَا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا سَبَقُوا إِنَّهُمْ لَا يُعْجِزُونَ ('Do not let those who disbelieve think they have gotten away. Surely they will not escape'). Al-Tabari argues that reading third-person 'yahsabanna' with 'innahum' (kasra) is grammatically defective in Arabic because the verb 'yahsabu' requires two accusative objects, and explains that those reciters were influenced by the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud, which explicitly included the word أَنَّهُمْ ('that they'): وَلَا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنَّهُمْ سَبَقُوا إِنَّهُمْ لَا يُعْجِزُونَ.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: disbelieve think they have gotten away

variants.uthmanic_full_english: Do not let those who disbelieve think they have gotten away. Surely they will not escape.

variants.variant_full_english: Do not let those who disbelieve think that they have gotten away. Surely they will not escape.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Grammarians defending the Hafs reading argue either that 'annahum' is implicitly elided (mudmar) before 'sabaqu' or that 'sabaqu' functions in the sense of a participial second object ('sabiqin').
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari explicitly declares the Hafs/Kufan reading 'non-praiseworthy' (ghayr mahmudah) and distant from eloquent Arabic speech unless 'annahum' is present in the text as it was in Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقرأ ذلك بعض قرأة أهل المدينة والكوفة: " ولا يحسبن الذين كفروا "، بالياء في " يحسبن "، وكسر الألف من " إنهم ". وهي قراءة غير محمودة، لعلتين: إحداهما، خروجها عن قراءة القرأة وشذوذها عنها; والأخرى، بعدها عن الفصيح من كلام العرب. وأحسب أن الذي دعاه إلى ذلك، الاعتبار بقراءة عبد الله. وذلك أنه فيما ذكر في مصحف عبد الله: " ولا يحسبن الذين كفروا أنهم سبقوا إنهم لا يعجزون "، وهذا فصيح صحيح، إذا أدخلت " أنهم " في الكلام, لأن " يحسبن " عاملة في " أنهم ", وإذا لم يكن في الكلام " أنهم " كانت خالية من اسم تعمل فيه.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: And some of the reciters of Al-Madinah and Al-Kufah recited it: "Wa la yahsabanna alladhina kafaru," with a Ya' in "yahsabanna", and a Kasrah on the Alif of "innahum". And it is a non-praiseworthy recitation, for two reasons: one of them is its departure from the recitation of the reciters and its anomaly from it; and the other: its distance from the eloquent speech of the Arabs... And I suppose that what called him to that was the consideration of the recitation of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]. And that is because it is as was mentioned in the Mushaf of 'Abdullah: "Do not let those who disbelieve think that they [annahum] have gotten away; surely they will not escape" (Wa la yahsabanna alladhina kafaru annahum sabaqu innahum la yu'jizun), and this is eloquent and sound if "annahum" is inserted into the speech, because "yahsabanna" governs "annahum", and if "annahum" is not in the speech, it is devoid of a noun in which to operate.

variants.short_title: 11:81 — Omitting 'Let None of You Turn Around'
variants.plain_english_hook: In the angels' command to Lot, Ibn Mas'ud's codex read 'So journey with your family in a part of the night, except your wife,' omitting 'and let none of you turn around.'
variants.title: Omission of 'And Let None of You Turn Around' Before 'Except Your Wife' in 11:81
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 11:81, the Uthmanic text reads 'فَأَسۡرِ بِأَهۡلِكَ بِقِطۡعٖ مِّنَ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَلَا يَلۡتَفِتۡ مِنكُمۡ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا ٱمۡرَأَتَكَۖ' ('So journey with your family in a part of the night, and let none of you turn around, except your wife,'), creating a famous grammatical dispute over whether 'except your wife' modifies 'your family' or 'let none of you turn around.' Al-Tabari (18423) and Ibn Kathir record that in the reading (ḥarf) of Abdullah bin Mas'ud it read 'فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ إِلَّا امْرَأَتَكَ' ('So journey with your family in a part of the night, except your wife,'), omitting the intervening clause.
variants.uthmanic_target_arabic: فَأَسۡرِ بِأَهۡلِكَ بِقِطۡعٖ مِّنَ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَلَا يَلۡتَفِتۡ مِنكُمۡ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا ٱمۡرَأَتَكَ
variants.uthmanic_target_english: So journey with your family in a part of the night, and let none of you turn around, except your wife
variants.variant_target_arabic: فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ إِلَّا امْرَأَتَكَ
variants.variant_target_english: So journey with your family in a part of the night, except your wife
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: قَالُواْ يَٰلُوطُ إِنَّا رُسُلُ رَبِّكَ لَن يَصِلُوٓاْ إِلَيۡكَۖ فَأَسۡرِ بِأَهۡلِكَ بِقِطۡعٖ مِّنَ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَلَا يَلۡتَفِتۡ مِنكُمۡ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا ٱمۡرَأَتَكَۖ إِنَّهُۥ مُصِيبُهَا مَآ أَصَابَهُمۡۚ إِنَّ مَوۡعِدَهُمُ ٱلصُّبۡحُۚ أَلَيۡسَ ٱلصُّبۡحُ بِقَرِيبٖ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: They said, ‘Lot! Surely we are messengers of your Lord. They will not reach you. So journey with your family in a part of the night, and let none of you turn around, except your wife, (for) surely what is about to smite them is going to smite her. Surely their appointment is the morning. Is the morning not near?’

So journey with your family in a part of the night, except your wife, (for) surely what is about to smite them is going to smite her. Surely their appointment is the morning. Is the morning not near?’

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Grammarians and exegetes cite Ibn Mas'ud's reading as an interpretive reordering or abridged citation demonstrating why the majority of canonical readers place 'your wife' (imra'ataka) in the accusative case as an exception to 'your family.'
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari (18423) transmits this directly via Abu Ubayd al-Qasim bin Sallam as the reading (ḥarf) of Ibn Mas'ud, resolving the syntactic ambiguity in the Uthmanic text where the prohibition against turning around separates 'your family' from 'except your wife.'

variants.short_title: 'Pressing Grapes' vs 'Pressing Wine' in 12:36
variants.plain_english_hook: In Joseph's prison, the cupbearer says 'I saw myself pressing wine' in the standard Quran; in Abdullah bin Masud's recitation, he said 'pressing grapes'.
variants.title: Surah Yusuf 12:36 — 'A'siru 'Inaban' (Pressing Grapes) vs 'Khamran' (Wine)
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 12:36, Pharaoh's cupbearer tells Joseph in prison, 'Surely I saw myself (in a dream) pressing wine [خَمْرًا].' Because one physically presses grapes rather than finished wine, both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record via multiple chains (through Muhammad bin al-Hanafiyyah and al-A'mash from Zayd bin Wahb) that Abdullah bin Mas'ud recited 'Surely I saw myself pressing grapes [عِنَبًا]'.

variants.variant_target_english: pressing grapes
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: وَدَخَلَ مَعَهُ ٱلسِّجۡنَ فَتَيَانِۖ قَالَ أَحَدُهُمَآ إِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰنِيٓ أَعۡصِرُ خَمۡرٗاۖ وَقَالَ ٱلۡأٓخَرُ إِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰنِيٓ أَحۡمِلُ فَوۡقَ رَأۡسِي خُبۡزٗا تَأۡكُلُ ٱلطَّيۡرُ مِنۡهُۖ نَبِّئۡنَا بِتَأۡوِيلِهِۦٓۖ إِنَّا نَرَىٰكَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ

Inform us about its interpretation. Surely we see you are one of the doers of good.’

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical commentators explain the Uthmanic word 'khamran' (wine) either as rhetorical metonymy (calling raw grapes by what they will eventually become) or as a dialectal usage from Oman where grapes were reportedly called khamr.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Ibn Kathir cites a direct Kufan chain (Sharīk from al-A'mash from Zayd bin Wahb from Ibn Mas'ud) alongside al-Tabari's transmission proving that Ibn Mas'ud's codex read the literal noun 'inaban' (grapes) in place of 'khamran' (wine).

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وعني بقوله: (أعصر خمرا) ، أي: إني أرى في نومي أني أعصر عنبا . وكذلك ذلك في قراءة ابن مسعود فيما ذكر عنه . 19273 - حدثنا ابن وكيع , قال: حدثنا أبي , عن أبي سلمة الصائغ , عن إبراهيم بن بشير الأنصاري , عن محمد بن الحنفية قال في قراءة ابن مسعود: " إني أراني أعصر عنبا".
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: And He meant by His saying: {pressing wine (khamr)}, meaning: "I see in my sleep that I am pressing grapes ('inab)." And so it is in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud based on what was mentioned about him. 19273 — Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, from Abu Salamah Al-Sa'igh, from Ibrahim bin Bashir Al-Ansari, from Muhammad bin Al-Hanafiyyah who said [that it is] in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: "Surely I saw myself pressing grapes ('inab)."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة ابن مسعود: " إني أراني أعصر عنبا"
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: "Surely I saw myself pressing grapes ('inab)."

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: فرأى الساقي أنه يعصر خمرا - يعني عنبا - وكذلك هي في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود : " إني أراني أعصر عنبا " . ورواه ابن أبي حاتم ، عن أحمد بن سنان ، عن يزيد بن هارون ، عن شريك ، عن الأعمش ، عن زيد بن وهب ، عن ابن مسعود : أنه قرأها : " أعصر عنبا " .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: The cupbearer saw that he was pressing wine - meaning grapes - and likewise it is in the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud: "Surely I saw myself pressing grapes." Ibn Abi Hatim recorded it from Ahmad bin Sinan, from Yazid bin Harun, from Sharik, from Al-A'mash, from Zayd bin Wahb, from Ibn Mas'ud, that he recited it: "pressing grapes."

variants.short_title: 'Above Every Knower' ('Alim vs Dhi 'Ilm) in 12:76
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran concludes 12:76 with 'and above everyone who has knowledge [dhi 'ilmin] is the One who knows', Ibn Masud's reading had 'above every knower ['alimin]'.
variants.title: Surah Yusuf 12:76 — 'Wa-Fawqa Kulli 'Alimin 'Alim' in Ibn Mas'ud's Recitation
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 12:76, the verse concludes وَفَوْقَ كُلِّ ذِي عِلْمٍ عَلِيمٌ ('and above everyone who has knowledge is the One who knows'). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record via Qatadah that in the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud it read وَفَوْقَ كُلِّ عَالِمٍ عَلِيمٌ ('and above every knower is the One who knows'), replacing the two-word construct ذِي عِلْمٍ with the single active participle عَالِمٍ.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: and above everyone who has knowledge is the One who knows
variants.variant_target_english: and above every knower is the One who knows
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: فَبَدَأَ بِأَوۡعِيَتِهِمۡ قَبۡلَ وِعَآءِ أَخِيهِ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَخۡرَجَهَا مِن وِعَآءِ أَخِيهِۚ كَذَٰلِكَ كِدۡنَا لِيُوسُفَۖ مَا كَانَ لِيَأۡخُذَ أَخَاهُ فِي دِينِ ٱلۡمَلِكِ إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُۚ نَرۡفَعُ دَرَجَٰتٖ مَّن نَّشَآءُۗ وَفَوۡقَ كُلِّ ذِي عِلۡمٍ عَلِيمٞ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: So he began with their packs before (searching) his brother’s pack, (and) then he brought it out of his brother’s pack. In this way We plotted for (the sake of) Joseph. He was not one to take his brother, in (accord with) the religion of the king, unless God had (so) pleased. We raise in rank whomever We please, and above everyone who has knowledge is the One who knows.
variants.variant_full_arabic: فَبَدَأَ بِأَوۡعِيَتِهِمۡ قَبۡلَ وِعَآءِ أَخِيهِ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَخۡرَجَهَا مِن وِعَآءِ أَخِيهِۚ كَذَٰلِكَ كِدۡنَا لِيُوسُفَۖ مَا كَانَ لِيَأۡخُذَ أَخَاهُ فِي دِينِ ٱلۡمَلِكِ إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُۚ نَرۡفَعُ دَرَجَٰتٖ مَّن نَّشَآءُۗ وَفَوۡقَ كُلِّ عَالِمٍ عَلِيمٞ

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical commentators view 'kulli 'alimin' (every knower) and 'kulli dhi 'ilmin' (everyone possessing knowledge) as synonymous expressions from the same root.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: While semantically close, the replacement of the two-word Uthmanic construct 'dhi 'ilmin' with the single participle ''alimin' is an unmistakable consonantal difference attested in both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir.

variants.short_title: 'Load Up Our Mounts' vs 'Fill Up the Measure' (12:88)
variants.plain_english_hook: When Joseph's brothers bring meager goods in 12:88, they ask him to 'fill up the measure for us' in the standard Quran; in Ibn Masud's codex, they said 'load up our mounts'.
variants.title: Surah Yusuf 12:88 — 'Fa-Awqir Rikabana' (Load Up Our Mounts) in Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 12:88, Joseph's brothers say: 'we have brought merchandise of little value [مُزْجَاةٍ]. Fill up the measure for us [فَأَوْفِ لَنَا الْكَيْلَ] and be charitable to us.' Al-Tabari records through three independent chains to Ibrahim al-Nakha'i that in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud and the recitation of his disciples it read فَأَوْقِرْ رِكَابَنَا / وَأَوْقِرْ رِكَابَنَا ('Load up our mounts for us'), which Ibrahim cited to prove that 'muzjah' meant scanty in quantity rather than counterfeit.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: Fill up the measure for us
variants.variant_target_english: Load up our mounts for us
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: فَلَمَّا دَخَلُواْ عَلَيۡهِ قَالُواْ يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلۡعَزِيزُ مَسَّنَا وَأَهۡلَنَا ٱلضُّرُّ وَجِئۡنَا بِبِضَٰعَةٖ مُّزۡجَىٰةٖ فَأَوۡفِ لَنَا ٱلۡكَيۡلَ وَتَصَدَّقۡ عَلَيۡنَآۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَجۡزِي ٱلۡمُتَصَدِّقِينَ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: When they entered upon him, they said, ‘Great one! Hardship has touched us and our house, and we have brought merchandise of little value. Fill up the measure for us and be charitable to us. Surely God rewards the charitable.’

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical scholars treat 'wa-awqir rikabana' (load up our mounts) as an explanatory reading conveying the practical meaning of 'fa-awfi lana al-kayla' (fill up the measure for us).
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari preserves three separate Kufan chains from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i explicitly attesting that 'wa-awqir rikabana' was written in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud and actively recited by his companions.

variants.hadith_arabic: 19754- حدثنا ابن حميد ، قال: حدثنا جرير ، عن مغيرة ، عن يزيد بن الوليد ، عن إبراهيم ، في قوله: ( وجئنا ببضاعة مزجاة ) ، قال: قليلة ، ألا تسمع إلى قوله: " فَأَوْقِرْ رِكَابَنَا " ، وهم يقرءون كذلك. 19755- حدثني يعقوب بن إبراهيم ، قال: حدثنا هشيم ، قال، أخبرنا مغيرة ، عن إبراهيم ، أنه قال: ما أراها إلا القليلة ، لأنها في مصحف عبد الله: " وَأَوْقِرْ رِكَابَنا " ، يعني قوله: " مزجاة ".
variants.hadith_english: **19754** — *Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Yazid b. al-Walid, from Ibrahim, regarding His saying:* {and we have brought merchandise of little value [muzjah]}, he said: "Meager, do you not hear His saying: 'And fill up our mounts' [fa'awqir rikābanā], and they recite it thus." **19755** — *Ya'qub b. Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, he said: Mughirah informed us, from Ibrahim, that he said:* "I do not consider it to be other than 'meager', because it is in the codex of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]: 'And fill up our mounts' [wa'awqir rikābanā], meaning His saying: 'of little value' [muzjah]."

variants.short_title: 'Walk Upon Them' vs 'Pass By Them' in 12:105
variants.plain_english_hook: In 12:105, the standard Quran asks how many signs in the heavens and earth people 'pass by' (yamurruna); in Abdullah bin Masud's codex, it read 'walk upon' (yamshuna).
variants.title: Surah Yusuf 12:105 — 'Yamshuna 'Alayha' in Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf vs 'Yamurruna'
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 12:105, the verse reads وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ آيَةٍ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ يَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْهَا ('How many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by!'). Al-Tabari records via Qatadah that in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud it was written يَمْشُونَ عَلَيْهَا ('do they walk upon!').
variants.uthmanic_target_english: do they pass by!
variants.variant_target_english: do they walk upon!
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: وَكَأَيِّن مِّنۡ ءَايَةٖ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ يَمُرُّونَ عَلَيۡهَا وَهُمۡ عَنۡهَا مُعۡرِضُونَ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: How many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by! Yet they turn away from it.
variants.variant_full_arabic: وَكَأَيِّن مِّنۡ ءَايَةٖ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ يَمۡشُونَ عَلَيۡهَا وَهُمۡ عَنۡهَا مُعۡرِضُونَ
variants.variant_full_english: How many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they walk upon! Yet they turn away from it.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical commentators view 'yamshuna' (they walk) and 'yamurruna' (they pass by) as near-synonyms describing heedless traversal over God's signs.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari preserves Qatadah's direct testimony that 'yamshuna 'alayha' (replacing the root m-r-r with m-sh-y) stood in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud.

variants.short_title: 'Almost Removed Mountains' (Kada vs Kana) in 14:46
variants.plain_english_hook: Whether 14:46 means their plot 'could never' move mountains or 'almost' moved mountains depends on one letter: standard 'kana' (was) vs Ibn Masud, Ubayy, Umar, and Ali's 'kada' (almost).
variants.title: Surah Ibrahim 14:46 — 'Wa-In Kada Makruhum' in Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy's Codices
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 14:46, the clause وَإِنْ كَانَ مَكْرُهُمْ لِتَزُولَ مِنْهُ الْجِبَالُ (with nun in 'kana') is interpreted by the majority of reciters (who read 'litazula') as a negation: 'and their scheme was not such as to remove the mountains.' Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record that Abdullah bin Mas'ud (in his Mushaf), Ubayy bin Ka'b, Umar bin al-Khattab, and Ali bin Abi Talib read وَإِنْ كَادَ مَكْرُهُمْ لَتَزُولُ مِنْهُ الْجِبَالُ (with dal in 'kada' and dammah on 'latazulu'), reversing the sense to an affirmative near-occurrence: 'and indeed their scheme almost removed the mountains by it.'
variants.uthmanic_target_arabic: وَإِن كَانَ مَكۡرُهُمۡ لِتَزُولَ مِنۡهُ ٱلۡجِبَالُ
variants.uthmanic_target_english: even though their scheme was (such as) to remove the mountains by it
variants.variant_target_arabic: وَإِن كَادَ مَكۡرُهُمۡ لَتَزُولُ مِنۡهُ ٱلۡجِبَالُ
variants.variant_target_english: and indeed their scheme almost removed the mountains by it
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: وَقَدۡ مَكَرُواْ مَكۡرَهُمۡ وَعِندَ ٱللَّهِ مَكۡرُهُمۡ وَإِن كَانَ مَكۡرُهُمۡ لِتَزُولَ مِنۡهُ ٱلۡجِبَالُ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: They schemed their scheme, but their scheme was known to God, even though their scheme was (such as) to remove the mountains by it.’
variants.variant_full_arabic: وَقَدۡ مَكَرُواْ مَكۡرَهُمۡ وَعِندَ ٱللَّهِ مَكۡرُهُمۡ وَإِن كَادَ مَكۡرُهُمۡ لَتَزُولُ مِنۡهُ ٱلۡجِبَالُ
variants.variant_full_english: They schemed their scheme, but their scheme was known to God, and indeed their scheme almost removed the mountains by it.’

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari acknowledges that Companions and Successors recited 'wa-in kada' with a dal, but rules that it is impermissible to recite it today because the Uthmanic manuscripts are written 'wa-in kana' with a nun, and one may not alter the orthography of the Muslims' Mushafs.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari's explicit concession—that the Companion reading 'wa-in kada' (attested for Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf, Umar, Ali, and Ubayy) is grammatically sound and was adapted by the canonical Kufan reciter al-Kisa'i onto the Uthmanic rasm 'wa-in kana latazulu'—demonstrates how a non-Uthmanic consonantal variant directly generated a canonical Qira'at dispute.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: قال ابن جريج: أخبرني عمرو بن دينار ، عن عكرمة ، عن عمر بن الخطاب ، أنه كان يقرأ " وَإِنْ كادَ مَكْرُهُمْ لَتَزُولُ مِنْهُ الجِبالُ ". قال قتادة: وفي مصحف عبد الله بن مسعود: " وَإِنْ كادَ مَكْرُهُمْ لَتَزُولُ مِنْهُ الجِبالُ ". وذلك أن الذين قرءوا ذلك بفتح اللام الأولى ورفع الثانية قرءوا: " وَإِنْ كادَ مَكْرُهُمْ " بالدال ، وهي إذا قرئت كذلك ، فالصحيح من القراءة مع " وَإِنْ كادَ " فتح اللام الأولى ورفع الثانية على ما قرءوا ، وغير جائز عندنا القراءة كذلك ، لأن مصاحفنا بخلاف ذلك ، وإنما خطَّ مصاحفنا وإن كان بالنون لا بالدال.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Ibn Jurayj said: 'Amr bin Dinar informed me, from 'Ikrimah, from 'Umar bin al-Khattab, that he used to recite: '{And their plot almost caused the mountains to move from it}'. Qatadah said: And in the codex (Mushaf) of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud: '{And their plot almost caused the mountains to move from it}'. And that is because those who recited it with a fathah on the first lam and a dammah on the second recited: '{wa-in kada makruhum}' with a dal... And it is not permissible in our view to recite like that, because our manuscripts are contrary to that. The script of our manuscripts is 'wa-in kana' with a nun, not with a dal.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وفي مصحف عبد الله بن مسعود: " وَإِنْ كادَ مَكْرُهُمْ لَتَزُولُ مِنْهُ الجِبالُ "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the codex (Mushaf) of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud: '{And their plot almost caused the mountains to move from it}'

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: قال : فهو قول الله - عز وجل - : " وإن كاد مكرهم لتزول منه الجبال " . قال أبو إسحاق : وكذلك هي في قراءة عبد الله : " وإن كاد مكرهم " . قلت : وكذا روي عن أبي بن كعب ، وعمر بن الخطاب - رضي الله عنهما - أنهما قرآ : " وإن كاد " كما قرأ علي .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: This is the saying of Allah (the Exalted and Most Honored): 'though their plot was almost (*Wa in kad*) one to remove the mountains from their places.' Abu Ishaq said: "And similarly it is in the recitation of 'Abdullah: '*Wa in kad makruhum*' (though their plot was almost...)." I (Ibn Kathir) say: And similarly it was narrated from Ubayy bin Ka'b and 'Umar bin Al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with them) that they recited "*Wa in kad*" as 'Ali recited.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة عبد الله : " وإن كاد مكرهم "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of 'Abdullah: '*Wa in kad makruhum*'

variants.short_title: 16:9 — 'Among You Is One Who Deviates' vs. 'From It'
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran says 'there is deviation from it [the way],' Ibn Mas'ud's codex read 'and among you is one who deviates, and if God had pleased, He would have guided you.'
variants.title: Substitution of 'And Among You Is One Who Deviates' (Wa-Minkum Jā'ir) in 16:9
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 16:9, the Uthmanic text reads 'وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ قَصۡدُ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَمِنۡهَا جَآئِرٞۚ وَلَوۡ شَآءَ لَهَدَىٰكُمۡ أَجۡمَعِينَ' ('(It is incumbent) on God (to set the) direction of the way, yet (there is) deviation from it. If He had (so) pleased, He would indeed have guided you all.'). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record via Qatadah that Abdullah bin Mas'ud recited 'وَمِنْكُمْ جَائِرٌ وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَهَدَاكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ' ('yet among you is one who deviates. If God had (so) pleased, He would indeed have guided you all.'), shifting the subject of deviation from the paths ('minhā') to the human audience ('minkum') and adding the divine name 'Allāh.'
variants.uthmanic_target_english: yet (there is) deviation from it. If He had (so) pleased
variants.variant_target_english: yet among you is one who deviates. If God had (so) pleased
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ قَصۡدُ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَمِنۡهَا جَآئِرٞۚ وَلَوۡ شَآءَ لَهَدَىٰكُمۡ أَجۡمَعِينَ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: (It is incumbent) on God (to set the) direction of the way, yet (there is) deviation from it. If He had (so) pleased, He would indeed have guided you all.
variants.variant_full_arabic: وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ قَصۡدُ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَمِنْكُمْ جَائِرٌ وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَهَدَىٰكُمۡ أَجۡمَعِينَ
variants.variant_full_english: (It is incumbent) on God (to set the) direction of the way, yet among you is one who deviates. If God had (so) pleased, He would indeed have guided you all.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Commentators explain that whether deviation is attributed to the roads ('minhā,' i.e., deviant sects and paths) or to the people traveling them ('minkum,' i.e., those who stray from the truth), the underlying theological meaning remains consistent.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari transmits via two independent chains from Qatadah (through Sa'id bin Abi Arubah and Ma'mar) that Ibn Mas'ud's codex read both 'وَمِنْكُمْ جَائِرٌ' and the explicit subject 'وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ.'

And in the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud it is: "And among you is a deviating one, and if Allah had (so) pleased, He would have guided you all" (*wa minkum ja'ir wa law sha' Allahu la-hadakum ajma'in*).
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وفي قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود: " وَمِنْكُمْ جَائِرٌ وَلَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ لَهَدَاكُمْ أجمَعِينَ"
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: And in the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud it is: "And among you is a deviating one, and if Allah had (so) pleased, He would have guided you all"

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: قال ابن عباس وغيره : هي الطرق المختلفة ، والآراء والأهواء المتفرقة ، كاليهودية والنصرانية والمجوسية ، وقرأابن مسعود : " ومنكم جائر " .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Ibn 'Abbas and others said, "They are the differing ways, and disparate opinions and desires, like Judaism, Christianity, and Zoroastrianism, and Ibn Mas'ud recited: '*And among you is he who strays*.'"

variants.short_title: 17:23 — 'Your Lord Enjoined' vs. 'Your Lord Decreed'
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran reads 'Your Lord has decreed (wa-qaḍā) that you worship none but Him,' Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy's codices read 'Your Lord has enjoined (wa-waṣṣā).'
variants.title: Substitution of 'Enjoined' (Wa-Waṣṣā) for 'Decreed' (Wa-Qaḍā) in 17:23
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 17:23, the Uthmanic text begins '۞وَقَضَىٰ رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعۡبُدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ' ('Your Lord has decreed that you do not serve any but Him'). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record that Abdullah bin Mas'ud and the Mushaf of Ubayy bin Ka'b transmitted by Ibn Abbas read 'وَوَصَّى رَبُّكَ' ('Your Lord has enjoined'), with al-Dahhak claiming in Tabari that scribes inadvertently joined the letter wāw to the ṣād so that it turned into a qāf.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Commentators explain that 'qaḍā' in the Uthmanic reading carries the lexical meaning of religious command (amr) rather than deterministic decree, making it synonymous in meaning with 'waṣṣā' (enjoined).
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari preserves both physical manuscript testimony of Ubayy's Mushaf reading 'wa-waṣṣā rabbuka' and al-Dahhak's explicit paleographic claim that the Uthmanic 'wa-qaḍā' arose when scribes ligatured the wāw and ṣād into a qāf.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: حدثنا ابن عبد الأعلى، قال: ثنا محمد بن ثور، عن معمر، عن قتادة ( وَقَضَى رَبُّكَ أَلا تَعْبُدُوا إِلا إِيَّاهُ ) قال: أمر ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه، وفي حرف ابن مسعود: (وَصَّى رَبُّكَ ألا تَعْبُدُوا إِلا إِيَّاهُ).
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: (And your Lord has decreed that you do not serve any but Him), he said: Commanded that you do not serve any but Him. And in the reading (harf) of Ibn Mas'ud: (And your Lord has enjoined that you do not serve any but Him).
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وفي حرف ابن مسعود: (وَصَّى رَبُّكَ ألا تَعْبُدُوا إِلا إِيَّاهُ)
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: And in the reading (harf) of Ibn Mas'ud: (And your Lord has enjoined that you do not serve any but Him)

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: قال مجاهد ( وقضى ) يعني وصى وكذا قرأ أبي بن كعب وعبد الله بن مسعود والضحاك بن مزاحم ووصى ربك ألا تعبدوا إلا إياه ولهذا قرن بعبادته بر الوالدين فقال ( وبالوالدين إحسانا ) أي وأمر بالوالدين إحسانا كما قال في الآية الأخرى ( أن اشكر لي ولوالديك إلي المصير ) [ لقمان 14 .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: *(And He has Qada)* means enjoined. This is also how Ubayy bin Ka'b, Ibn Mas'ud and Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim recited the Ayah as: "And your Lord enjoined that you worship none but Him."

variants.short_title: Ibn Mas'ud Reads 'They Were Given' in Q. 17:85
variants.plain_english_hook: Instead of 'You have only been given a little knowledge' (addressing all people), Ibn Mas'ud's codex read 'They have only been given a little knowledge,' restricting the statement to the questioners.
variants.title: Third-Person 'Wa-Ma Utu' Instead of 'Wa-Ma Utitum' in Q. 17:85 (Ibn Mas'ud)
variants.diff_summary: In Sahih al-Bukhari 7462 and Sahih Muslim 2794b, 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud narrates the revelation of Q. 17:85 when Jewish questioners in Medina asked the Prophet about the Spirit (al-Ruh) and recites the final clause as 'وَمَا أُوتُوا مِنَ الْعِلْمِ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً' ('And they have only been given a little knowledge'), with the Kufan master al-A'mash explicitly noting: 'Thus it is in our recitation' ('هَكَذَا فِي قِرِاءَتِنَا'). Shifting the verb from second-person plural ('أُوتِيتُم', 'you have been given') to third-person plural ('أُوتُوا', 'they have been given') alters both the consonantal rasm and the theological scope of who possesses little knowledge.
variants.uthmanic_target_arabic: وَمَآ أُوتِيتُم مِّنَ ٱلۡعِلۡمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلٗا
variants.uthmanic_target_english: You have only been given a little knowledge (of it).
variants.variant_target_arabic: وَمَا أُوتُوا مِنَ الْعِلْمِ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً
variants.variant_target_english: They have only been given a little knowledge (of it).
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: وَيَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلرُّوحِۖ قُلِ ٱلرُّوحُ مِنۡ أَمۡرِ رَبِّي وَمَآ أُوتِيتُم مِّنَ ٱلۡعِلۡمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلٗا
variants.uthmanic_full_english: They ask you about the spirit. Say: ‘The spirit (comes) from the command of my Lord. You have only been given a little knowledge (of it).’
variants.variant_full_arabic: وَيَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلرُّوحِۖ قُلِ ٱلرُّوحُ مِنۡ أَمۡرِ رَبِّي وَمَا أُوتُوا مِنَ الْعِلْمِ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً
variants.variant_full_english: They ask you about the spirit. Say: ‘The spirit (comes) from the command of my Lord. They have only been given a little knowledge (of it).’

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Exegetes such as al-Tabari explain that the Uthmanic second-person plural ('utitum') addresses either the Jewish questioners directly or all humanity, whereas Ibn Mas'ud's third-person plural ('utu') matches the preceding third-person verb 'they ask you' (yas'alunaka).
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In Sahih al-Bukhari 7462, Ibn Mas'ud was physically present when the Prophet received and recited this verse in Medina, and al-A'mash confirms that 'wa-ma utu' remained the established text of the Kufan codex of Ibn Mas'ud.

hadiths.transmitted_by: Al-A'mash -> Ibrahim -> Alqamah -> Abdullah bin Masud
hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الْوَاحِدِ، عَنِ الأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، قَالَ بَيْنَا أَنَا أَمْشِي، مَعَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي بَعْضِ حَرْثِ الْمَدِينَةِ وَهْوَ يَتَوَكَّأُ عَلَى عَسِيبٍ مَعَهُ، فَمَرَرْنَا عَلَى نَفَرٍ مِنَ الْيَهُودِ فَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ سَلُوهُ عَنِ الرُّوحِ‏.‏ فَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ لاَ تَسْأَلُوهُ أَنْ يَجِيءَ فِيهِ بِشَىْءٍ تَكْرَهُونَهُ‏.‏ فَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ لَنَسْأَلَنَّهُ‏.‏ فَقَامَ إِلَيْهِ رَجُلٌ مِنْهُمْ فَقَالَ يَا أَبَا الْقَاسِمِ مَا الرُّوحُ فَسَكَتَ عَنْهُ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَعَلِمْتُ أَنَّهُ يُوحَى إِلَيْهِ فَقَالَ ‏{‏وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الرُّوحِ قُلِ الرُّوحُ مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّي وَمَا أُوتُوا مِنَ الْعِلْمِ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ الأَعْمَشُ هَكَذَا فِي قِرِاءَتِنَا‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Ibn Mas`ud:While I was walking in company with the Prophet (ﷺ) in one of the fields of Medina, the Prophet (ﷺ) was reclining on a palm leave stalk which he carried with him. We passed by a group of Jews. Some of them said to the others, "Ask him about the spirit." The others said, "Do not ask him, lest he would say something that you hate." Some of them said, "We will ask him." So a man from among them stood up and said, 'O Abal-Qasim! What is the spirit?" The Prophet (ﷺ) kept quiet and I knew that he was being divinely inspired. Then he said: "They ask you concerning the Spirit, Say: The Spirit; its knowledge is with my Lord. And of knowledge you (mankind) have been given only a little (wa-ma utu mina l-'ilmi illa qalilan: "And they have only been given a little knowledge")." Al-A'mash said: "Thus it is in our recitation."
hadiths.highlight_arabic: وَمَا أُوتُوا مِنَ الْعِلْمِ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ الأَعْمَشُ هَكَذَا فِي قِرِاءَتِنَا
hadiths.highlight_english: (wa-ma utu mina l-'ilmi illa qalilan: "And they have only been given a little knowledge")." Al-A'mash said: "Thus it is in our recitation."

hadiths.transmitted_by: Isa bin Yunus -> Al-A'mash -> Ibrahim -> Alqamah -> Abdullah bin Masud
hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو بَكْرِ بْنُ أَبِي شَيْبَةَ، وَأَبُو سَعِيدٍ الأَشَجُّ قَالاَ حَدَّثَنَا وَكِيعٌ، ح وَحَدَّثَنَا إِسْحَاقُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ الْحَنْظَلِيُّ، وَعَلِيُّ بْنُ خَشْرَمٍ، قَالاَ أَخْبَرَنَا عِيسَى بْنُ يُونُسَ، كِلاَهُمَا عَنِ الأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، قَالَ كُنْتُ أَمْشِي مَعَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي حَرْثٍ بِالْمَدِينَةِ ‏.‏ بِنَحْوِ حَدِيثِ حَفْصٍ غَيْرَ أَنَّ فِي حَدِيثِ وَكِيعٍ وَمَا أُوتِيتُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً ‏.‏ وَفِي حَدِيثِ عِيسَى بْنِ يُونُسَ وَمَا أُوتُوا ‏.‏ مِنْ رِوَايَةِ ابْنِ خَشْرَمٍ ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Abdullah reported: I was walking along with Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) in a field of Medina. The rest of the hadith is similar to the narration of Hafs, except that in the narration of Waki' it is: "And you have only been given a little knowledge" (wa-ma utitum mina l-'ilmi illa qalilan), and in the narration of 'Isa bin Yunus from the transmission of Ibn Khashram it is: "And they have only been given" (wa-ma utu).
hadiths.highlight_arabic: وَفِي حَدِيثِ عِيسَى بْنِ يُونُسَ وَمَا أُوتُوا ‏.‏ مِنْ رِوَايَةِ ابْنِ خَشْرَمٍ
hadiths.highlight_english: and in the narration of 'Isa bin Yunus from the transmission of Ibn Khashram it is: "And they have only been given" (wa-ma utu).

variants.short_title: 'A House of Gold' vs 'Decorative House' in 17:93
variants.plain_english_hook: Early exegetes like Mujahid admitted they did not know what 'zukhruf' meant in 17:93 until they saw Abdullah bin Masud's reading: 'or you have a house of gold'.
variants.title: Surah Al-Isra 17:93 — 'Baytun min Dhahabin' (House of Gold) in Ibn Mas'ud
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 17:93, the Meccan disbelievers demand of Muhammad, 'or (until) you have a house of ornament/decoration [مِنْ زُخْرُفٍ].' Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record authentic reports from Mujahid stating: 'We did not know what al-zukhruf was until we saw it in the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud: or (until) you have a house of gold [أَوْ يَكُونَ لَكَ بَيْتٌ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ].'
variants.uthmanic_target_english: a decorative house
variants.variant_target_english: a house of gold
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: أَوۡ يَكُونَ لَكَ بَيۡتٞ مِّن زُخۡرُفٍ أَوۡ تَرۡقَىٰ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَلَن نُّؤۡمِنَ لِرُقِيِّكَ حَتَّىٰ تُنَزِّلَ عَلَيۡنَا كِتَٰبٗا نَّقۡرَؤُهُۥۗ قُلۡ سُبۡحَانَ رَبِّي هَلۡ كُنتُ إِلَّا بَشَرٗا رَّسُولٗا
variants.uthmanic_full_english: or (until) you have a decorative house, or (until) you ascend into the sky. And we shall not believe in your ascent until you bring down on us a book, so that we may read it.’ Say: ‘Glory to my Lord! Am I anything but a human being, a messenger?’
variants.variant_full_arabic: أَوۡ يَكُونَ لَكَ بَيۡتٞ مِّن ذَهَبٍ أَوۡ تَرۡقَىٰ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَلَن نُّؤۡمِنَ لِرُقِيِّكَ حَتَّىٰ تُنَزِّلَ عَلَيۡنَا كِتَٰبٗا نَّقۡرَؤُهُۥۗ قُلۡ سُبۡحَانَ رَبِّي هَلۡ كُنتُ إِلَّا بَشَرٗا رَّسُولٗا
variants.variant_full_english: or (until) you have a house of gold, or (until) you ascend into the sky. And we shall not believe in your ascent until you bring down on us a book, so that we may read it.’ Say: ‘Glory to my Lord! Am I anything but a human being, a messenger?’

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical scholars explain 'min dhahabin' (of gold) in Ibn Mas'ud's reading as a lexical synonym clarifying the rarer Quranic word 'zukhruf'.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari transmits two authentic chains (via Sufyan al-Thawri and Shu'bah from al-Hakam from Mujahid) in which Mujahid states he saw 'baytun min dhahabin' written in the recitation/codex of Ibn Mas'ud.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: حدثنا الحسن بن يحيى، قال: أخبرنا عبد الرزاق، قال: أخبرنا الثوري، عن رجل، عن الحكم قال: قال مجاهد: كنا لا ندري ما الزخرف حتى رأيناه في قراءة ابن مسعود: " أو يكون لك بيت من ذهب". حدثنا محمد بن المثنى، قال: ثنا محمد بن جعفر، قال: ثنا شعبة، عن الحكم، عن مجاهد، قال: لم أدر ما الزخرف، حتى سمعنا في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود: " بيت من ذهب".
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: *Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Al-Thawri informed us, from a man, from Al-Hakam, who said: Mujahid said:* We did not know what al-Zukhruf was until we saw it in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: 'or you have a house of gold.' *Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna narrated to us... from Mujahid, who said:* I did not know what al-Zukhruf was, until we heard in the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud: 'a house of gold.'
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة ابن مسعود: " أو يكون لك بيت من ذهب"
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: 'or you have a house of gold.'

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: ( أو يكون لك بيت من زخرف ) قال ابن عباس ، ومجاهد ، وقتادة : هو الذهب . وكذلك هو في قراءة ابن مسعود : " أو يكون لك بيت من ذهب " .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt:
> **{ Or you have a house of Zukhruf. }**

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said, "This is gold." This was also what was said in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud, "Or you have a house of gold."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة ابن مسعود : " أو يكون لك بيت من ذهب "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud, "Or you have a house of gold."

variants.variant_arabic: أَوۡ يَكُونَ لَكَ بَيۡتٞ مِّن ذَهَبٍ أَوۡ تَرۡقَىٰ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَلَن نُّؤۡمِنَ لِرُقِيِّكَ حَتَّىٰ تُنَزِّلَ عَلَيۡنَا كِتَٰبٗا نَّقۡرَؤُهُۥۗ قُلۡ سُبۡحَانَ رَبِّي هَلۡ كُنتُ إِلَّا بَشَرٗا رَّسُولٗا
variants.variant_english: or (until) you have a house of gold, or (until) you ascend into the sky. And we shall not believe in your ascent until you bring down on us a book, so that we may read it.’ Say: ‘Glory to my Lord! Am I anything but a human being, a messenger?’

variants.short_title: 'Other Than God' vs 'Except God' in 18:16
variants.plain_english_hook: In 18:16, the Arabic literally says 'withdraw from them and what they worship except God' (illa Allaha); Ibn Masud's codex read 'other than God' (min duni Allahi).
variants.title: Surah Al-Kahf 18:16 — 'Wa-Ma Ya'buduna min Duni Allahi' in Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 18:16, the Youths of the Cave say: وَإِذِ اعْتَزَلْتُمُوهُمْ وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا اللَّهَ ('When you have withdrawn from them and what they serve except God [rendered by Droge as instead of God]'). Because the youths' pagan people worshipped idols rather than Allah, grammarians debated how 'except God' (إِلَّا اللَّهَ) fits the clause unless إِلَّا carries the sense of سِوَى / مِنْ دُونِ ('other than'). Al-Tabari records from Qatadah that in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud it was written: 'and what they serve other than God' (وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ).
variants.uthmanic_target_english: and what they serve instead of God
variants.variant_target_english: and what they serve besides God (min dūni llāhi)
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: وَإِذِ ٱعۡتَزَلۡتُمُوهُمۡ وَمَا يَعۡبُدُونَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ فَأۡوُۥٓاْ إِلَى ٱلۡكَهۡفِ يَنشُرۡ لَكُمۡ رَبُّكُم مِّن رَّحۡمَتِهِۦ وَيُهَيِّئۡ لَكُم مِّنۡ أَمۡرِكُم مِّرۡفَقٗا
variants.uthmanic_full_english: When you have withdrawn from them and what they serve instead of God, take refuge in the cave. Your Lord will display some of His mercy to you, and will furnish some relief for you in your situation.’
variants.variant_full_arabic: وَإِذِ ٱعۡتَزَلۡتُمُوهُمۡ وَمَا يَعۡبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ فَأۡوُۥٓاْ إِلَى ٱلۡكَهۡفِ يَنشُرۡ لَكُمۡ رَبُّكُم مِّن رَّحۡمَتِهِۦ وَيُهَيِّئۡ لَكُم مِّنۡ أَمۡرِكُم مِّرۡفَقٗا
variants.variant_full_english: When you have withdrawn from them and what they serve besides God (min dūni llāhi), take refuge in the cave. Your Lord will display some of His mercy to you, and will furnish some relief for you in your situation.’

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari and Qatadah state that 'min duni Allahi' (other than God) in Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf represents the intended interpretation (tafsir) of the Uthmanic exception 'illa Allaha'.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Droge's English translation of the Uthmanic text already renders 'illa Allaha' as 'instead of God' precisely because the literal Uthmanic wording ('except God') is syntactically difficult without Ibn Mas'ud's reading 'min duni Allahi'.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: حدثنا بشر، قال: ثنا يزيد، قال: ثنا سعيد، عن قتادة، قوله ( وإذ اعتزلتموهم وما يعبدون إلا الله ) وهي في مصحف عبد الله: " وما يعبدون من دون الله " هذا تفسيرها.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: *Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah,* regarding His saying: {and what they serve instead of God}: 'And it is in the codex (Mushaf) of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]: "and what they serve other than God" (wa-ma ya'buduna min duni Allah); this is its interpretation.'
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وهي في مصحف عبد الله: " وما يعبدون من دون الله "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: And it is in the codex (Mushaf) of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]: "and what they serve other than God"
