scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical scholars argue that 'al-isti'nas' in Arabic can mean ascertaining a resident's presence or seeking permission, and Ibn Kathir characterizes the attribution of the scribal-error statement to Ibn Abbas as very strange (gharib jiddan).
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari records multiple independent chains (via Sufyan al-Thawri, Shu'bah, and Hushaym from Sa'id bin Jubayr, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and al-A'mash) attesting that Ibn Mas'ud's codex, Ubayy bin Ka'b, and Ibn Abbas all read 'tasta'dhinu' (with dhal) rather than 'tasta'nisu' (with nun), and al-Tabari himself adopts Ibn Mas'ud's sequence ('greet and ask permission') as the intended meaning.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: حدثنا ابن بشار، قال: ثنا محمد بن جعفر، قال: ثنا شعبة، عن أبي بشر، عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، في هذه الآية ( حَتَّى تَسْتَأْنِسُوا وَتُسَلِّمُوا عَلَى أَهْلِهَا ) قال: أخطأ الكاتب، وكان ابن عباس يقرأ "حَتَّى تَسْتَأْذِنُوا وَتُسَلِّمُوا" وكان يقرؤها على قراءة أُبيّ بن كعب. حدثنا القاسم، قال: ثنا الحسين، قال: ثني هشيم، قال: أخبرنا مغيرة، عن إبراهيم، قال: في مصحف ابن مسعود: "حَتَّى تُسَلِّمُوا عَلَى أَهْلِهَا وَتَسْتَأْذِنُوا". قال: ثنا هشيم، قال: أخبرنا جعفر بن إياس، عن سعيد، عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرؤها: "يَأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتًا غَيْرَ بُيُوتِكُمْ حَتَّى تُسَلِّمُوا عَلَى أَهْلِهَا وَتَسْتَأْذِنُوا" قال: وإنما تستأنسوا وَهْم من الكاتب.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us... from Sa'id bin Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding this verse: {until you ask permission [tasta'nisu] and greet its inhabitants}, he said: 'The scribe made a mistake. And Ibn 'Abbas used to recite, "until you ask permission [tasta'dhinu] and greet." And he used to recite it according to the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b.' Al-Qasim narrated to us... from Ibrahim, who said: 'In the Mushaf of Ibn Mas'ud [it is]: "until you greet its inhabitants and ask for permission."' He said: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Ja'far bin Iyas informed us, from Sa'id, from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite it: 'O you who believe! Do not enter houses other than your own houses until you greet its inhabitants and ask for permission.' He said: 'And "tasta'nisu" is merely an illusion (mistake) from the scribe.'
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في مصحف ابن مسعود: "حَتَّى تُسَلِّمُوا عَلَى أَهْلِهَا وَتَسْتَأْذِنُوا"
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: In the Mushaf of Ibn Mas'ud [it is]: "until you greet its inhabitants and ask for permission."

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وروى معاذ بن سليمان ، عن جعفر بن إياس ، عن سعيد ، عن ابن عباس ، بمثله ، وزاد : وكان ابن عباس يقرأ : " حتى تستأذنوا وتسلموا " ، وكان يقرأ على قراءة أبي بن كعب رضي الله عنه . وهذا غريب جدا عن ابن عباس . وقال هشيم أخبرنا مغيرة ، عن إبراهيم قال : في مصحف ابن مسعود : " حتى تسلموا على أهلها وتستأذنوا " . وهذا أيضا رواية عن ابن عباس ، وهو اختيار ابن جرير .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Mu'adh bin Sulayman narrated from Ja'far bin Iyas, from Sa'id, from Ibn 'Abbas similarly, and added: "And Ibn 'Abbas used to recite it: 'until you ask permission (Tasta'thinu) and greet,' and he used to recite according to the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him." This is very strange coming from Ibn 'Abbas. Hushaym said: Mughirah informed us, from Ibrahim, who said: "In the Mushaf of Ibn Mas'ud, it says: 'until you greet its inhabitants and ask permission'." This is also a narration from Ibn 'Abbas, and it is the choice of Ibn Jarir.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في مصحف ابن مسعود : " حتى تسلموا على أهلها وتستأذنوا "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: In the Mushaf of Ibn Mas'ud, it says: 'until you greet its inhabitants and ask permission'

variants.variant_arabic: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَدۡخُلُواْ بُيُوتًا غَيۡرَ بُيُوتِكُمۡ حَتَّىٰ تُسَلِّمُواْ عَلَىٰٓ أَهۡلِهَا وَتَسۡتَأۡذِنُواْۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ خَيۡرٞ لَّكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَذَكَّرُونَ
variants.variant_english: You who believe! Do not enter houses other than your (own) houses, until you ask permission (tasta'dhinu) and greet its inhabitants. That is better for you, so that you may take heed.
variants.hadith_arabic: حدثنا ابن بشار، قال: ثنا محمد بن جعفر، قال: ثنا شعبة، عن أبي بشر، عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس، في هذه الآية ( حَتَّى تَسْتَأْنِسُوا وَتُسَلِّمُوا عَلَى أَهْلِهَا ) قال: أخطأ الكاتب، وكان ابن عباس يقرأ "حَتَّى تَسْتَأْذِنُوا وَتُسَلِّمُوا" وكان يقرؤها على قراءة أُبيّ بن كعب. حدثنا القاسم، قال: ثنا الحسين، قال: ثني هشيم، قال: أخبرنا مغيرة، عن إبراهيم، قال: في مصحف ابن مسعود: "حَتَّى تُسَلِّمُوا عَلَى أَهْلِهَا وَتَسْتَأْذِنُوا". قال: ثنا هشيم، قال: أخبرنا جعفر بن إياس، عن سعيد، عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرؤها: "يَأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتًا غَيْرَ بُيُوتِكُمْ حَتَّى تُسَلِّمُوا عَلَى أَهْلِهَا وَتَسْتَأْذِنُوا" قال: وإنما تستأنسوا وَهْم من الكاتب.
variants.hadith_english: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us... from Sa'id bin Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding this verse: {until you ask permission [tasta'nisu] and greet its inhabitants}, he said: 'The scribe made a mistake. And Ibn 'Abbas used to recite, "until you ask permission [tasta'dhinu] and greet." And he used to recite it according to the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b.' Al-Qasim narrated to us... from Ibrahim, who said: 'In the Mushaf of Ibn Mas'ud [it is]: "until you greet its inhabitants and ask for permission."' He said: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Ja'far bin Iyas informed us, from Sa'id, from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite it: 'O you who believe! Do not enter houses other than your own houses until you greet its inhabitants and ask for permission.' He said: 'And "tasta'nisu" is merely an illusion (mistake) from the scribe.'

variants.short_title: Ibn Mas'ud & Jabir Add 'To Them' in Q. 24:33
variants.plain_english_hook: In verse 24:33 on slave-girls forced into prostitution, the Uthmanic text says 'God is forgiving after their compulsion' without specifying whom He forgives. Ibn Mas'ud's codex adds 'to them' (the women).
variants.title: Addition of 'Lahunna' ('Forgiving to Them') in Q. 24:33 (Ibn Mas'ud & Jabir)
variants.diff_summary: In Sahih Muslim 3029a (narrated via the Kufan reciter al-A'mash from Jabir bin 'Abdullah), Tafsir al-Tabari (from Sa'id bin Jubayr), and Tafsir Ibn Kathir (explicitly cited as 'في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود' — 'in the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud'), Q. 24:33 includes the feminine plural prepositional phrase 'لَهُنَّ' ('to them [feminine]') after 'مِنْ بَعْدِ إِكْرَاهِهِنَّ': 'فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ مِنْ بَعْدِ إِكْرَاهِهِنَّ لَهُنَّ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ' ('surely God is forgiving and compassionate to them [the coerced women] after their being forced'). Whereas the Uthmanic Arabic text lacks 'لَهُنَّ', Ibn Mas'ud's codex and Jabir's recitation contain 'لَهُنَّ' explicitly in the Arabic text.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: forgiving (and) compassionate (to them) after their being forced.
variants.variant_target_arabic: مِنْ بَعْدِ إِكْرَاهِهِنَّ لَهُنَّ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ
variants.variant_target_english: forgiving (and) compassionate to them [lahunna] after their being forced.
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: وَلۡيَسۡتَعۡفِفِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَجِدُونَ نِكَاحًا حَتَّىٰ يُغۡنِيَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦۗ وَٱلَّذِينَ يَبۡتَغُونَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِمَّا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُمۡ فَكَاتِبُوهُمۡ إِنۡ عَلِمۡتُمۡ فِيهِمۡ خَيۡرٗاۖ وَءَاتُوهُم مِّن مَّالِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِيٓ ءَاتَىٰكُمۡۚ وَلَا تُكۡرِهُواْ فَتَيَٰتِكُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡبِغَآءِ إِنۡ أَرَدۡنَ تَحَصُّنٗا لِّتَبۡتَغُواْ عَرَضَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۚ وَمَن يُكۡرِههُّنَّ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ إِكۡرَٰهِهِنَّ غَفُورٞ رَّحِيمٞ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: Let those who do not find (the means for) marriage abstain, until God enriches them from His favor. Those who seek the writ, among what your right (hands) own, write (it) for them, if you know any good in them, and give them some of the wealth of God which He has given you. And do not force your young women into prostitution, if they wish (to live in) chastity, so that you may seek (the fleeting) goods of this present life. Whoever forces them – surely God is forgiving (and) compassionate (to them) after their being forced.
variants.variant_full_arabic: وَلۡيَسۡتَعۡفِفِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَجِدُونَ نِكَاحًا حَتَّىٰ يُغۡنِيَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦۗ وَٱلَّذِينَ يَبۡتَغُونَ ٱلۡكَٰتَبَ مِمَّا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُمۡ فَكَاتِبُوهُمۡ إِنۡ عَلِمۡتُمۡ فِيهِمۡ خَيۡرٗاۖ وَءَاتُوهُم مِّن مَّالِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِيٓ ءَاتَىٰكُمۡۚ وَلَا تُكۡرِهُواْ فَتَيَٰتِكُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡبِغَآءِ إِنۡ أَرَدۡنَ تَحَصُّنٗا لِّتَبۡتَغُواْ عَرَضَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۚ وَمَن يُكۡرِههُّنَّ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مِنْ بَعْدِ إِكْرَاهِهِنَّ لَهُنَّ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ
variants.variant_full_english: Let those who do not find (the means for) marriage abstain, until God enriches them from His favor. Those who seek the writ, among what your right (hands) own, write (it) for them, if you know any good in them, and give them some of the wealth of God which He has given you. And do not force your young women into prostitution, if they wish (to live in) chastity, so that you may seek (the fleeting) goods of this present life. Whoever forces them – surely God is forgiving (and) compassionate to them [lahunna] after their being forced.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Exegetes explain that 'lahunna' ('to them') makes explicit what is already grammatically understood in the Uthmanic text—that divine forgiveness applies to the coerced female slaves rather than to the masters who coerced them.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In Sahih Muslim 3029a, Jabir bin 'Abdullah quotes the verse as revealed with the word 'lahunna,' and Ibn Kathir confirms via Sa'id bin Jubayr that this exact word stood in the codex recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud.

hadiths.transmitted_by: Al-A'mash -> Abu Sufyan -> Jabir bin Abdullah
hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو بَكْرِ بْنُ أَبِي شَيْبَةَ، وَأَبُو كُرَيْبٍ جَمِيعًا عَنْ أَبِي مُعَاوِيَةَ، - وَاللَّفْظُ لأَبِي كُرَيْبٍ - حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو مُعَاوِيَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا الأَعْمَشُ، عَنْ أَبِي سُفْيَانَ، عَنْ جَابِرٍ، قَالَ كَانَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ أُبَىٍّ ابْنِ سَلُولَ يَقُولُ لِجَارِيَةٍ لَهُ اذْهَبِي فَابْغِينَا شَيْئًا فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ ‏{‏ وَلاَ تُكْرِهُوا فَتَيَاتِكُمْ عَلَى الْبِغَاءِ إِنْ أَرَدْنَ تَحَصُّنًا لِتَبْتَغُوا عَرَضَ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَمَنْ يُكْرِهْهُنَّ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ مِنْ بَعْدِ إِكْرَاهِهِنَّ‏}‏ لَهُنَّ ‏{‏ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ‏}‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Jabir reported that 'Abdullah b. Ubayy b. Salul used to say to his slave-girl: Go and fetch something for us by committing prostitution. It was in this connection that Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, revealed this verse: "And compel not your slave-girls to prostitution when they desire to keep chaste in order to seek the frail goods of this world's life, and whoever compels them, then surely after their compulsion Allah is Forgiving, Merciful to them (lahunna)" (24:33).
hadiths.highlight_arabic: فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ مِنْ بَعْدِ إِكْرَاهِهِنَّ‏}‏ لَهُنَّ ‏{‏ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ‏}
hadiths.highlight_english: then surely after their compulsion Allah is Forgiving, Merciful to them (lahunna)

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: حدثنا أبو كريب ، قال: ثنا ابن يمان، عن أشعث، عن جعفر، عن سعيد بن جُبير، أنه كان يقرأ: فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ مِنْ بَعْدِ إِكْرَاهِهِنَّ لهن غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id bin Jubayr, that he used to recite: "surely God, after their being forced, is forgiving and compassionate to them (lahunna)."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ مِنْ بَعْدِ إِكْرَاهِهِنَّ لهن غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: surely God, after their being forced, is forgiving and compassionate to them (lahunna).

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقال ابن أبي حاتم : حدثنا أبو زرعة ، حدثنا يحيى بن عبد الله ، حدثني ابن لهيعة ، حدثني عطاء ، عن سعيد بن جبير قال : في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود : " فإن الله من بعد إكراههن لهن غفور رحيم " وإثمهن على من أكرههن .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Yahya bin 'Abdullah narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me, 'Ata' narrated to me, from Sa'id bin Jubayr who said: "In the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud it is: 'surely God, after their being forced, is forgiving (and) compassionate to them,' and their sin is upon the one who forced them."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود : " فإن الله من بعد إكراههن لهن غفور رحيم "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: In the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud it is: 'surely God, after their being forced, is forgiving (and) compassionate to them,'

variants.short_title: 'Lay Down Some of Their Clothes' in 24:60
variants.plain_english_hook: Surah 24:60 literally permits elderly women to 'lay down their clothes'; Ibn Masud and Ubayy's readings added 'some of' (min), clarifying that only the outer cloak is meant.
variants.title: Surah An-Nur 24:60 — Addition of 'Min' ('Some of Their Clothes') in Ibn Mas'ud
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 24:60, elderly women past childbearing are told there is no blame on them 'that they lay down their clothes' (أَنْ يَضَعْنَ ثِيَابَهُنَّ). Because laying down all clothes is universally forbidden, jurists restricted 'their clothes' to the outer wrap (jilbab/rida') by appealing to the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud (recorded by Ibn Kathir via Sa'id bin Jubayr) and Ubayy bin Ka'b (recorded by al-Tabari via al-Sha'bi), which read 'that they lay down some of their clothes' (أَنْ يَضَعْنَ مِنْ ثِيَابِهِنَّ).
variants.uthmanic_target_english: that they lay down their clothes
variants.variant_target_english: that they lay down some of their clothes
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: وَٱلۡقَوَٰعِدُ مِنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ ٱلَّـٰتِي لَا يَرۡجُونَ نِكَاحٗا فَلَيۡسَ عَلَيۡهِنَّ جُنَاحٌ أَن يَضَعۡنَ ثِيَابَهُنَّ غَيۡرَ مُتَبَرِّجَٰتِۭ بِزِينَةٖۖ وَأَن يَسۡتَعۡفِفۡنَ خَيۡرٞ لَّهُنَّۗ وَٱللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٞ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: And your women who are past childbearing and have no hope of marriage, there is no blame on them that they lay down their clothes, (as long as there is) no flaunting of (their) charms. But that they abstain is better for them. God is hearing, knowing.
variants.variant_full_arabic: وَٱلۡقَوَٰعِدُ مِنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ ٱلَّـٰتِي لَا يَرۡجُونَ نِكَاحٗا فَلَيۡسَ عَلَيۡهِنَّ جُنَاحٌ أَن يَضَعۡنَ مِن ثِيَابِهِنَّ غَيۡرَ مُتَبَرِّجَٰتِۭ بِزِينَةٖۖ وَأَن يَسۡتَعۡفِفۡنَ خَيۡرٞ لَّهُنَّۗ وَٱللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٞ
variants.variant_full_english: And your women who are past childbearing and have no hope of marriage, there is no blame on them that they lay down some of their clothes, (as long as there is) no flaunting of (their) charms. But that they abstain is better for them. God is hearing, knowing.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical exegetes treat the partitive preposition 'min' (some of) in the readings of Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy as an explanatory clarification of what is already implied by context in the Uthmanic text.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Both al-Tabari (citing al-Sha'bi for Ubayy bin Ka'b) and Ibn Kathir (citing Sa'id bin Jubayr for Abdullah bin Mas'ud) invoke this non-Uthmanic preposition to qualify an otherwise unqualified legal permission in the Uthmanic rasm.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: حدثنا ابن حميد، قال: ثنا جرير، عن مغيرة، عن الشعبي ( أَنْ يَضَعْنَ ثِيَابَهُنَّ غَيْرَ مُتَبَرِّجَاتٍ بِزِينَةٍ ) قال: تضع الجلباب المرأة التي قد عجزت ولم تزوّج. قال الشعبيّ: فإن أُبيّ بن كعب يقرأ " أنْ يَضَعْنَ مِنْ ثِيَابِهِنَّ".
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: *Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Al-Sha'bi:* {that they lay down their clothes, (as long as there is) no flaunting of (their) charms}, he said: 'The woman who has grown old and does not marry lays down her outer cloak (jilbab).' Al-Sha'bi said: 'For indeed Ubayy bin Ka'b recites: "that they lay down some of their clothes [min thiyabihinna]."'
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: فإن أُبيّ بن كعب يقرأ " أنْ يَضَعْنَ مِنْ ثِيَابِهِنَّ"
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: Ubayy bin Ka'b recites: "that they lay down some of their clothes [min thiyabihinna]."

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقال سعيد بن جبير وغيره ، في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود : " أن يضعن من ثيابهن " وهو الجلباب من فوق الخمار فلا بأس أن يضعن عند غريب أو غيره ، بعد أن يكون عليها خمار صفيق .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Sa'id bin Jubayr and others said: "In the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud it is: 'that they lay down some of their clothes (min thiyabihinna),' which is the outer cloak (Jilbab) over the headcover (Khimar), so there is no harm if they lay it down in the presence of a stranger or others, provided she is wearing a thick Khimar."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود : " أن يضعن من ثيابهن "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: In the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud it is: 'that they lay down some of their clothes (min thiyabihinna),'

variants.short_title: 26:20 — Moses Was 'Of the Ignorant' vs. 'Gone Astray'
variants.plain_english_hook: When Moses explains his past killing of the Egyptian, the standard Quran has him say 'I was one of those who had gone astray,' whereas Ibn Mas'ud's codex read 'one of the ignorant.'
variants.title: Substitution of 'The Ignorant' (Al-Jāhilīn) for 'Gone Astray' (Al-Ḍāllīn) in 26:20
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 26:20, Moses replies to Pharaoh regarding his killing of the Egyptian: 'قَالَ فَعَلۡتُهَآ إِذٗا وَأَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ' ('He said, ‘I did it when I was one of those who had gone astray,'). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record via Ibn Jurayj and al-Dahhak that in the recitation (ḥarf) of Abdullah bin Mas'ud it read 'وَأَنَا مِنَ الْجَاهِلِينَ' ('when I was one of the ignorant'), avoiding attributing 'going astray' (ḍalāl) to Moses.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: when I was one of those who had gone astray
variants.variant_target_english: when I was one of the ignorant
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: قَالَ فَعَلۡتُهَآ إِذٗا وَأَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: He said, ‘I did it when I was one of those who had gone astray,
variants.variant_full_arabic: قَالَ فَعَلۡتُهَآ إِذٗا وَأَنَا مِنَ الْجَاهِلِينَ
variants.variant_full_english: He said, ‘I did it when I was one of the ignorant,

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Exegetes harmonize the two readings by interpreting 'al-ḍāllīn' in the Uthmanic text not as religious misguidance, but as meaning 'unaware/ignorant of the fatal consequence' (al-jāhilīn), treating Ibn Mas'ud's wording as an explanatory synonym.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Both al-Tabari (citing Ibn Jurayj and al-Dahhak) and Ibn Kathir explicitly attest 'وَأَنَا مِنَ الْجَاهِلِينَ' as the wording of Ibn Mas'ud's recitation (في قراءة ابن مسعود / في حرف ابن مسعود).

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: حُدثت عن الحسين, قال: سمعت أبا معاذ يقول: أخبرنا عبيد, قال: سمعت الضحاك يقول في قوله:  وَأَنْتَ مِنَ الْكَافِرِينَ  فقال موسى: لم أكفر, ولكن فعلتها وأنا من الضالين. وفي حرف ابن مسعود: " فعلتها إذا وأنا من الجاهلين ".
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: {while you were one of the ingrates} - Musa said: "I did not disbelieve, but I did it when I was one of those who had gone astray." And in the reading (harf) of Ibn Mas'ud: "I did it then when I was one of the ignorant."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وفي حرف ابن مسعود: " فعلتها إذا وأنا من الجاهلين "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: And in the reading (harf) of Ibn Mas'ud: "I did it then when I was one of the ignorant."

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: قال ابن عباس ، رضي الله عنهما ، ومجاهد ، وقتادة ، والضحاك ، وغيرهم : ( وأنا من الضالين ) أي : الجاهلين . قال ابن جريج : وهي كذلك في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, and others said: {when I was one of those who go astray} means: 'of the ignorant (min al-jahilin).' Ibn Jurayj said: 'It is like this in the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him.'

variants.short_title: 33:50 — Adding 'And' Before 'Those Who Emigrated'
variants.plain_english_hook: By adding a single 'and' (wa-allātī) before 'those who emigrated with you,' Ibn Mas'ud's codex made all female emigrants lawful for the Prophet to marry, not just emigrating cousins.
variants.title: Addition of the Conjunction Wāw ('And Those Who Emigrated') in 33:50
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 33:50, the Uthmanic text restricts the cousins lawful for the Prophet to marry with the relative clause 'وَبَنَاتِ خَٰلَٰتِكَ ٱلَّـٰتِي هَاجَرۡنَ مَعَكَ' ('and maternal aunts, who have emigrated with you'). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record that Abdullah bin Mas'ud recited 'وَبَنَاتِ خَالَاتِكَ وَاللَّاتِي هَاجَرْنَ مَعَكَ' ('and maternal aunts, and those who have emigrated with you') with the conjunction wāw (and), which al-Dahhak explained as establishing a separate category encompassing all emigrating women beyond the Prophet's cousins.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: and maternal aunts, who have emigrated with you
variants.variant_target_english: and maternal aunts, and those who have emigrated with you
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ إِنَّآ أَحۡلَلۡنَا لَكَ أَزۡوَٰجَكَ ٱلَّـٰتِيٓ ءَاتَيۡتَ أُجُورَهُنَّ وَمَا مَلَكَتۡ يَمِينُكَ مِمَّآ أَفَآءَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡكَ وَبَنَاتِ عَمِّكَ وَبَنَاتِ عَمَّـٰتِكَ وَبَنَاتِ خَالِكَ وَبَنَاتِ خَٰلَٰتِكَ ٱلَّـٰتِي هَاجَرۡنَ مَعَكَ وَٱمۡرَأَةٗ مُّؤۡمِنَةً إِن وَهَبَتۡ نَفۡسَهَا لِلنَّبِيِّ إِنۡ أَرَادَ ٱلنَّبِيُّ أَن يَسۡتَنكِحَهَا خَالِصَةٗ لَّكَ مِن دُونِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَۗ قَدۡ عَلِمۡنَا مَا فَرَضۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ فِيٓ أَزۡوَٰجِهِمۡ وَمَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُهُمۡ لِكَيۡلَا يَكُونَ عَلَيۡكَ حَرَجٞۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورٗا رَّحِيمٗا
variants.uthmanic_full_english: Prophet! Surely We have made lawful for you your wives to whom you have granted their marriage gifts, and what your right (hand) owns from what God has given you, and the daughters of your paternal uncles and paternal aunts, your maternal uncles and maternal aunts, who have emigrated with you, and any believing woman, if she gives herself to the prophet, and if the prophet wishes to take her in marriage. (That is) exclusively for you, apart from the believers – We know what We have made obligatory for them concerning their wives and what their right (hands) own – so that there may be no blame on you. God is forgiving, compassionate.

variants.variant_full_english: Prophet! Surely We have made lawful for you your wives to whom you have granted their marriage gifts, and what your right (hand) owns from what God has given you, and the daughters of your paternal uncles and paternal aunts, your maternal uncles and maternal aunts, and those who have emigrated with you, and any believing woman, if she gives herself to the prophet, and if the prophet wishes to take her in marriage. (That is) exclusively for you, apart from the believers – We know what We have made obligatory for them concerning their wives and what their right (hands) own – so that there may be no blame on you. God is forgiving, compassionate.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari and al-Farra' suggest that even with the conjunction wāw in Ibn Mas'ud's reading, Arabic syntax occasionally permits a pleonastic wāw before a descriptive relative clause ('wa-allātī'), preserving the same restriction as the Uthmanic text.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir both record that al-Dahhak bin Muzahim understood Ibn Mas'ud's wāw in its normal conjunctive sense, making all female emigrants a distinct legal category apart from the Prophet's paternal and maternal cousins.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقد ذكر أن ذلك في قراءة ابن مسعود (وَبَنَاتِ خَالاتِكَ وَالَّلاتِي هَاجَرْنَ مَعَكَ) بواو، وذلك وإن كان كذلك في قراءته محتمل أن يكون بمعنى قراءتنا بغير الواو، وذلك أن العرب تدخل الواو في نعت من تقدم ذكره أحيانا، كما قال الشاعر:
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: It is mentioned that in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud, it is: (and the daughters of your maternal aunts, and who have emigrated with you) with a *waw* (and). Even if it is thus in his recitation, it carries the possibility of meaning the same as our recitation without the *waw*. This is because the Arabs sometimes insert the *waw* into the description of what was previously mentioned, as the poet said:
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة ابن مسعود (وَبَنَاتِ خَالاتِكَ وَالَّلاتِي هَاجَرْنَ مَعَكَ) بواو
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud, it is: (and the daughters of your maternal aunts, and who have emigrated with you) with a *waw* (and)

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: ورواه الترمذي في جامعه . وهكذا قال أبو رزين وقتادة : إن المراد : من هاجر معه إلى المدينة . وفي رواية عن قتادة : ( اللاتي هاجرن معك ) أي : أسلمن . وقال الضحاك : قرأ ابن مسعود : " واللاتي هاجرن معك " .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Ibn Abi Hatim then recorded it from the *Hadith* of Isma'il bin Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, from her with a similar meaning. At-Tirmidhi also recorded it in his *Jami'*. This was also stated by Abu Razin and Qatadah: that the intended meaning is those who emigrated with him to Al-Madinah. In another narration from Qatadah: (who have emigrated with you) means: who embraced Islam. Ad-Dahhak said: Ibn Mas'ud recited it as: "And those who emigrated with you."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وقال الضحاك : قرأ ابن مسعود : " واللاتي هاجرن معك "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: Ad-Dahhak said: Ibn Mas'ud recited it as: "And those who emigrated with you."

variants.short_title: 34:14 — Jinn Toiling a Full Year After Solomon's Death
variants.plain_english_hook: In the story of Solomon's death, Ibn Mas'ud's reading contains an extended narrative stating that the jinn labored for a full year after he died before people realized the jinn had lied.
variants.title: Extended Narrative Clause on Solomon's Death and the Jinn in 34:14
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 34:14, the Uthmanic text concisely states 'فَلَمَّا خَرَّ تَبَيَّنَتِ ٱلۡجِنُّ أَن لَّوۡ كَانُواْ يَعۡلَمُونَ ٱلۡغَيۡبَ مَا لَبِثُواْ فِي ٱلۡعَذَابِ ٱلۡمُهِينِ' ('When he fell down, it became clear to the jinn that, if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment.'). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record via al-Suddi that in the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud this clause read 'فَمَكَثُوا يَدْأَبُونَ لَهُ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَوْتِهِ حَوْلًا كَامِلًا فَأَيْقَنَ النَّاسُ عِنْدَ ذَلِكَ أَنَّ الْجِنَّ كَانُوا يَكْذِبُونَهُمْ وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ عَلِمُوا الْغَيْبَ لَعَلِمُوا بِمَوْتِ سُلَيْمَانَ وَلَمْ يَلْبَثُوا فِي الْعَذَابِ سَنَةً يَعْمَلُونَ لَهُ', explicitly stating that the jinn toiled for a full year after Solomon's death and that mankind realized the jinn had been lying.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Commentators treat this extended passage in Ibn Mas'ud's reading as a narrative commentary (tafsīr) clarifying how long Solomon leaned on his staff and how mankind realized the jinn did not know the unseen.

variants.short_title: 36:8 — Chains Placed 'On Their Right Hands' vs. 'Necks'
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran says 'We have placed chains on their necks,' Abdullah bin Mas'ud's reading says 'We have placed chains on their right hands.'
variants.title: Substitution of 'On Their Right Hands' (Fī Aymānihim) for 'On Their Necks' in 36:8
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 36:8, the Uthmanic text reads 'إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَا فِيٓ أَعۡنَٰقِهِمۡ أَغۡلَٰلٗا فَهِيَ إِلَى ٱلۡأَذۡقَانِ' ('Surely We have placed chains on their necks, and it (reaches up) to the chin'). Al-Tabari and al-Farra' record that in the recitation (ḥarf) of Abdullah bin Mas'ud this verse read 'إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا فِي أَيْمَانِهِمْ أَغْلَالًا فَهِيَ إِلَى الْأَذْقَانِ' ('Surely We have placed chains on their right hands, and it (reaches up) to the chin').
variants.uthmanic_target_english: on their necks
variants.variant_target_english: on their right hands
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَا فِيٓ أَعۡنَٰقِهِمۡ أَغۡلَٰلٗا فَهِيَ إِلَى ٱلۡأَذۡقَانِ فَهُم مُّقۡمَحُونَ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: Surely We have placed chains on their necks, and it (reaches up) to the chin, and so they (are forced to) hold their heads up.
variants.variant_full_arabic: إِنَّا جَعَلۡنَا فِي أَيْمَانِهِمْ أَغۡلَٰلٗا فَهِيَ إِلَى ٱلۡأَذۡقَانِ فَهُم مُّقۡمَحُونَ
variants.variant_full_english: Surely We have placed chains on their right hands, and it (reaches up) to the chin, and so they (are forced to) hold their heads up.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari and al-Farra' explain that because an iron collar (ghull) binds a prisoner's hands and neck together up to the chin, the Uthmanic text mentions the necks while leaving the hands implicit, whereas Ibn Mas'ud's reading mentions the right hands while leaving the necks implicit.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari relies directly on Ibn Mas'ud's variant 'فِي أَيْمَانِهِمْ' to explain why the feminine singular pronoun 'fahiya' ('and it reaches up to the chin') in the Uthmanic text refers to the unmentioned 'right hands' (aymān).

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: يقول تعالى ذكره: إنا جعلنا أيمان هؤلاء الكفار مغلولة إلى أعناقهم بالأغلال، فلا تُبسط بشيء من الخيرات. وهي في قراءة عبد الله فيما ذُكر (إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا فِي أَيْمَانِهِمْ أَغْلالا فَهِيَ إِلَى الأذْقَانِ) وقوله ( إِلَى الأذْقَانِ ) يعني: فأيمانهم مجموعة بالأغلال في أعناقهم، فكُني عن الأيمان، ولم يجر لها ذكر لمعرفة السامعين بمعنى الكلام، وأن الأغلال إذا كانت في الأعناق لم تكن إلا وأيدي المغلولين مجموعة بها إليها ، فاستغنى بذكر كون الأغلال في الأعناق من ذكر الأيمان، كما قال الشاعر:
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: He, whose mention is exalted, says: Surely We have made the right hands of these disbelievers tied to their necks with chains, so they cannot be extended [to perform] any good deeds. And it is [recited] in the reading of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud], according to what was mentioned: "Surely We have placed chains on their right hands, and it (reaches up) to the chin."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وهي في قراءة عبد الله فيما ذُكر (إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا فِي أَيْمَانِهِمْ أَغْلالا فَهِيَ إِلَى الأذْقَانِ)
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: And it is [recited] in the reading of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud], according to what was mentioned: "Surely We have placed chains on their right hands, and it (reaches up) to the chin."

variants.short_title: 36:35 — 'And From What Their Hands Made' vs. 'Not Made'
variants.plain_english_hook: In 36:35, scholars debated whether 'wa-mā' means 'what their hands made' or 'their hands did NOT make it'; Ibn Mas'ud's codex read 'wa-mimmā' ('and from what their hands made').
variants.title: Addition of the Preposition Min ('Wa-Mimmā ʿAmilathu Aydīhim') in 36:35
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 36:35, the Uthmanic text reads 'لِيَأۡكُلُواْ مِن ثَمَرِهِۦ وَمَا عَمِلَتۡهُ أَيۡدِيهِمۡۚ' ('so that they may eat from its fruit and what their hands have made.'), where the particle 'mā' was interpreted by Ibn Abbas and Qatadah as a negation ('and their hands did not make it') and by al-Tabari as a relative pronoun ('and what their hands have made'). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record that Abdullah bin Mas'ud recited 'وَمِمَّا عَمِلَتْهُ أَيْدِيهِمْ' ('and from what their hands have made'), adding the preposition 'min' so that human cultivation is unambiguously affirmed.

variants.variant_target_english: and from what their hands have made
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: لِيَأۡكُلُواْ مِن ثَمَرِهِۦ وَمَا عَمِلَتۡهُ أَيۡدِيهِمۡۚ أَفَلَا يَشۡكُرُونَ

variants.variant_full_english: so that they may eat from its fruit and from what their hands have made. Will they not be thankful?

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari argues that the Uthmanic 'wa-mā' is a relative pronoun conjoined in the genitive case to 'its fruit' ('from its fruit and [from] that which their hands have made'), matching the meaning of Ibn Mas'ud's 'wa-mimmā.'
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Ibn Kathir notes that while Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, and the Kufan canonical readers (who drop the pronoun '-hu' to read 'wa-mā ʿamilat aydīhim') favored the negative meaning ('their hands did not make it'), al-Tabari relied on Ibn Mas'ud's non-Uthmanic reading 'wa-mimmā ʿamilathu' to argue for the affirmative meaning.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: يقول تعالى ذكره: أنشأنا هذه الجنات في هذه الأرض ليأكل عبادي من ثمره، وما عملت أيديهم يقول: ليأكلوا من ثمر الجنات التي أنشأنا لهم، وما عملت أيديهم مما غرسوا هم وزرعوا. و " ما " التي في قوله ( وَمَا عَمِلَتْهُ أَيْدِيهِمْ ) في موضع خفض عطفًا على الثمر، بمعنى: ومن الذي عملت؛ وهي في قراءة عبد الله فيما ذُكر: (وَممَّا عَمِلَتْهُ) بالهاء على هذا المعنى ، فالهاء في قراءتنا مضمرة، لأن العرب تضمرها أحيانًا، وتظهرها في صلات: من، وما، والذي. ولو قيل: " ما " بمعنى المصدر كان مذهبًا، فيكون معنى الكلام: ومن عمل أيديهم ، ولو قيل: إنها بمعنى الجحد ولا موضع لها كان أيضًا مذهبا، فيكون معنى الكلام: ليأكلوا من ثمره ولم تعمله أيديهم. وقوله ( أَفَلا يَشْكُرُونَ ) يقول: أفلا يشكر هؤلاء القوم الذين رزقناهم هذا الرزق من هذه الأرض الميتة التي أحييناها لهم مَنْ رزقهم ذلك وأنعم عليهم به؟
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: And the "ma" in His saying *{and what their hands have made}* is in a position of genitive (*khafd*) by conjunction (*'atf*) with the fruit, meaning: 'and from that which they have made'; and it is in the recitation of 'Abdullah, according to what was mentioned: *{wa mimma 'amilathu}* ('and from what they made [it]') with the 'ha'' based on this meaning. Thus, the 'ha'' in our recitation is implicit (*mudmarah*), because the Arabs sometimes make it implicit, and they make it apparent in the relative clauses (*silat*) of 'man', 'ma', and 'al-ladhi'.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وهي في قراءة عبد الله فيما ذُكر: (وَممَّا عَمِلَتْهُ) بالهاء على هذا المعنى
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: and it is in the recitation of 'Abdullah, according to what was mentioned: *{wa mimma 'amilathu}* ('and from what they made [it]')

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: واختار ابن جرير - بل جزم به ، ولم يحك غيره إلا احتمالا - أن " ما " في قوله : ( وما عملته أيديهم ) بمعنى : " الذي " ، تقديره : ليأكلوا من ثمره ومما عملته أيديهم ، أي : غرسوه ونصبوه ، قال : وهي كذلك في قراءة ابن مسعود .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Ibn Jarir, however, understood the word Ma to mean Alladhi (i.e., a relative pronoun). In this case, the meaning of the Ayah would be that they eat from the fruits provided by Allah's bounty and from what their own hands have worked [wa-mimma 'amilathu aydihim], i.e., by planting the seeds and tending the plants. He said: And it is likewise in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: تقديره : ليأكلوا من ثمره ومما عملته أيديهم ، أي : غرسوه ونصبوه ، قال : وهي كذلك في قراءة ابن مسعود
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: from what their own hands have worked [wa-mimma 'amilathu aydihim], i.e., by planting the seeds and tending the plants. He said: And it is likewise in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud.

variants.short_title: Ibn Mas'ud's Variant on the Sun's Course in 36:38
variants.plain_english_hook: In Sahih al-Bukhari 7424, Sahih Muslim 112, and Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Abdullah bin Mas'ud recites Surah 36:38 with a different wording for the sun's resting place ('wa-dhalika mustaqarrun laha').
variants.title: Divergent Recitations of 'Mustaqarr' in Surah Ya-Sin 36:38 in Ibn Mas'ud's Codex
variants.diff_summary: Whereas the Uthmanic Mushaf reads 'wa-sh-shamsu tajrī li-mustaqarrin lahā dhālika taqdīru al-'azīzi al-'alīm' ('And the sun: it runs to a dwelling place (appointed) for it. That is the decree of the Mighty, the Knowing.'), Sahih al-Bukhari 7424 and Sahih Muslim 112 record the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud as 'wa-dhālika mustaqarrun lahā' ('and that is a dwelling place for it'). Furthermore, Tafsir Ibn Kathir records that Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas also recited 'wa-sh-shamsu tajrī lā mustaqarra lahā' ('And the sun runs having no resting place for it'), negating the resting place entirely to mean that the sun moves unceasingly day and night.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: And the sun: it runs to a dwelling place (appointed) for it.
variants.variant_target_english: And the sun: it runs, and that is a dwelling place (appointed) for it.
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: وَٱلشَّمۡسُ تَجۡرِي لِمُسۡتَقَرّٖ لَّهَاۚ ذَٰلِكَ تَقۡدِيرُ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡعَلِيمِ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: And the sun: it runs to a dwelling place (appointed) for it. That is the decree of the Mighty, the Knowing.
variants.variant_full_arabic: وَالشَّمْسُ تَجْرِي وَذَلِكَ مُسْتَقَرٌّ لَهَاۚ ذَٰلِكَ تَقۡدِيرُ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡعَلِيمِ
variants.variant_full_english: And the sun: it runs, and that is a dwelling place (appointed) for it. That is the decree of the Mighty, the Knowing.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Ibn Kathir harmonizes the Uthmanic reading ('to a resting place for it') with the negative variant attributed to Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas ('no resting place for it') by suggesting the former refers to its ultimate end on the Day of Judgment while the latter refers to its continuous daily motion.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: The existence of three distinct wordings in the primary sources—Uthmanic 'li-mustaqarrin lahā', Bukhari/Muslim's 'wa-dhālika mustaqarrun lahā', and Ibn Kathir's 'lā mustaqarra lahā'—shows substantive consonantal and syntactic variation in how the early Companions transmitted 36:38.

hadiths.transmitted_by: Abu Dharr / Ibrahim at-Taymi / Al-Amash
hadiths.hadith_arabic: وَحَدَّثَنَا أَبُو بَكْرِ بْنُ أَبِي شَيْبَةَ، وَأَبُو كُرَيْبٍ - وَاللَّفْظُ لأَبِي كُرَيْبٍ - قَالاَ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو مُعَاوِيَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا الأَعْمَشُ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ التَّيْمِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَبِي ذَرٍّ، قَالَ دَخَلْتُ الْمَسْجِدَ وَرَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم جَالِسٌ فَلَمَّا غَابَتِ الشَّمْسُ قَالَ ‏"‏ يَا أَبَا ذَرٍّ هَلْ تَدْرِي أَيْنَ تَذْهَبُ هَذِهِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ قُلْتُ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَعْلَمُ ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ فَإِنَّهَا تَذْهَبُ فَتَسْتَأْذِنُ فِي السُّجُودِ فَيُؤْذَنُ لَهَا وَكَأَنَّهَا قَدْ قِيلَ لَهَا ارْجِعِي مِنْ حَيْثُ جِئْتِ فَتَطْلُعُ مِنْ مَغْرِبِهَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ ثُمَّ قَرَأَ فِي قِرَاءَةِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ وَذَلِكَ مُسْتَقَرٌّ لَهَا ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Abu Dharr reported:I entered the mosque and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting there. When the sun disappeared (from the sight) he said: O Abu Dharr! Do you know where it goes? He (the narrator) said: Allah and His Apostle know best. He (the Holy Prophet) said. Verily it goes and begs permission, for prostration (to Allah) and the permission is granted to it. Once it would be said: Return to the place whence you came, and then it would rise from its setting place. Then he, after the recitation of 'Abdullah recited it: And that is its appointed term
hadiths.highlight_arabic: ثُمَّ قَرَأَ فِي قِرَاءَةِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ وَذَلِكَ مُسْتَقَرٌّ لَهَا
hadiths.highlight_english: Then he, after the recitation of 'Abdullah recited it: And that is its appointed term

hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Ibrahim: My father said, 'I went to Al-Kufa with Masruq and we entered upon 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud...' 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud recited: 'And the sun runs on its fixed course: and that is its resting place [wa-dhalika mustaqarrun laha]' (36:38).

variants.short_title: 37:68 — 'Their Midday Resting-Place' vs. 'Their Return'
variants.plain_english_hook: Instead of saying 'Then their return (marji'ahum) is to the Furnace,' Abdullah bin Mas'ud recited 'Then their midday resting-place (maqīlahum / munqalabahum) is to the Furnace.'
variants.title: Substitution of 'Resting-Place' (Maqīlahum / Munqalabahum) for 'Return' in 37:68
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 37:68, the Uthmanic text reads 'ثُمَّ إِنَّ مَرۡجِعَهُمۡ لَإِلَى ٱلۡجَحِيمِ' ('Then their return is to the Furnace.'). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record via al-Suddi and Sufyan al-Thawri that Abdullah bin Mas'ud recited 'ثُمَّ إِنَّ مَقِيلَهُمْ لَإِلَى الْجَحِيمِ' ('Then their midday resting-place is to the Furnace.' — transmitted in Tabari's print as 'مُنْقَلَبَهُمْ' 'their place of return'), which Ibn Mas'ud paired with 25:24 to swear that midday on the Day of Resurrection will not pass before the people of Paradise and Hell take their midday rest (qaylūla).
variants.uthmanic_target_english: their return
variants.variant_target_english: their midday resting-place
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: ثُمَّ إِنَّ مَرۡجِعَهُمۡ لَإِلَى ٱلۡجَحِيمِ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: Then their return is to the Furnace.
variants.variant_full_arabic: ثُمَّ إِنَّ مَقِيلَهُمْ لَإِلَى ٱلۡجَحِيمِ
variants.variant_full_english: Then their midday resting-place is to the Furnace.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Commentators treat Ibn Mas'ud's wording as a thematic link between 37:68 and 25:24 ('best abode and fairest place for midday repose [maqīlā]'), illustrating the speed of the Reckoning on Judgment Day.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Ibn Kathir cites both al-Suddi and Sufyan al-Thawri's Kufan chain from Abu Ubaydah bin Abdullah bin Mas'ud confirming that Ibn Mas'ud recited 'ثُمَّ إِنَّ مَقِيلَهُمْ لَإِلَى الْجَحِيمِ' directly after 25:24.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: حدثنا محمد بن الحسين، قال: ثنا أحمد، قال: ثنا أسباط، عن السديّ، في قوله ( ثُمَّ إِنَّ مَرْجِعَهُمْ لإلَى الْجَحِيمِ ) قال: في قراءة عبد الله: " ثم إن منقلبهم لإلى الجحيم " وكان عبد الله يقول: والذي نفسي بيده، لا ينتصف النهار يوم القيامة حتى يَقِيلَ أهلُ الجنة في الجنة، وأهل النار في النار، ثم قال:  أَصْحَابُ الْجَنَّةِ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَيْرٌ مُسْتَقَرًّا وَأَحْسَنُ مَقِيلا
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: In the recitation of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]: "Then their place of return is to the Furnace." And 'Abdullah used to say: "By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, midday on the Day of Resurrection will not arrive until the people of Paradise take their midday rest in Paradise, and the people of the Fire in the Fire." Then he said: "The dwellers of Paradise will, on that Day, have the best abode, and have the fairest of places for repose."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة عبد الله: " ثم إن منقلبهم لإلى الجحيم "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: In the recitation of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]: "Then their place of return is to the Furnace."

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقال السدي في قراءة عبد الله : " ثم إن مقيلهم لإلى الجحيم " وكان عبد الله يقول : والذي نفسي بيده لا ينتصف النهار يوم القيامة حتى يقيل أهل الجنة في الجنة ، وأهل النار في النار . ثم قرأ : ( أصحاب الجنة يومئذ خير مستقرا وأحسن مقيلا ) [ الفرقان : 24 ] .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: As-Suddi said concerning the recitation of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]: "Then their resting-place is to the Furnace." 'Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say: "By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, midday on the Day of Resurrection will not come until the people of Paradise will rest in Paradise and the people of Hell will rest in Hell." Then he recited:
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وقال السدي في قراءة عبد الله : " ثم إن مقيلهم لإلى الجحيم "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: As-Suddi said concerning the recitation of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]: "Then their resting-place is to the Furnace."

variants.variant_arabic: ثُمَّ إِنَّ مَقِيلَهُمْ لَإِلَى ٱلۡجَحِيمِ
variants.variant_english: Then their midday resting-place is to the Furnace.
variants.hadith_arabic: حدثنا محمد بن الحسين، قال: ثنا أحمد، قال: ثنا أسباط، عن السديّ، في قوله ( ثُمَّ إِنَّ مَرْجِعَهُمْ لإلَى الْجَحِيمِ ) قال: في قراءة عبد الله: " ثم إن منقلبهم لإلى الجحيم " وكان عبد الله يقول: والذي نفسي بيده، لا ينتصف النهار يوم القيامة حتى يَقِيلَ أهلُ الجنة في الجنة، وأهل النار في النار، ثم قال:  أَصْحَابُ الْجَنَّةِ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَيْرٌ مُسْتَقَرًّا وَأَحْسَنُ مَقِيلا
variants.hadith_english: In the recitation of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]: "Then their place of return is to the Furnace." And 'Abdullah used to say: "By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, midday on the Day of Resurrection will not arrive until the people of Paradise take their midday rest in Paradise, and the people of the Fire in the Fire." Then he said: "The dwellers of Paradise will, on that Day, have the best abode, and have the fairest of places for repose."

variants.short_title: 39:53 — God Forgives All Sins 'For Whomever He Wills'
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran declares unconditionally that 'God forgives all sins,' the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud added the theological qualification 'for whomever He wills.'
variants.title: Addition of 'For Whomever He Wills' (Li-Man Yashā'u) in 39:53
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 39:53, the Uthmanic text proclaims 'إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَغۡفِرُ ٱلذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًاۚ' ('Surely God forgives sins – all (of them).'). Al-Tabari records that in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud, this promise is qualified by the phrase addition 'لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ' ('إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ' — 'Surely God forgives sins – all (of them) – for whomever He wills.'), harmonizing the verse with 4:48.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: Surely God forgives sins – all (of them).
variants.variant_target_arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ
variants.variant_target_english: Surely God forgives sins – all (of them) – for whomever He wills.
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: ۞قُلۡ يَٰعِبَادِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسۡرَفُواْ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ لَا تَقۡنَطُواْ مِن رَّحۡمَةِ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَغۡفِرُ ٱلذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًاۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلۡغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: Say: ‘My servants who have acted wantonly against themselves! Do not despair of the mercy of God. Surely God forgives sins – all (of them). Surely He – He is the Forgiving, the Compassionate.
variants.variant_full_arabic: ۞قُلۡ يَٰعِبَادِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسۡرَفُواْ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ لَا تَقۡنَطُواْ مِن رَّحۡمَةِ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلۡغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
variants.variant_full_english: Say: ‘My servants who have acted wantonly against themselves! Do not despair of the mercy of God. Surely God forgives sins – all (of them) – for whomever He wills. Surely He – He is the Forgiving, the Compassionate.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Theologians and commentators explain that the unconditional wording in the Uthmanic text applies to those who repent, while Ibn Mas'ud's addition 'for whomever He wills' was an interpretive gloss aligning 39:53 with 4:48.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari notes that early scholars who restricted the verse to Muslims cited its written presence in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud (وهي كذلك في مصحف عبد الله) as direct textual support.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقال آخرون: بل عني بذلك أهل الإسلام, وقالوا: تأويل الكلام: إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا لمن يشاء, قالوا: وهي كذلك في مصحف عبد الله, وقالوا: إنما نـزلت هذه الآية في قوم صدّهم المشركون عن الهجرة وفتنوهم, فأشفقوا أن لا يكون لهم توبة.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: And others said: Rather, it means the people of Islam. They said: The interpretation of the statement is: 'Indeed, Allah forgives all sins for whomever He wills.' They said: And it is so in the Mushaf of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]. And they said: This Ayah was only revealed regarding a people whom the polytheists prevented from migrating and put them to trial (tortured them), so they feared that they would have no repentance.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا لمن يشاء, قالوا: وهي كذلك في مصحف عبد الله
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: The interpretation of the statement is: 'Indeed, Allah forgives all sins for whomever He wills.' They said: And it is so in the Mushaf of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud].

variants.short_title: 42:2 — Omitting the Letter ʿAyn from 'ʿAyn Sīn Qāf'
variants.plain_english_hook: In the mysterious opening letters of Surah al-Shura (42:1-2), Ibn Abbas and the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud omitted the letter ʿAyn, reading only 'Ḥā Mīm. Sīn Qāf.'
variants.title: Omission of the Disjointed Letter ʿAyn ('Sīn Qāf' for 'ʿAyn Sīn Qāf') in 42:2
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 42:2, the Uthmanic text consists of the three disjointed letters 'عٓسٓقٓ' ('‘Ayn Sīn Qāf.'). Al-Tabari records that Ibn Abbas recited this verse as 'سٓقٓ' ('Sīn Qāf.') without the letter ʿAyn ('بغير عين'), and notes that it was likewise written without an ʿAyn in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: ‘Ayn Sīn Qāf.
variants.variant_target_english: Sīn Qāf.
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: عٓسٓقٓ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: ‘Ayn Sīn Qāf.
variants.variant_full_arabic: سٓقٓ
variants.variant_full_english: Sīn Qāf.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical scholars note that all canonical reciters across the Islamic cities follow the Uthmanic rasm 'ʿAyn Sīn Qāf,' treating the omission of ʿAyn attributed to Ibn Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud's codex as an uncanonical anomaly.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari explicitly documents that both Ibn Abbas's oral recitation and the written Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud lacked the letter ʿAyn in 42:2 ('من غير عين').

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وذُكر عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرأه " حم. سق " بغير عين, ويقول: إن السين: عمر كل فرقة كائنة وإن القاف: كل جماعة كائنة; ويقول: إن عليا إنما كان يعلم العين بها. وذُكر أن ذلك في مصحف عبد الله على مثل الذي ذكر عن ابن عباس من قراءته من غير عين.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: And it was mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite it: "Hā Mīm. Sīn Qāf" without an ‘Ayn, and he would say: "Indeed, the Sīn is the lifespan of every faction that comes into being, and the Qāf is every community that comes into being." And he would say: "Indeed, 'Ali only knew the ‘Ayn by means of it." And it was mentioned that this is in the Mushaf of 'Abdullah (bin Mas'ud), similar to what was mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas in his recitation without an ‘Ayn.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وذُكر أن ذلك في مصحف عبد الله على مثل الذي ذكر عن ابن عباس من قراءته من غير عين.

variants.short_title: 43:45 — Ask 'Those to Whom We Sent' Our Messengers
variants.plain_english_hook: Instead of telling Muhammad to ask the departed 'messengers We sent before you,' Ibn Mas'ud's reading tells him to ask 'those to whom We sent Our messengers before you.'
variants.title: Recitation of 'Ask Those to Whom We Sent Our Messengers' in 43:45
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 43:45, the Uthmanic text commands the Prophet: 'وَسۡـَٔلۡ مَنۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مِن قَبۡلِكَ مِن رُّسُلِنَآ' ('Ask those of Our messengers whom We sent before you'). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir report via Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and al-Dahhak that Abdullah bin Mas'ud recited 'وَاسْأَلِ الَّذِينَ أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْهِمْ قَبْلَكَ رُسُلَنَا' ('Ask those to whom We sent Our messengers before you'), directing the inquiry to the living People of the Book rather than past prophets.
variants.uthmanic_target_arabic: وَسۡـَٔلۡ مَنۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مِن قَبۡلِكَ مِن رُّسُلِنَآ
variants.uthmanic_target_english: Ask those of Our messengers whom We sent before you
variants.variant_target_arabic: وَاسْأَلِ الَّذِينَ أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْهِمْ قَبْلَكَ رُسُلَنَا
variants.variant_target_english: Ask those to whom We sent Our messengers before you
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: وَسۡـَٔلۡ مَنۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مِن قَبۡلِكَ مِن رُّسُلِنَآ أَجَعَلۡنَا مِن دُونِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ ءَالِهَةٗ يُعۡبَدُونَ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: Ask those of Our messengers whom We sent before you: Did We appoint any other gods than the Merciful to be served?
variants.variant_full_arabic: وَاسْأَلِ الَّذِينَ أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْهِمْ قَبْلَكَ رُسُلَنَا أَجَعَلۡنَا مِن دُونِ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ ءَالِهَةٗ يُعۡبَدُونَ
variants.variant_full_english: Ask those to whom We sent Our messengers before you: Did We appoint any other gods than the Merciful to be served?

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Ibn Kathir remarks that this wording transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud appears to be an explanatory paraphrase (tafsīr) rather than a canonical recitation (tilāwa), resolving how the Prophet could question long-deceased messengers.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Four independent early authorities in Tabari (Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and al-Dahhak) explicitly transmit this wording as 'the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud' (قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود).

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: حدثني عبد الأعلى بن واصل, قال: ثنا يحيى بن آدم, عن ابن عيينة, عن ابن أبي نجيح, عن مجاهد قال: في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود " وَاسأَلْ الَّذِينَ أرْسَلْنا إلَيْهِمْ قَبْلَكَ رُسُلنا ".
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: *'Abd al-A'la bin Wasil narrated to me, he said: Yahya bin Adam narrated to us, from Ibn 'Uyaynah, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said:* In the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud [it is]: "And ask those to whom We sent Our messengers before you."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود " وَاسأَلْ الَّذِينَ أرْسَلْنا إلَيْهِمْ قَبْلَكَ رُسُلنا "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: In the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud [it is]: "And ask those to whom We sent Our messengers before you."

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقوله : ( واسأل من أرسلنا من قبلك من رسلنا أجعلنا من دون الرحمن آلهة يعبدون ) ؟ أي : جميع الرسل دعوا إلى ما دعوت الناس إليه من عبادة الله وحده لا شريك له ، ونهوا عن عبادة الأصنام والأنداد ، كقوله : ( ولقد بعثنا في كل أمة رسولا أن اعبدوا الله واجتنبوا الطاغوت ) [ النحل : 36 ] . قال مجاهد : في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود : " واسأل الذين أرسلنا إليهم قبلك رسلنا " . وهكذا حكاه قتادة والضحاك والسدي ، عن ابن مسعود . وهذا كأنه تفسير لا تلاوة ، والله أعلم .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Mujahid said: "In the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud it is: 'And ask those to whom We sent Our Messengers before you.'" This was also narrated by Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, and As-Suddi, from Ibn Mas'ud. And this seems to be an explanation, not a recitation, and Allah knows best.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: قال مجاهد : في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود : " واسأل الذين أرسلنا إليهم قبلك رسلنا "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: Mujahid said: "In the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud it is: 'And ask those to whom We sent Our Messengers before you.'"

variants.short_title: 43:58 — 'Are Our Gods Better, or Is This Man?'
variants.plain_english_hook: Instead of the polytheists asking 'Are our gods better, or is he?' (referring to Jesus), Ubayy bin Ka'b and Ibn Mas'ud read 'or is this (man)?' (referring to Muhammad).
variants.title: Substitution of 'Or Is This (Man)?' (Am Hādhā) for 'Or Is He?' (Am Huwa) in 43:58
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 43:58, following the mention of Jesus in 43:57, the Uthmanic text quotes the Meccan polytheists asking 'ءَأَٰلِهَتُنَا خَيۡرٌ أَمۡ هُوَۚ' ('‘Are our gods better, or is he?’'). Al-Tabari records from Qatadah that in the reading (ḥarf) of Ubayy bin Ka'b—and in Ibn Kathir from Qatadah as the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud—this verse read 'أَآلِهَتُنَا خَيْرٌ أَمْ هَذَا' ('‘Are our gods better, or is this (man)?’'), shifting the comparison from Jesus to Muhammad.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: ‘Are our gods better, or is he?’
variants.variant_target_english: ‘Are our gods better, or is this (man)?’
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: وَقَالُوٓاْ ءَأَٰلِهَتُنَا خَيۡرٌ أَمۡ هُوَۚ مَا ضَرَبُوهُ لَكَ إِلَّا جَدَلَۢاۚ بَلۡ هُمۡ قَوۡمٌ خَصِمُونَ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: and they say, ‘Are our gods better, or is he?’ They only cite him to you as a (matter of) dispute. Yes! They are a contentious people.
variants.variant_full_arabic: وَقَالُوٓاْ أَآلِهَتُنَا خَيْرٌ أَمْ هَذَاۚ مَا ضَرَبُوهُ لَكَ إِلَّا جَدَلَۢاۚ بَلۡ هُمۡ قَوۡمٌ خَصِمُونَ
variants.variant_full_english: and they say, ‘Are our gods better, or is this (man)?’ They only cite him to you as a (matter of) dispute. Yes! They are a contentious people.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Commentators explain that under the Uthmanic reading 'or is he,' the Quraysh compared their idols to Jesus (since Christians worshipped him), whereas 'or is this' in Ubayy and Ibn Mas'ud's reading was viewed as an interpretive gloss referring either to Muhammad or demonstratively to Jesus.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir, Qatadah explicitly cites the variant demonstrative pronoun 'أَمْ هَذَا' ('or is this?') and adds that the speakers meant Muhammad rather than Jesus.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: * ذكر الرواية بذلك: حدثنا ابن عبد الأعلى, قال: ثنا ابن ثور عن معمر, عن قتادة أن في حرف أبي بن كعب " وقالوا أآلهتنا خير أم هذا " يعنون محمدا صَلَّى الله عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّم.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: It was mentioned that this is in the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b: "Are our gods better or is this?"
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في حرف أبي بن كعب " وقالوا أآلهتنا خير أم هذا " يعنون محمدا
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b: "Are our gods better or is this?"

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقوله : ( وقالوا أآلهتنا خير أم هو ) : قال قتادة : يقولون : آلهتنا خير منه . وقال قتادة : قرأ ابن مسعود : " وقالوا أآلهتنا خير أم هذا " ، يعنون محمدا - صلى الله عليه وسلم - .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Qatadah said, "They were saying, 'Our gods are better than him.'" Qatadah said; "Ibn Mas'ud recited it: 'Are our gods better or is this (person)?' meaning Muhammad, peace be upon him."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وقال قتادة : قرأ ابن مسعود : " وقالوا أآلهتنا خير أم هذا "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: Qatadah said; "Ibn Mas'ud recited it: 'Are our gods better or is this (person)?' meaning Muhammad, peace be upon him."

variants.variant_arabic: وَقَالُوٓاْ أَآلِهَتُنَا خَيْرٌ أَمْ هَذَاۚ مَا ضَرَبُوهُ لَكَ إِلَّا جَدَلَۢاۚ بَلۡ هُمۡ قَوۡمٌ خَصِمُونَ
variants.variant_english: and they say, ‘Are our gods better, or is this (man)?’ They only cite him to you as a (matter of) dispute. Yes! They are a contentious people.
variants.hadith_arabic: * ذكر الرواية بذلك: حدثنا ابن عبد الأعلى, قال: ثنا ابن ثور عن معمر, عن قتادة أن في حرف أبي بن كعب " وقالوا أآلهتنا خير أم هذا " يعنون محمدا صَلَّى الله عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّم.
variants.hadith_english: It was mentioned that this is in the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b: "Are our gods better or is this?"

variants.short_title: Ibn Mas'ud's Apocopated Reading 'Ya Mali' in 43:77
variants.plain_english_hook: In Sahih al-Bukhari 3230, Abdullah bin Mas'ud recites Surah 43:77 with the final consonant 'kaf' dropped from the angel Malik's name ('wa-nadaw ya Mali' instead of 'wa-nadaw ya Maliku').
variants.title: Apocopated Vocative 'Ya Mali' Without Final 'Kaf' in Surah Az-Zukhruf 43:77
variants.diff_summary: Whereas the Uthmanic Mushaf reads 'wa-nādaw yā Māliku li-yaqḍi 'alaynā rabbuka' ('They will call out, "Master [O Mālik]! Let your Lord finish us off!"'), Sahih al-Bukhari 3230 records that in the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud the final consonant kāf is omitted in an apocopated vocative (tarkhīm): 'wa-nādaw yā Māli' ('They will call out, "O Māli!"'). In the same hadith, Ya'la bin Umayyah testifies that he heard the Prophet on the pulpit reciting the full form 'yā Māliku'.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: They will call out, ‘Master!
variants.variant_target_english: They will call out, ‘O Māli [Master, without final kāf]!
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: وَنَادَوۡاْ يَٰمَٰلِكُ لِيَقۡضِ عَلَيۡنَا رَبُّكَۖ قَالَ إِنَّكُم مَّـٰكِثُونَ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: They will call out, ‘Master! Let your Lord finish us off!’ He will say, ‘Surely you will remain.
variants.variant_full_arabic: وَنَادَوْا يَا مَالِ لِيَقۡضِ عَلَيۡنَا رَبُّكَۖ قَالَ إِنَّكُم مَّـٰكِثُونَ
variants.variant_full_english: They will call out, ‘O Māli [Master, without final kāf]! Let your Lord finish us off!’ He will say, ‘Surely you will remain.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical grammarians and commentators explain 'yā Māli' as an instance of Arabic vocative apocopation (tarkhīm al-munādā), portraying how the exhausted inhabitants of Hell cut off the final letter of Malik's name in distress.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Because dropping the final consonant kāf alters the consonantal skeleton (rasm), Ibn Mas'ud's reading 'yā Māli' could not be accommodated by the Uthmanic rasm (ياملك) and was consequently classified as non-canonical (shādhdh) despite its attestation in Sahih al-Bukhari 3230.

hadiths.transmitted_by: Ya'la bin Umayyah / Sufyan bin Uyaynah
hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ عَمْرٍو، عَنْ عَطَاءٍ، عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَعْلَى، عَنْ أَبِيهِ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقْرَأُ عَلَى الْمِنْبَرِ ‏{‏وَنَادَوْا يَا مَالِكُ‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ سُفْيَانُ فِي قِرَاءَةِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ وَنَادَوْا يَا مَالِ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Yali:I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) reciting the following Verse on the pulpit: "They will call: O Malik...' and Sufyan said that `Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud] recited it: 'They will call: O Mali
hadiths.highlight_arabic: قَالَ سُفْيَانُ فِي قِرَاءَةِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ وَنَادَوْا يَا مَالِ
hadiths.highlight_english: and Sufyan said that `Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud] recited it: 'They will call: O Mali

variants.short_title: Ibn Mas'ud's Reading 'And the Messenger Said' (43:88)
variants.plain_english_hook: In Sahih al-Bukhari 4819, Abdullah bin Mas'ud reads Surah 43:88 as 'And the Messenger said: My Lord!' instead of the Uthmanic 'And his saying: My Lord!', replacing an ambiguous noun with a verb and subject.
variants.title: Substitution of 'Wa-Qala ar-Rasulu Ya Rabbi' for 'Wa-Qilihi Ya Rabbi' in Surah 43:88
variants.diff_summary: Whereas the Uthmanic Mushaf reads 'wa-qīlihi yā rabbi' ('And his saying: My Lord!'), whose grammatical case (genitive wa-qīlihi vs. accusative wa-qīlahu) perplexed classical grammarians due to the absence of an explicit governing verb, Sahih al-Bukhari 4819 and Tafsir Ibn Kathir record that Abdullah bin Mas'ud read 'wa-qāla ar-rasūlu yā rabbi' ('And the Messenger said: My Lord!'). This reading replaces the verbal noun and pronoun suffix ('qīlihi') with a finite verb and explicit subject ('qāla ar-rasūlu', matching the phrasing of Surah Al-Furqan 25:30).
variants.uthmanic_target_english: And his saying: ‘My Lord!
variants.variant_target_english: And the Messenger said: ‘My Lord!
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: وَقِيلِهِۦ يَٰرَبِّ إِنَّ هَـٰٓؤُلَآءِ قَوۡمٞ لَّا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: And his saying: ‘My Lord! Surely these are a people who do not believe.’
variants.variant_full_arabic: وَقَالَ الرَّسُولُ يَا رَبِّ إِنَّ هَـٰٓؤُلَآءِ قَوۡمٞ لَّا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
variants.variant_full_english: And the Messenger said: ‘My Lord! Surely these are a people who do not believe.’

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir cite Ibn Mas'ud's reading ('And the Messenger said: O my Lord') as an exegetical clarification proving that 'his saying' (wa-qīlahu) can be read in the accusative as the object of an implied verb ('he said his saying').
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In Sahih al-Bukhari 4819, the text is explicitly recorded as the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud ('wa-qara'a 'Abdullāh: wa-qāla ar-rasūlu yā rabbi'), representing a distinct consonantal rasm that resolves the syntactic ellipsis of the Uthmanic text.

hadiths.transmitted_by: Imam al-Bukhari
hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا حَجَّاجُ بْنُ مِنْهَالٍ، حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ بْنُ عُيَيْنَةَ، عَنْ عَمْرٍو، عَنْ عَطَاءٍ، عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَعْلَى، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، قَالَ سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقْرَأُ عَلَى الْمِنْبَرِ ‏{‏وَنَادَوْا يَا مَالِكُ لِيَقْضِ عَلَيْنَا رَبُّكَ‏}‏ وَقَالَ قَتَادَةُ مَثَلاً لِلآخِرِينَ عِظَةً ‏لِمَنْ بَعْدَهُمْ.‏ وَقَالَ غَيْرُهُ ‏{‏مُقْرِنِينَ‏}‏ ضَابِطِينَ يُقَالُ فُلاَنٌ مُقْرِنٌ لِفُلاَنٍ ضَابِطٌ لَهُ وَالأَكْوَابُ الأَبَارِيقُ الَّتِي لاَ خَرَاطِيمَ لَهَا ‏{‏أَوَّلُ الْعَابِدِينَ‏}‏ أَىْ مَا كَانَ فَأَنَا أَوَّلُ الأَنِفِينَ وَهُمَا لُغَتَانِ رَجُلٌ عَابِدٌ وَعَبِدٌ وَقَرَأَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ ‏{‏وَقَالَ الرَّسُولُ يَا رَبِّ‏}‏ وَيُقَالُ أَوَّلُ الْعَابِدِينَ الْجَاحِدِينَ مِنْ عَبِدَ يَعْبَدُ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Ya`la:I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) reciting when on the pulpit: 'They will cry, "O Malik (Keeper of Hell) Let your Lord make an end of us." And Qatada said: 'an example for the later ones' means an admonishment for those after them. And 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud] recited: '{wa qala ar-rasulu ya rabbi}' (And the Messenger said, O my Lord).
hadiths.highlight_arabic: وَقَرَأَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ ‏{‏وَقَالَ الرَّسُولُ يَا رَبِّ‏}
hadiths.highlight_english: And 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud] recited: '{wa qala ar-rasulu ya rabbi}' (And the Messenger said, O my Lord).

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقوله : ( وقيله يارب إن هؤلاء قوم لا يؤمنون ) أي : وقال : محمد : قيله ، أي : شكا إلى ربه شكواه من قومه الذين كذبوه ، فقال : يا رب ، إن هؤلاء قوم لا يؤمنون ، كما أخبر تعالى في الآية الأخرى : ( وقال الرسول يارب إن قومي اتخذوا هذا القرآن مهجورا ) . قال البخاري : وقرأ عبد الله - يعني ابن مسعود - : " وقال الرسول يا رب " .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: And His saying: {And his saying: 'My Lord! Surely these are a people who do not believe.'} meaning, Muhammad said his saying, complaining to his Lord about his people who denied him... Al-Bukhari said: "'Abdullah - meaning Ibn Mas'ud - recited: 'And the Messenger said: O my Lord!'"
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: قال البخاري : وقرأ عبد الله - يعني ابن مسعود - : " وقال الرسول يا رب "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: Al-Bukhari said: "'Abdullah - meaning Ibn Mas'ud - recited: 'And the Messenger said: O my Lord!'"

variants.short_title: 56:79 — Declarative 'Mā Yamassuhu' vs. 'Lā Yamassuhu'
variants.plain_english_hook: Jurists debated whether 'lā yamassuhu' forbids the unwashed from touching a Quran or describes angels; Ibn Mas'ud's codex read 'mā yamassuhu' (which can only be a description).
variants.title: Substitution of Negation 'Mā' for 'Lā' in 56:79 ('Mā Yamassuhu Illā al-Muṭahharūn')
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 56:79, the Uthmanic text reads 'لَّا يَمَسُّهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱلۡمُطَهَّرُونَ' ('No one touches it but the purified.'), which jurists debated as either a legal prohibition against touching a Mushaf without ritual ablution or a declarative statement about the angels touching the heavenly Book. Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record from Qatadah that in the reading (ḥarf) of Abdullah bin Mas'ud it read 'مَا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ' ('It is not touched except by the purified.'), using the negative particle 'mā' which in Arabic grammar cannot express a command or prohibition.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: No one touches it but the purified.
variants.variant_target_english: It is not touched except by the purified.
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: لَّا يَمَسُّهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱلۡمُطَهَّرُونَ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: No one touches it but the purified.
variants.variant_full_arabic: مَا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ
variants.variant_full_english: It is not touched except by the purified.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Commentators who interpret 56:79 as a declarative statement about the angels in heaven cite Ibn Mas'ud's 'mā yamassuhu' as confirming that 'lā' in the Uthmanic text is a particle of negation (nafy) rather than prohibition (nahy).
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir, Qatadah explicitly appeals to Ibn Mas'ud's reading 'مَا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ' to argue that the verse describes the heavenly archetype rather than earthly copies, which impure persons can physically touch.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: حدثنا ابن عبد الأعلى، قال: ثنا ابن ثور، عن معمر، عن قتادة، قوله: ( لا يَمَسُّهُ إِلا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ ) قال لا يمسه عند الله إلا المطهرون، فأما في الدنيا فإنه يمسه المجوسيّ النجس، والمنافق الرجس. وقال في حرف ابن مسعود ( ما يَمَسُّهُ إلا المُطَهَّرُونَ ).
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: > No one touches it with Allah except the purified. However, in this life, the impure Zoroastrian and the filthy hypocrite touch it. And he said: In the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud, it is: "It is not touched except by the purified."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وقال في حرف ابن مسعود ( ما يَمَسُّهُ إلا المُطَهَّرُونَ )
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: In the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud, it is: "It is not touched except by the purified."

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقال ابن جرير : حدثنا ابن عبد الأعلى ، حدثنا ابن ثور ، حدثنا معمر ، عن قتادة : ( لا يمسه إلا المطهرون ) قال : لا يمسه عند الله إلا المطهرون ، فأما في الدنيا فإنه يمسه المجوسي النجس ، والمنافق الرجس . وقال : وهي في قراءة ابن مسعود : " ما يمسه إلا المطهرون " . وقال أبو العالية : ( لا يمسه إلا المطهرون ) ليس أنتم أصحاب الذنوب .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: that he said, "None can touch it, with Allah, except the purified ones. However, in this life, the impure Zoroastrian and the filthy hypocrite touch it." And he said, "In the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud it is: 'It is not touched, except by the purified ones.'"
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وهي في قراءة ابن مسعود : " ما يمسه إلا المطهرون "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: And he said, "In the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud it is: 'It is not touched, except by the purified ones.'"

variants.short_title: 62:9 — 'Proceed' vs. 'Hurry' to Friday Prayer
variants.plain_english_hook: Instead of commanding believers to 'hurry' (fas'aw) to the Friday prayer, Umar bin al-Khattab and Ibn Mas'ud insisted until death that the verse reads 'proceed' (famḍū).
variants.title: Substitution of 'Proceed' (Famḍū) for 'Hurry' (Fas'aw) in 62:9
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 62:9, the Uthmanic text commands believers on Friday: 'فَٱسۡعَوۡاْ إِلَىٰ ذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِ' ('hurry to the remembrance of God'). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir document through numerous chains that Umar bin al-Khattab and Abdullah bin Mas'ud recited 'فَامْضُوا إِلَى ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ' ('proceed to the remembrance of God'), with Ibn Mas'ud stating that had the verse read 'fas'aw' (hurry/run), he would have run until his cloak fell off.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: hurry to the remembrance of God
variants.variant_target_english: proceed to the remembrance of God
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا نُودِيَ لِلصَّلَوٰةِ مِن يَوۡمِ ٱلۡجُمُعَةِ فَٱسۡعَوۡاْ إِلَىٰ ذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِ وَذَرُواْ ٱلۡبَيۡعَۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ خَيۡرٞ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: You who believe! When the call to prayer is made on the day of assembly, hurry to the remembrance of God, and leave business aside. That is better for you, if (only) you knew.
variants.variant_full_arabic: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا نُودِيَ لِلصَّلَوٰةِ مِن يَوۡمِ ٱلۡجُمُعَةِ فَامْضُوا إِلَى ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَذَرُواْ ٱلۡبَيۡعَۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ خَيۡرٞ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
variants.variant_full_english: You who believe! When the call to prayer is made on the day of assembly, proceed to the remembrance of God, and leave business aside. That is better for you, if (only) you knew.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Commentators explain that 'fas'aw' in the Uthmanic text means 'intend and proceed with care' rather than physical running, citing the Prophetic hadith forbidding running to prayer, and view 'famḍū' as an abrogated reading or synonym.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In Tabari's reports, when Umar was informed that Ubayy bin Ka'b recited 'fas'aw,' Umar replied that although Ubayy was the best reciter, the wording is 'famḍū,' and Ibn Umar testified that Umar never recited the verse any other way until he died.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: حدثني يونس بن عبد الأعلى، قال: أخبرنا ابن وهب، قال: ثنا حنظلة بن أَبي سفيان الجمحّي، أنه سمع سالم بن عبد الله يحدّث عن أبيه، أنه سمع عمر بن الخطاب يقرأ ( إذَا نُودِيَ لِلْصَّلاةِ مِنْ يَوْمِ الجُمْعَةِ فَامْضُوْاْ إِلَى ذِكْرِ اللهِ ).
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to recite it: (Proceed to the remembrance of God).
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: أنه سمع عمر بن الخطاب يقرأ ( إذَا نُودِيَ لِلْصَّلاةِ مِنْ يَوْمِ الجُمْعَةِ فَامْضُوْاْ إِلَى ذِكْرِ اللهِ )
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to recite it: (Proceed to the remembrance of God).

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقد أمر الله المؤمنين بالاجتماع لعبادته يوم الجمعة ، فقال : ( يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا نودي للصلاة من يوم الجمعة فاسعوا إلى ذكر الله ) أي : اقصدوا واعمدوا واهتموا في مسيركم إليها ، وليس المراد بالسعي ها هنا المشي السريع ، وإنما هو الاهتمام بها ، كقوله تعالى : ( ومن أراد الآخرة وسعى لها سعيها وهو مؤمن ) [ الإسراء : 19 ] وكان عمر بن الخطاب وابن مسعود رضي الله عنهما يقرآنها : " فامضوا إلى ذكر الله " . فأما المشي السريع إلى الصلاة فقد نهي عنه ، لما أخرجاه في الصحيحين ، عن أبي هريرة عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال : " إذا سمعتم الإقامة فامشوا إلى الصلاة ، وعليكم السكينة والوقار ، ولا تسرعوا ، فما أدركتم فصلوا ، وما فاتكم فأتموا " . لفظ البخاري
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 'Umar bin Al-Khattab and Ibn Mas'ud - may Allah be pleased with them - recited it: "Then proceed to the remembrance of Allah."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وكان عمر بن الخطاب وابن مسعود رضي الله عنهما يقرآنها : " فامضوا إلى ذكر الله "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: 'Umar bin Al-Khattab and Ibn Mas'ud - may Allah be pleased with them - recited it: "Then proceed to the remembrance of Allah."

variants.short_title: Omission of 'What Created' in Surah Al-Layl 92:3
variants.plain_english_hook: In eight Sahih Bukhari and Muslim narrations, Abdullah bin Mas'ud and Abu Ad-Darda recited Surah 92:3 as 'By the male and the female,' omitting the Uthmanic words 'by what created.'
variants.title: Recitation of 'Wa-dh-Dhakari wa-l-Untha' Without 'Ma Khalaqa' in Surah 92:3
variants.diff_summary: Whereas the Uthmanic Mushaf reads 'wa-mā khalaqa adh-dhakara wa-l-unthā' ('By what created the male and the female!'), the codex and recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud—corroborated by Abu Ad-Darda across six reports in Sahih al-Bukhari and two in Sahih Muslim—omitted the two words 'mā khalaqa' ('what created'), reading directly in the genitive oath: 'wa-dh-dhakari wa-l-unthā' ('By the male and the female!'). In these reports, Ibn Mas'ud's Kufan disciple Alqamah travels to Syria, where Abu Ad-Darda confirms that both he and Ibn Mas'ud learned the shorter reading directly from the Prophet's own lips.

variants.variant_full_english: By the male and the female!

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical scholars such as Ibn Kathir and Ibn Hajar state that while Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Ad-Darda heard this reading from the Prophet under the license of the seven ahruf, the majority of Companions followed the final presentation (al-'ardah al-akhirah) preserved in the Uthmanic Mushaf.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In Sahih al-Bukhari 3761, 4944, and Sahih Muslim 824a, Abu Ad-Darda swears by Allah after the Prophet's death that the Prophet taught him this exact wording 'mouth to mouth' (fāhu ilā fiyya) and declares regarding the Syrian Uthmanic reading: 'These people want me to recite wa-mā khalaqa, and I will not follow them.'

hadiths.transmitted_by: Alqamah / Ibrahim an-Nakha'i
hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا عُمَرُ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي، حَدَّثَنَا الأَعْمَشُ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ قَدِمَ أَصْحَابُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَى أَبِي الدَّرْدَاءِ فَطَلَبَهُمْ فَوَجَدَهُمْ فَقَالَ أَيُّكُمْ يَقْرَأُ عَلَى قِرَاءَةِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ قَالَ كُلُّنَا‏.‏ قَالَ فَأَيُّكُمْ يَحْفَظُ وَأَشَارُوا إِلَى عَلْقَمَةَ‏.‏ قَالَ كَيْفَ سَمِعْتَهُ يَقْرَأُ ‏{‏وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ عَلْقَمَةُ ‏{‏وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ أَشْهَدُ أَنِّي سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقْرَأُ هَكَذَا، وَهَؤُلاَءِ يُرِيدُونِي عَلَى أَنْ أَقْرَأَ ‏{‏وَمَا خَلَقَ الذَّكَرَ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏ وَاللَّهِ لاَ أُتَابِعُهُمْ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Ibrahim:The companions of `Abdullah (bin Mas`ud) came to Abu Darda', (and before they arrived at his home), he looked for them and found them. Then he asked them,: 'Who among you can recite (Qur'an) as `Abdullah recites it?" They replied, "All of us." He asked, "Who among you knows it by heart?" They pointed at 'Alqama. Then he asked Alqama. "How did you hear `Abdullah bin Mas`ud reciting Surat Al-Lail (The Night)?" Alqama recited: 'By the male and the female.' Abu Ad-Darda said, "I testify that I heard me Prophet reciting it likewise, but these people want me to recite it:-- 'And by Him Who created male and female.' but by Allah, I will not follow them
hadiths.highlight_arabic: وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ عَلْقَمَةُ ‏{‏وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى
hadiths.highlight_english: Alqama recited: 'By the male and the female.' Abu Ad-Darda said, "I testify that I heard me Prophet reciting it likewise, but these people want me to recite it:-- 'And by Him Who created male and female.' but by Allah, I will not follow them

hadiths.hadith_arabic: وَحَدَّثَنَا أَبُو بَكْرِ بْنُ أَبِي شَيْبَةَ، وَأَبُو كُرَيْبٍ - وَاللَّفْظُ لأَبِي بَكْرٍ - قَالاَ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو مُعَاوِيَةَ عَنِ الأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ، قَالَ قَدِمْنَا الشَّامَ فَأَتَانَا أَبُو الدَّرْدَاءِ فَقَالَ أَفِيكُمْ أَحَدٌ يَقْرَأُ عَلَى قِرَاءَةِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ فَقُلْتُ نَعَمْ أَنَا ‏.‏ قَالَ فَكَيْفَ سَمِعْتَ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ يَقْرَأُ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ ‏{‏ وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى‏}‏ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقْرَأُ ‏{‏ وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى * وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ وَأَنَا وَاللَّهِ هَكَذَا سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقْرَؤُهَا وَلَكِنْ هَؤُلاَءِ يُرِيدُونَ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ وَمَا خَلَقَ ‏.‏ فَلاَ أُتَابِعُهُمْ ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Alqama reported. We went to Syria and Abu Darda' came to us and said:Is there anyone among you who recites according to the recitation of Abdullah? I said: Yes, it is I. He again said: How did you hear 'Abdullah reciting this verse: (wa'l-lail-i-idha yaghsha = when the night covers)? He ('Alqama) said: I heard him reciting it (like this) (wa'l-lail-i-idha yaghsha) wa-dhakar wal untha = when the night covers and the males and the females). Upon this he said: By Allah, I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reciting in this way, but they (the Muslims of Syria) desire us to recite: (wa ma khalaqa), but I do not yield to their desire
hadiths.highlight_arabic: وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى‏}‏ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقْرَأُ ‏{‏ وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى * وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى
hadiths.highlight_english: By Allah, I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reciting in this way, but they (the Muslims of Syria) desire us to recite: (wa ma khalaqa), but I do not yield to their desire
