hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى، عَنْ أَبِي عَوَانَةَ، عَنْ مُغِيرَةَ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ، دَخَلْتُ الشَّأْمَ فَصَلَّيْتُ رَكْعَتَيْنِ، فَقُلْتُ اللَّهُمَّ يَسِّرْ لِي جَلِيسًا‏.‏ فَرَأَيْتُ شَيْخًا مُقْبِلاً، فَلَمَّا دَنَا قُلْتُ أَرْجُو أَنْ يَكُونَ اسْتَجَابَ‏.‏ قَالَ مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ قُلْتُ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكُوفَةِ‏.‏ قَالَ أَفَلَمْ يَكُنْ فِيكُمْ صَاحِبُ النَّعْلَيْنِ وَالْوِسَادِ وَالْمِطْهَرَةِ أَوَلَمْ يَكُنْ فِيكُمُ الَّذِي أُجِيرَ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ أَوَلَمْ يَكُنْ فِيكُمْ صَاحِبُ السِّرِّ الَّذِي لاَ يَعْلَمُهُ غَيْرُهُ كَيْفَ قَرَأَ ابْنُ أُمِّ عَبْدٍ ‏{‏وَاللَّيْلِ‏}‏ فَقَرَأْتُ ‏{‏وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى * وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّى * وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ أَقْرَأَنِيهَا النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَاهُ إِلَى فِيَّ، فَمَا زَالَ هَؤُلاَءِ حَتَّى كَادُوا يَرُدُّونِي‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Alqama:I went to Sham and was offering a two-rak`at prayer; I said, "O Allah! Bless me with a (pious) companion." Then I saw an old man coming towards me, and when he came near I said, (to myself), "I hope Allah has given me my request." The man asked (me), "Where are you from?" I replied, "I am from the people of Kufa." He said, "Weren't there amongst you the Carrier of the (Prophet's) shoes, Siwak and the ablution water container? Weren't there amongst you the man who was given Allah's Refuge from the Satan? And weren't there amongst you the man who used to keep the (Prophet's) secrets which nobody else knew? How did Ibn Um `Abd (i.e. `Abdullah bin Mas`ud) use to recite Surat-al-lail (the Night:92)?" I recited:-- "By the Night as it envelops By the Day as it appears in brightness. And by male and female." (92.1- 3) On that, Abu Darda said, "By Allah, the Prophet (ﷺ) made me read the Verse in this way after listening to him, but these people (of Sham) tried their best to let me say something different
hadiths.highlight_arabic: وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى * وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّى * وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى
hadiths.highlight_english: On that, Abu Darda said, "By Allah, the Prophet (ﷺ) made me read the Verse in this way after listening to him, but these people (of Sham) tried their best to let me say something different

hadiths.transmitted_by: Alqamah
hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا قَبِيصَةُ بْنُ عُقْبَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنِ الأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ، قَالَ دَخَلْتُ فِي نَفَرٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الشَّأْمَ فَسَمِعَ بِنَا أَبُو الدَّرْدَاءِ فَأَتَانَا فَقَالَ أَفِيكُمْ مَنْ يَقْرَأُ فَقُلْنَا نَعَمْ‏.‏ قَالَ فَأَيُّكُمْ أَقْرَأُ فَأَشَارُوا إِلَىَّ فَقَالَ اقْرَأْ‏.‏ فَقَرَأْتُ ‏{‏وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى * وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّى * وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ أَنْتَ سَمِعْتَهَا مِنْ فِي صَاحِبِكَ قُلْتُ نَعَمْ‏.‏ قَالَ وَأَنَا سَمِعْتُهَا مِنْ فِي النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهَؤُلاَءِ يَأْبَوْنَ عَلَيْنَا‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Alqama:I went to Sham with a group of the companions of `Abdullah (bin Mas`ud). Abu Ad-Darda' heard of our arrival so he came to us and said, "Is there anybody among you who can recite (Qur'an)" We replied in the affirmative. Then he asked, "Who is the best reciter?" They pointed at me. Then he told me to recite, so I recited the verse:-- 'By the night as it envelops 'By the day as it appears in brightness; And by the male and the female [wa-l-dhakari wa-l-untha, without 'wa-ma khalaqa'].' (92.1-3) Abu Ad-Darda' then said to me, "Did you hear it (like this) from the mouth of your friend (`Abdullah bin Mas`ud)?" I said, "Yes." He said, "I too, heard it (like this) from the mouth of the Prophet, but these people do not consider this recitation as the correct one
hadiths.highlight_arabic: وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى * وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّى * وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى
hadiths.highlight_english: And by the male and the female [wa-l-dhakari wa-l-untha, without 'wa-ma khalaqa']

hadiths.transmitted_by: Alqamah / Ash-Sha'bi
hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ حُجْرٍ السَّعْدِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ أَبِي، هِنْدٍ عَنِ الشَّعْبِيِّ، عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ، قَالَ لَقِيتُ أَبَا الدَّرْدَاءِ فَقَالَ لِي مِمَّنْ أَنْتَ قُلْتُ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْعِرَاقِ ‏.‏ قَالَ مِنْ أَيِّهِمْ قُلْتُ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكُوفَةِ ‏.‏ قَالَ هَلْ تَقْرَأُ عَلَى قِرَاءَةِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ قَالَ قُلْتُ نَعَمْ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَاقْرَأْ ‏{‏ وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى‏}‏ قَالَ فَقَرَأْتُ ‏{‏ وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى * وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّى * وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَضَحِكَ ثُمَّ قَالَ هَكَذَا سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقْرَؤُهَا ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Alqama reported:I met Abu Darda', and he said to me: To which country do you belong? I said: I am one of the people of Iraq. He again said: To which city? I replied: City of Kufa. He again said: Do you recite according to the recitation of 'Abdullah b. Mas'ud? I said: Yes. He said: Recite this verse (By the night when it covers) So I recited it: (By the night when it covers, and the day when it shines, and by the male and the female [wa-l-dhakari wa-l-untha, omitting 'and He Who created']). He laughed and said: I have heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reciting like this
hadiths.highlight_arabic: وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى‏}‏ قَالَ فَقَرَأْتُ ‏{‏ وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى * وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّى * وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى
hadiths.highlight_english: and by the male and the female [wa-l-dhakari wa-l-untha, omitting 'and He Who created']

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقد ذُكر عن عبد الله بن مسعود وأبي الدرداء: أنهما كانا يقرآن ذلك ( والذَّكَرِ والأنْثَى ) ويأثُرُه أبو الدرداء عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم. حدثنا محمد بن المثنى، قال: ثنا محمد بن جعفر، قال: ثنا شعبة، عن أبي إسحاق قال: في قراءة عبد الله ( وَاللَّيْلِ إذَا يَغْشَى والنَّهارِ إذَا تَجَلَّى والذَّكَر والأنْثَى ).
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: It has been mentioned regarding 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud and Abu Ad-Darda': that they used to recite that as: {And the male and the female}, and Abu Ad-Darda' transmits it from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. ... In the recitation of 'Abdullah it is {By the night as it envelops, and the day as it appears, and the male and the female}.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة عبد الله ( وَاللَّيْلِ إذَا يَغْشَى والنَّهارِ إذَا تَجَلَّى والذَّكَر والأنْثَى )
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: In the recitation of 'Abdullah it is {By the night as it envelops, and the day as it appears, and the male and the female}.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: هكذا قرأ ذلك ابن مسعود ، وأبو الدرداء - ورفعه أبو الدرداء - وأما الجمهور فقرأوا ذلك كما هو مثبت في المصحف الإمام العثماني في سائر الآفاق : ( وما خلق الذكر والأنثى )
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: This is how Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Ad-Darda' recited it - and Abu Ad-Darda' attributed it to the Prophet. However, the majority recited it as it is established in the 'Uthmani Mus-haf in all regions: {By what created the male and the female!}
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: هكذا قرأ ذلك ابن مسعود ، وأبو الدرداء - ورفعه أبو الدرداء
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: This is how Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Ad-Darda' recited it - and Abu Ad-Darda' attributed it to the Prophet.

variants.variant_arabic: وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى
variants.variant_english: By the male and the female!
variants.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا عُمَرُ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي، حَدَّثَنَا الأَعْمَشُ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ قَدِمَ أَصْحَابُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَى أَبِي الدَّرْدَاءِ فَطَلَبَهُمْ فَوَجَدَهُمْ فَقَالَ أَيُّكُمْ يَقْرَأُ عَلَى قِرَاءَةِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ قَالَ كُلُّنَا‏.‏ قَالَ فَأَيُّكُمْ يَحْفَظُ وَأَشَارُوا إِلَى عَلْقَمَةَ‏.‏ قَالَ كَيْفَ سَمِعْتَهُ يَقْرَأُ ‏{‏وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ عَلْقَمَةُ ‏{‏وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ أَشْهَدُ أَنِّي سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقْرَأُ هَكَذَا، وَهَؤُلاَءِ يُرِيدُونِي عَلَى أَنْ أَقْرَأَ ‏{‏وَمَا خَلَقَ الذَّكَرَ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏ وَاللَّهِ لاَ أُتَابِعُهُمْ‏.‏
variants.hadith_english: Narrated Ibrahim:The companions of `Abdullah (bin Mas`ud) came to Abu Darda', (and before they arrived at his home), he looked for them and found them. Then he asked them,: 'Who among you can recite (Qur'an) as `Abdullah recites it?" They replied, "All of us." He asked, "Who among you knows it by heart?" They pointed at 'Alqama. Then he asked Alqama. "How did you hear `Abdullah bin Mas`ud reciting Surat Al-Lail (The Night)?" Alqama recited: 'By the male and the female.' Abu Ad-Darda said, "I testify that I heard me Prophet reciting it likewise, but these people want me to recite it:-- 'And by Him Who created male and female.' but by Allah, I will not follow them

variants.short_title: 93:8 — 'Found You Destitute and Sheltered You'
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran says 'Did He not find you poor and enrich you?' (ʿā'ilan fa-aghnā), the Mushaf of Ibn Mas'ud read 'find you destitute and shelter you' (ʿadīman fa-āwā).
variants.title: Substitution of 'Destitute and Sheltered' (ʿAdīman Fa-Āwā) in 93:8
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 93:8, the Uthmanic text reads 'وَوَجَدَكَ عَآئِلٗا فَأَغۡنَىٰ' ('Did He not find you poor and enrich (you)?'). Al-Tabari records that in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud this verse read 'وَوَجَدَكَ عَدِيمًا فَآوَى' ('Did He not find you destitute and shelter (you)?'), replacing both the adjective 'ʿā'ilan' (poor/burdened with dependents) with 'ʿadīman' (destitute) and the rhyme verb 'fa-aghnā' (and enrich) with 'fa-āwā' (and shelter).
variants.uthmanic_target_english: poor and enrich (you)?
variants.variant_target_english: destitute and shelter (you)?
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: وَوَجَدَكَ عَآئِلٗا فَأَغۡنَىٰ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: Did He not find you poor and enrich (you)?
variants.variant_full_arabic: وَوَجَدَكَ عَدِيمًا فَآوَى
variants.variant_full_english: Did He not find you destitute and shelter (you)?

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Commentators view 'ʿadīman' (destitute) as an explanatory synonym for 'ʿā'ilan' (poor) and attribute 'fa-āwā' to an assimilation with the rhyme of verse 93:6 ('Did He not find you an orphan and shelter you [fa-āwā]?').
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari explicitly records that 'وَوَجَدَكَ عَدِيمًا فَآوَى' was written in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud (في مصحف عبد الله), representing a two-word consonantal divergence from the Uthmanic text.

variants.short_title: 93:9 — 'Do Not Scowl at the Orphan' (Takhar vs. Taqhar)
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran commands 'As for the orphan, do not oppress him' (fala taqhar, with qāf), the Mushaf of Ibn Mas'ud read 'do not scowl at him' (fala takhar, with kāf).
variants.title: Consonantal Substitution of 'Fa-Lā Takhar' (With Kāf) for 'Fa-Lā Taqhar' in 93:9
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 93:9, the Uthmanic text commands: 'فَأَمَّا ٱلۡيَتِيمَ فَلَا تَقۡهَرۡ' ('As for the orphan, do not oppress (him),') spelled with the letter qāf. Al-Tabari records that in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud this word was written with the letter kāf: 'فَلَا تَكْهَرْ' ('do not scowl at (him),'), from 'kahara' meaning to frown or rebuke harshly.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Linguists and commentators explain 'taqhar' and 'takhar' as closely related phonetic or dialectal forms prohibiting mistreatment or harshness toward orphans.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Because qāf (ق) and kāf (ك) have distinct consonantal skeletons in the Arabic script, 'فَلَا تَكْهَرْ' in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud represents a genuine rasm divergence rather than a diacritical dotting shift.

variants.short_title: 100:9 — Graves 'Excavated' (Buḥitha) vs. 'Ransacked'
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran uses the four-letter verb 'buʿthira' ('when what is in the graves is ransacked'), the Mushaf of Ibn Mas'ud had the three-letter verb 'buḥitha' ('excavated').
variants.title: Triliteral 'Buḥitha' for Quadriliteral 'Buʿthira' in Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf on 100:9
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 100:9, the Uthmanic text reads '۞أَفَلَا يَعۡلَمُ إِذَا بُعۡثِرَ مَا فِي ٱلۡقُبُورِ' ('Does he not know? When what is in the graves is ransacked,'). Al-Tabari records that in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud this clause was written 'إِذَا بُحِثَ مَا فِي الْقُبُورِ' ('When what is in the graves is excavated,'), using the triliteral verb 'buḥitha' (dug up/excavated) without the letter ʿayn or rā' of the quadriliteral 'buʿthira.'
variants.uthmanic_target_english: When what is in the graves is ransacked
variants.variant_target_english: When what is in the graves is excavated

variants.uthmanic_full_english: Does he not know? When what is in the graves is ransacked,

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Lexicographers and commentators explain that 'buʿthira' (overturned/scattered) and 'buḥitha' (dug up/excavated) converge in describing the resurrection of the dead from their graves.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari directly cites the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud ('وذكر أنها في مصحف عبد الله: إذا بحث ما في القبور') to establish the lexical meaning of 'buʿthira.'

variants.short_title: 104:9 — Closed Upon Them 'With' vs. 'In' Columns
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran says the Fire is closed upon them 'in extended columns' (fī ʿamadin), Abdullah bin Mas'ud's codex read 'with extended columns' (bi-ʿamadin).
variants.title: Reading 'With Extended Columns' (Bi-ʿAmadin) for 'In Extended Columns' in 104:9
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 104:9, the Uthmanic text describes Hellfire as closed over the damned 'فِي عَمَدٖ مُّمَدَّدَةِۭ' ('in extended columns (of flame).'). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record via Sufyan al-Thawri from Qatadah that in the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud this verse read 'بِعَمَدٍ مُمَدَّدَةٍ' ('with extended columns (of flame).'), indicating that the gates of Hell are bolted shut with outstretched pillars rather than the damned being inside columns.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: in extended columns (of flame).
variants.variant_target_english: with extended columns (of flame).
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: فِي عَمَدٖ مُّمَدَّدَةِۭ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: in extended columns (of flame).
variants.variant_full_arabic: بِعَمَدٍ مُمَدَّدَةٍ
variants.variant_full_english: with extended columns (of flame).

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Grammarians and commentators harmonize the two readings by arguing that the preposition 'fī' (in) in the Uthmanic text can carry the instrumental sense of 'bi-' (with), or that the damned are both inside columns and bolted shut with them.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir cite Ibn Mas'ud's reading 'إِنَّهَا عَلَيْهِمْ مُؤْصَدَةٌ بِعَمَدٍ مُمَدَّدَةٍ' via Qatadah as the primary evidence for the instrumental interpretation.

variants.short_title: Addition of 'Qad' ('And He Indeed Perished') in 111:1
variants.plain_english_hook: In Sahih al-Bukhari 4971, Sahih Muslim 208a, and Tafsir al-Tabari, the reading of Abdullah bin Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas adds the particle 'qad' in Surah 111:1 ('wa-qad tabba' instead of 'wa-tabba').
variants.title: Recitation of 'Wa-Qad Tabba' Instead of 'Wa-Tabba' in Surah Al-Masad 111:1
variants.diff_summary: Whereas the Uthmanic Mushaf ends Surah Al-Masad 111:1 with 'wa-tabba' ('and he has perished'), Sahih al-Bukhari 4971, Sahih Muslim 208a, and Tafsir al-Tabari document the non-Uthmanic reading 'wa-qad tabba' ('and he has indeed perished'), adding the emphatic particle 'qad'. Al-Tabari explicitly identifies this wording as the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud ('fī qirā'ati 'Abdillāh: tabbat yadā Abī Lahabin wa-qad tabba'), while Bukhari and Muslim record its transmission via the Kufan master reciter al-A'mash from Ibn Abbas.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: and he has perished.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari cites Ibn Mas'ud's reading ('wa-qad tabba') to prove grammatically that the first verb ('tabbat') is a curse ('May the hands of Abu Lahab perish') while the second verb ('wa-tabba') is a declarative statement ('and he has indeed perished').
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Both Sahih al-Bukhari 4971 and Sahih Muslim 208a preserve this reading within the same narrative report as the non-Uthmanic addition in 26:214 ('wa-rahṭaka minhumu al-mukhlaṣīn'), confirming that Kufan reciters transmitted Ibn Mas'ud's consonantal text even after the Uthmanic standardization.

hadiths.transmitted_by: Ibn Abbas / Said bin Jubair / Al-Amash
hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ بْنُ مُوسَى، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو أُسَامَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا الأَعْمَشُ، حَدَّثَنَا عَمْرُو بْنُ مُرَّةَ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ قَالَ لَمَّا نَزَلَتْ ‏{‏وَأَنْذِرْ عَشِيرَتَكَ الأَقْرَبِينَ‏}‏ وَرَهْطَكَ مِنْهُمُ الْمُخْلَصِينَ، خَرَجَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم حَتَّى صَعِدَ الصَّفَا فَهَتَفَ ‏"‏ يَا صَبَاحَاهْ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالُوا مَنْ هَذَا، فَاجْتَمَعُوا إِلَيْهِ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَخْبَرْتُكُمْ أَنَّ خَيْلاً تَخْرُجُ مِنْ سَفْحِ هَذَا الْجَبَلِ أَكُنْتُمْ مُصَدِّقِيَّ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالُوا مَا جَرَّبْنَا عَلَيْكَ كَذِبًا‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ فَإِنِّي نَذِيرٌ لَكُمْ بَيْنَ يَدَىْ عَذَابٍ شَدِيدٍ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو لَهَبٍ تَبًّا لَكَ مَا جَمَعْتَنَا إِلاَّ لِهَذَا ثُمَّ قَامَ فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏تَبَّتْ يَدَا أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ‏}‏ وَقَدْ تَبَّ هَكَذَا قَرَأَهَا الأَعْمَشُ يَوْمَئِذٍ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Ibn `Abbas:When the Verse:-- 'And warn your tribe of near kindred.' (26.214) was revealed. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) went out, and when he had ascended As-Safa mountain, he shouted, "O Sabahah!" The people said, "Who is that?" "Then they gathered around him, whereupon he said, "Do you see? If I inform you that cavalrymen are proceeding up the side of this mountain, will you believe me?" They said, "We have never heard you telling a lie." Then he said, "I am a plain warner to you of a coming severe punishment." Abu Lahab said, "May you perish! You gathered us only for this reason? " Then Abu Lahab went away. So the "Surat:--ul--LAHAB" 'Perish the hands of Abu Lahab!' (111.1) was revealed. {"...and he has perished"} [wa qad tabba]. This is how Al-A'mash recited it on that day.
hadiths.highlight_arabic: ثُمَّ قَامَ فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏تَبَّتْ يَدَا أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ‏}‏ وَقَدْ تَبَّ هَكَذَا قَرَأَهَا الأَعْمَشُ يَوْمَئِذٍ
hadiths.highlight_english: {"...and he has perished"} [wa qad tabba]. This is how Al-A'mash recited it on that day.

hadiths.transmitted_by: Ibn Abbas / Said bin Jubair / Al-Amash
hadiths.hadith_arabic: وَحَدَّثَنَا أَبُو كُرَيْبٍ، مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْعَلاَءِ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو أُسَامَةَ، عَنِ الأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ مُرَّةَ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، قَالَ لَمَّا نَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ ‏{‏ وَأَنْذِرْ عَشِيرَتَكَ الأَقْرَبِينَ‏}‏ وَرَهْطَكَ مِنْهُمُ الْمُخْلَصِينَ ‏.‏ خَرَجَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم حَتَّى صَعِدَ الصَّفَا فَهَتَفَ ‏"‏ يَا صَبَاحَاهْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالُوا مَنْ هَذَا الَّذِي يَهْتِفُ قَالُوا مُحَمَّدٌ ‏.‏ فَاجْتَمَعُوا إِلَيْهِ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ يَا بَنِي فُلاَنٍ يَا بَنِي فُلاَنٍ يَا بَنِي فُلاَنٍ يَا بَنِي عَبْدِ مَنَافٍ يَا بَنِي عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ ‏"‏ فَاجْتَمَعُوا إِلَيْهِ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ أَرَأَيْتَكُمْ لَوْ أَخْبَرْتُكُمْ أَنَّ خَيْلاً تَخْرُجُ بِسَفْحِ هَذَا الْجَبَلِ أَكُنْتُمْ مُصَدِّقِيَّ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالُوا مَا جَرَّبْنَا عَلَيْكَ كَذِبًا ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ فَإِنِّي نَذِيرٌ لَكُمْ بَيْنَ يَدَىْ عَذَابٍ شَدِيدٍ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَقَالَ أَبُو لَهَبٍ تَبًّا لَكَ أَمَا جَمَعْتَنَا إِلاَّ لِهَذَا ثُمَّ قَامَ فَنَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ السُّورَةُ تَبَّتْ يَدَا أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَقَدْ تَبَّ ‏.‏ كَذَا قَرَأَ الأَعْمَشُ إِلَى آخِرِ السُّورَةِ ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: It is reported on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that when this verse was revealed:" And warn thy nearest kindred" (and thy group of selected people among them) the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set off till he climbed Safa' and called loudly: Be on your guard! They said: Who is it calling aloud? They said: Muhammad. They gathered round him, and he said: O sons of so and so, O sons of so and so, O sons of 'Abd Manaf, O sons of 'Abd al-Muttalib, and they gathered around him. He (the Apostle) said: If I were to inform you that there were horsemen emerging out of the foot of this mountain, would you believe me? They said: We have not experienced any lie from you. He said: Well, I am a warner to you before a severe torment. He (the narrator) said that Abu Lahab then said: Destruction to you! Is it for this you have gathered us? He (the Holy Prophet) then stood up, and this verse was revealed:" Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and he indeed perished" (cxi. 1). A'mash recited this to the end of the Sura
hadiths.highlight_arabic: فَنَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ السُّورَةُ تَبَّتْ يَدَا أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَقَدْ تَبَّ ‏.‏ كَذَا قَرَأَ الأَعْمَشُ إِلَى آخِرِ السُّورَةِ
hadiths.highlight_english: and this verse was revealed:" Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and he indeed perished" (cxi. 1). A'mash recited this to the end of the Sura

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وأما قوله: ( وَتَبَّ ) فإنه خبر. ويُذكر أن ذلك في قراءة عبد الله: " تَبَّتْ يَدَا أبِي لَهَبٍ وَقَدْ تَبَّ". وفي دخول " قد " فيه دلالة على أنه خبر.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: As for His saying: {and he has perished}, it is a declarative statement. And it is mentioned that this is in the recitation of 'Abdullāh [Ibn Mas'ud]: "The hands of Abū Lahab have perished, and he has indeed perished." And in the inclusion of 'qad' (indeed) in it, there is an indication that it is a declarative statement.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: ويُذكر أن ذلك في قراءة عبد الله: " تَبَّتْ يَدَا أبِي لَهَبٍ وَقَدْ تَبَّ"
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: And it is mentioned that this is in the recitation of 'Abdullāh [Ibn Mas'ud]: "The hands of Abū Lahab have perished, and he has indeed perished."

variants.short_title: Ibn Mas'ud's Omission of Surahs 113 and 114
variants.plain_english_hook: Abdullah bin Mas'ud—the first Quran teacher endorsed by Muhammad—omitted the final two chapters (Surahs 113 and 114) from his codex, viewing them as protective prayers rather than chapters of the Book.
variants.title: Exclusion of Al-Mu'awwidhatayn (Surahs 113–114) from the Codex of Ibn Mas'ud
variants.diff_summary: Whereas the Uthmanic Mushaf and the codex of Ubayy bin Ka'b include Surah Al-Falaq (113) and Surah An-Nas (114) as the final two chapters of the Quran, Abdullah bin Mas'ud omitted both chapters from his written Mushaf and scraped them out when he saw them written in copies of the text. As documented in Sahih al-Bukhari 4977 and Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Ibn Mas'ud maintained that these two texts were revealed as prophetic invocations for seeking refuge rather than scriptural chapters of the Quranic canon.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical scholars such as Ibn Kathir and al-Nawawi argue that the overwhelming consensus of the Companions—led by Ubayy bin Ka'b—established the Mu'awwidhatayn as canonical chapters, suggesting Ibn Mas'ud initially mistook them for supplications like the Qunut prayer.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In Sahih al-Bukhari 4977 and multiple chains in Musnad Ahmad and Musnad Abu Ya'la cited by Ibn Kathir, Zirr bin Hubaysh and Alqamah testify that Ibn Mas'ud actively erased the two chapters from his codices and declared, 'They are not from the Book of Allah,' demonstrating that the senior Companions differed over the boundaries of the written canon.

hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدَةُ بْنُ أَبِي لُبَابَةَ، عَنْ زِرِّ بْنِ حُبَيْشٍ، وَحَدَّثَنَا عَاصِمٌ، عَنْ زِرٍّ، قَالَ سَأَلْتُ أُبَىَّ بْنَ كَعْبٍ قُلْتُ يَا أَبَا الْمُنْذِرِ إِنَّ أَخَاكَ ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ يَقُولُ كَذَا وَكَذَا‏.‏ فَقَالَ أُبَىٌّ سَأَلْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ لِي قِيلَ لِي‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ، قَالَ فَنَحْنُ نَقُولُ كَمَا قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏

Ubai said, "I asked Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) about them, and he said, 'They have been revealed to me, and I have recited them (as a part of the Qur'an)," So Ubai added, "So we say as Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) has said

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: ورواه عبد الله بن أحمد من حديث الأعمش ، عن أبي إسحاق ، عن عبد الرحمن بن يزيد قال : كان عبد الله يحك المعوذتين من مصاحفه ، ويقول : إنهما ليستا من كتاب الله ... وهذا مشهور عند كثير من القراء والفقهاء : أن ابن مسعود كان لا يكتب المعوذتين في مصحفه .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 'Abdullah bin Ahmad recorded it from the Hadith of Al-A'mash, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abdur-Rahman bin Yazid, who said: "'Abdullah used to scrape the Mu'awwidhatayn from his Mushafs, saying: 'They are not from the Book of Allah.'" ... This is famous among many of the reciters and jurists, that Ibn Mas'ud did not write the Mu'awwidhatayn in his Mushaf.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: كان عبد الله يحك المعوذتين من مصاحفه ، ويقول : إنهما ليستا من كتاب الله
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: 'Abdullah used to scrape the Mu'awwidhatayn from his Mushafs, saying: 'They are not from the Book of Allah.'
